body.input: No, I think it would be actually in some ways maybe the best way to die, knowing that you're in the first wave of people expanding the reaching of the stars.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It would be an honor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: The following is a conversation with Chris Mason, professor of genomics, physiology, and biophysics at Cornell.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: He and colleagues do some of their research out in space, experiments on space missions that seek to discern the molecular basis of changes in the human body during long-term human space travel.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: On this topic, he also wrote an epic book titled The Next 500 Years, Engineering Life to Reach New Worlds, that boldly looks at what it takes to colonize space far beyond our planet and even journey out towards livable worlds beyond our solar system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: This is the Lex Friedman Podcast. To support it, please check out our sponsors in the description.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And now, dear friends, here's Chris Mason.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: You wrote a book called The Next 500 Years, Engineering Life to Reach New Worlds, and you dedicated it to, quote, to all humans and any extinction-aware sentience.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: How fundamental is awareness of death and extinction to the human condition?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I think this is actually one of the most human-specific traits and features that we have.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It's actually maybe one of the few things that only we have and no one else has.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It sounds scary. It sounds like what people often don't like to think about their death, except now and again, or at funerals, or to recognize their mortality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But if you do it at a species-wide level, it's something that is actually an exemplary human-specific trait that you're exhibiting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: You think about something that is the loss of not just your life or your family or everyone you see, but everyone like you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And that is I dedicated it because I think we might not be the last sentience to have this awareness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: We're actually hoping we'll just be the first. But as far as we know, we're the only.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And I think this is part of the moral thrust for the book is that we're the only ones that have this awareness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: That gives us a duty that only we can exercise so far.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So we definitely contemplate our own mortality at the individual level.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It is true. When you wrote it, it was really powerful to realize for me that we do contemplate our extinction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: That is a creative force. So at the individual level, contemplating your own death is a creative force.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Yes. Like I have a deadline. Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But contemplating the extinction of the whole species, I suppose that stretches through human history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: That's many of the sort of subtext of religious ideas is that like if we screw this up, it's going to be over.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And Revelation and every religious text has some view of either the birth or the death of the world as they know it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But it was very abstract. It was fiction almost, or in some cases complete fiction of what you hope or think might happen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But it's become much more quantified and much more real, I think, in the past several hundred years and especially in the past few decades where we can see a sense of responsibility on a planetary scale.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So when we think about, like say, terraforming Mars, that would just be the second planet we've engineered at a planetary scale.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: We're already doing it for this one, just not that well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Well, yeah, that's right. So we're like a bunch of ants, extinction-aware sentience ants that are busy trying to terraform this planet to make it habitable so it can flourish.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And then you say that it's our duty to expand beyond Earth, to expand to other planets, to find a good backup, offsite backup solution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Why the word duty? It's an interesting word.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Duty is something that usually puts people to sleep, I'll say.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Duty is a bit like death. People don't often wake up in the morning and think, what is my duty today?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Most people, there are some people that think about it every day, people in the active military service wake up, it's a very concrete sense of duty to country.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Sometimes you can think about it though in terms of family. You feel a duty towards your spouse, your kids, your parents.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: You feel a real duty to them because you want them to flourish and to be safe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So we do have this sense of duty, but you don't, very much like death, you don't think about it actively usually. It's something that just becomes embedded in your day-to-day existence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But I think about duty because this is a, people think about duties for themselves, but there has never been a real overarching duty that we all feel as a species for each other and for generations that haven't yet been born.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And I think I want people to have a sense of the same love and compassion and fighting even to the tooth and nail, whether the way you protect your family, the way you'd fight for a country, for example,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: to feel the same way towards the rarity and preciousness of life and feel that sense of duty towards particularly extinction-aware life, which is just us so far.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: This ability that we have this awareness of not only our own frailty, which of course is often talked about in climate change and people think about pandemics,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: but other species that we sometimes cause extinction, but very soon will be even de-extinctifying species like the woolly mammoth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Colossal is a recent startup that's doing that on their advisory board and it might happen in three or four years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So it's an interesting point in history where we can actually think about preventing death at a species-wide level and even resurrecting things that we have killed or that have gone away,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: which brings its own series of questions of just as when you delete something from an ecosystem, adding something can be completely catastrophic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And so there are no real guidelines yet on how to do that. But the technology now exists, which is pretty extraordinary.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Yeah, I've just been working on backup and restoring databases quite a bit recently.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And you can do quite a lot of damage when you restore improperly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: When we bring back the mammoths, you have to be careful bringing that back. The best of science, the best of engineering is both dangerous and exciting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And that's why you have to have the best people, but also the most morally grounded people pushing us forward.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But on the point of duty, there's a kind of sense that there's something special to humanity, to human beings that we want to preserve.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And if that little flame, whatever that is, dies, that will be a real shame for the universe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: What is that? What is special about human beings? What is special about the human condition that we want to preserve? Why do we matter?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: There are some people who think we don't. There are some people who say, well, humans, take it or leave it. They think they're misanthropes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So the book is on the one sense, a call to misanthropes to hopefully shake them out of their slumber.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But there's some people who just people that dislike humanity there. They're just, again, the world just they're called nihilist, Donnie.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: That's a shout out for Bigelow.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: They're like nothing matters and why does anything and they just apply it more particularly to humans. But there are endless reasons, I think, to cherish and celebrate what humans have done.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: At the same time, many things we've done awfully and genocide and nuclear weapons testing on unsuspecting citizens of remote islands.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: There's definitely things we've done bad, but the poetry, the music, the engineering feats, the getting to the moon and eventually already rovers on Mars, these extraordinary feats that humans have already accomplished.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And just a really a sense of beauty, I think, is something that is you can't ask ants or cockroaches about their favorite paintings.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Or maybe if you could, it would be very different from ours. But in either case, there's a unique perspective that we carry.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And I think so that's something even just the old age old question in biology and geneticists.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: This comes up a lot of what makes humans unique. And so is it bipedalism? Is it our intelligence? Is it tool making? Is it language?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: All those things I just listed, other species have some degree of those traits.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So it's a question of degree, not of type of trait that defines humans a little bit. But I think for the extinction awareness, that is a uniquely human trait that is to our knowledge,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: no other species or entity or A.I. or sentience that carries that awareness of the frailty of life of our own life, but all life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Maybe it is that awareness of the frailty of life that allows us to be so urgently creative, create beauty, create innovation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It just seems like if you just measure humans are able to create some sort of subjectively beautiful things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And I see science that way. I see engineering that way. And ants are less efficient at that. They also create beautiful things,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: but less aggressively, less innovation, less building like standing on the shoulders of giants, building on top of each other over and over and over.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Where you're getting like these like hierarchical systems where you create and create a levels of abstraction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Then you use ideas to communicate those ideas and you share those ideas. And all of a sudden you have the rockets going out into space.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Which ants have been building the same structures for millions and millions of years with no real change. And so that is the key differentiator.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Yet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Yeah, that's right. We've got an experiment going right now and maybe they'll change.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Well, yeah, we will bring up some extreme organisms. Another thing you're interested in.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: OK. One interesting thing that comes up much later in your book is something I also haven't thought of.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And it's quite inspiring, which is the heat death in the universe is something worth fighting against.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Like that's also an engineering problem. Yes. You know, you kind of the I mean, you seriously look at the next 500 years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And this is such a beautiful thing. You know, seriously, we'll talk about like the uncertainty involved with that and all the different trajectories.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But to seriously look at that and then to seriously look at like what happens when the sun runs out?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: What happens when the the universe comes to an end?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Like we have an opportunity and a kind of duty, like you said, to fight against that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And that was so inspiring to me to think, wait, maybe we'll actually that's a worthy thing to think about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Maybe we can prevent it, actually. Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: The come up with the best known understanding current of how things end.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: You know, we have we kind of a building an intuition and data and models of the way the universe is, the way it started, the way it's going to end.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So our best model of the end, let's start thinking about how that can be prevented, how that could be avoided, how that could be channeled and misdirected.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And you can pivot it somehow. That's really inspiring.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: That's really powerful. I never really thought about that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: That eventually all things end. And that was the kind of melancholic notion behind all of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: You know, none of this matters in a way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Just to me, that's also inspiring to enjoy the moment, to really live in the moment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: You know that because that is truly where beauty exists is in the moment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But there is a long lasting aspect to beauty that is part of the engineering ethic, which is like, tell me what the problem is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And we're going to solve it. So what do you think about that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: The long scale beyond five hundred years is the humans have a chance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Absolutely. I think we have the best chance of any species and actually the best chance that humanity's ever had.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I think a lot of people fear that we can or will kill ourselves.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Actually, my favorite question I ask at the end of every interview for every potential graduate student, medical student, faculty, whoever I'm interviewing for whatever reason.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: The last question is, well, how long do you think that humans or our evolutionary derivatives will last?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And the answers are shockingly wide ranging.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Some people say, I think we've only got a hundred years left. Or some people say billions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Some people say as long as the universe lasts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But to the person who once said as a medical student applicant, he said, I think we've only got a hundred years left.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And I was like, really, for all of humanity, everything will be gone in a hundred years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And he said, yes. And I said, well, well, sweet Jesus, man, why go to med school?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Why not go sell bananas on the beach?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And then he said, I really want to make the last few hundred years count really matter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And I said, oh, well, that's actually kind of sort of hopeful in a really dark way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But I think we've never been better situated to actually last for the long term.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Even though we've also never been at the greater risk of being able to destroy ourselves ever since really the first nuclear test when they...

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Tony Orbez, a great book about this called The Precipice, where the precipice for humanity is at one point we made technologies that we weren't sure whether or not they would destroy the Earth or the entire universe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So the math was incomplete and there was too much error, but they tested the bomb anyway.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But it's an extraordinary place as a species to think we now have something in our hands that may destroy the Earth and possibly a chain reaction that destroys the whole universe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Let's try it anyway as a stage that we're at as a species.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But with that power comes an ability to get to other planets to survive long term.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And when you think about the heat death, that's an ad infinitum question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: If you keep thinking, well, we survive, we go to the next sun and then you go to the next sun, eventually the question will be, well, if you just keep doing that forever, at some point the universe either continues to expand or could collapse back in itself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And the heat death is more likely at this point where it just keeps expanding and expanding, everything gets too far away.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But even in that case, I think if we had a fundamental knowledge of physics and space time that you could try and restructure it quite literally the shape of the universe to prevent it, I think we would.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I think we would want to survive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I think, you know, unless we had done the math and we think that there's a greater chance that the next universe would form and make more life, maybe we would.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But even then, I think humans have always wanted to survive and you could argue maybe should survive because...

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And are able to engineer systems that help us survive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Yeah, yeah, and always have, yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So what is this?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: The Tsar Bomb, yeah, the hydrogen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Yeah, there's nothing more terrifying and somehow inspiring than watching the mushroom cloud of a nuclear explosion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It's like humans are capable of this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: They're capable of leveraging the power of nature.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: To completely obliterate everything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And to create propulsion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I mean, most of the Voyager spacecraft are nuclear powered because it's still in many ways the most efficient way to get a tiny amount of fissable material and make power out of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: You know, so they're still slowly drifting their path to heliosphere.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: They're out now into interstellar space and they're nuclear powered.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So it's like any tool or technology.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It's a tool or a weapon depending on how you hold it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Are we alone in the universe, Chris Mason?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: What do you think?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So the presumption that you've just mentioned is let's just focus on our thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Well, I think we, as far as we know, there's no other sentient life out in the universe that we've found yet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And I think there's probably bacteria life out there just because we found it everywhere we've looked on Earth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And there's, you know, halophilic organisms that can survive in extreme salts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: There are our psychrophiles that are in extreme cold.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: There's, you know, basically organisms that can survive in really almost any possible environment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: They can adapt and find a way to live.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But as far as we know, we're the only sentient ones.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And I think this is the famous, the Drake equation or, you know, how many, where is everyone is the, what Enrico Fermi said is the, why haven't we heard from anyone if there are these other life forms?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I actually think the question is wrong to phrase it that way because the Earth has only been here for 4.5 billion years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And, you know, life may be only for a few billion of those years, complex life only for several hundred years, 100 million years of life we've actually had, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: and humans only the past few million years since our last common ancestor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So it's not that much time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But even further back, the universe hasn't had that much time itself to cool and create atoms and have them spread around the universe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Right. So the current estimates 13.8 billion years of just the whole universe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But it's been the first five or six of those billion years really just like cooling and making enough of the stars to then make the atoms that would come from supernova.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So I actually think we might be the first or sit one of the very few or one of the early life forms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But the universe itself hasn't had that much time to make life in a galactic and universal time frame.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: You needed billions of years for the elements to be created and then distributed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And we're only really in the last few billion years where I think even life could have been made.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So I think the question of wherever is everyone is the wrong question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I think the question is, I think we're the first ones at the party. Let's set up the liquor. Let's set up the food.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I just think we're the first ones at the party of life. But more people are coming.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: One of the early attendees to the party.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Yeah, maybe the first as far as we know the first, but maybe we'll find some local pocket of the universe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Because the parties then expand and it overflows.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And then there's a mosh pit and then you bump into the other galaxy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I think the question should be, when else is everyone getting here instead of where is everyone?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I think we've just started on the genesis of life in the universe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Yes, not worry have they or not more about when and who and how do we set up the party?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And then how do we help them? I think it's an interesting other moral question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: A lot of Star Trek episodes, the prime directive is you do not interfere with another planet if you could pass by a planet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I think it's time to also revisit that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Because what if you go by a planet and we think that as far as we can tell,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: with enough certainty that they would never be able to leave their planet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And then the sun eventually would engulf that planet wherever that planet might be in some solar system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But if we had a way to help them, their culture, their science, their technology,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: everything about a different species to survive, would we not interfere?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I think that would actually be wrong to say, well, we can save this life here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And we decide not to. We decide after millions and billions of years pass and we know the sun will engulf that planet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: just all the engineering challenges and opportunities that we're exploring.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So there's things we can do that I think are very cheap and very easy.

body.input: So we should do some of that. We can walk and chew gum at the same time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: What if it will kill all of humanity?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Michael Creighton wrote a book, The Andromeda Strain, about this very idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And it could, but it hopefully won't.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: The only way you can really gauge that is the same way we do with any infectious agent here on Earth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: If it's a new pathogen, a new organism, you do it slowly, carefully.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: You often do it with levels of containment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It's going to be probably where some pioneers go.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: For example, on Mars, there might be other organisms there that only get activated once there's an ambient temperature and more humidity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Then suddenly the first settlers on Mars are encountering a strange new fungus or something that's not even like a fungus.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It might be a different clade of life, a different branch of life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It could be very dangerous or it could be very inert.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Most of life on Earth is not really dangerous or harmful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Let me go back on this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Most of life on Earth is neither harmful nor beneficial to you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It's just they're making its own way in the universe, just trying to survive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It's when it's inside of you and replicating your cells and destroying your cells like a virus like COVID, XRCV2, that becomes a big problem, of course.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It doesn't really have agency.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It's just trying to get by.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: For example, most of the bacteria on the table on your skin in the subway are pretty inert.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: They're just people hanging around for the ride.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Actually, just because we're talking so much trash about viruses, most viruses don't bother humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: They're phages.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Almost all the vast majority of viruses are phages.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: There's this battle in the biology that is really dorky.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: People who study bacteria think the bacteria are the most important because there's trillions and trillions of them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: They run a lot of our own biology in our body.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But then people who study phages, they say, well, there's 10 times more phages than the bacteria, which can attack the bacteria and destroy them as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Phage, people think that they run the world, but we need them both.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: What do you think about viruses?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: You said alien organisms. Wouldn't we encounter something like bacteria, something like viruses as the first alien life form?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: First of all, are viruses alive or not?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: The book definition, if you pick up a biology textbook, they'd say technically no because they don't have the ability to self-replicate independently.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But I would think if you restructure how you view what life is, it's just autonomously aggregating and replicating of information.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: For example, AI at some point, what if there's an AI platform that we could consider alive?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: At what point would you allow it to say it's alive?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I think we have the same definitional challenge there is that if it can continually propagate instructions for its own existence, then it is a version of living.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I think viruses don't get that category because they can't do it on their own, but they are a version of life, I'd say, but probably not alive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Well, they are expressing themselves and doing so on occasion quite powerfully in human civilization.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So like you said, at which point are AI systems allowed to say?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: We're life. We are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: We are allowed. Humans must allow them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And viruses didn't ask for permission to express themselves to humans. They just kind of did.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: We didn't have to allow them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Are they overall, though, exciting or terrifying to you as somebody who has studied viruses?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Whenever given two options, there's always two more. You can do both or neither.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So here I'll say they're both terrifying and exciting, I think, to me. More exciting than terrifying, I think.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: If I had to make that sandwich and how many layers are meat versus cheese, there's a lot more cheese of excitement.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And meat is the fear in this metaphor, apparently.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And the sandwich. Well, I love both, so it's a hell of a delicious sandwich.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: You quote President Dwight D. Eisenhower in your book, quote,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Plans are useless, but planning is essential. And you provide a thought experiment called entropy goggles.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Can you describe this thought experiment?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Happily. I do this almost every day somewhere when I'm sitting in a given room.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I will. Well, a quick comment about that quote, actually, for all the NASA planning meetings for the twin study and other missions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: That was often the quote that goes put up on the wall before we'd sit down for the day to plan the mission.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It was that quote, which I thought was hilarious for an official NASA meeting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But it was because you need to have a plan, but you have to know that plan might change.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And so I think that's just a quick context for that quote.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Craig Kundrow, who is a leader at NASA headquarters now, always put that first slide up and are like,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: hmm, this meeting, are they going to go really well or really bad?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I don't know what's about to happen, but it's an inspiring quote because it's very true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: In any case, the entropy goggles is a thought experiment I detail in my book,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: which is if you just sit in a room, any room, wherever you are,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: and imagine what it will look like in 10 years, 100 years, 500 years, or even thousands of years,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: it is a wonderfully terrifying and exciting exercise against definitely both because you realize the transience of everything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: You think of what might survive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Almost everything that you're looking at will probably not be there in hundreds of years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It will be at the very least degraded or it might be changed, altered, completely different, moved.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It is just that trait, though, of humans to just sit there and project into the future easily,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: really seamlessly with whatever you were doing previously is powerful because it shows what can change

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: and what should change in some cases, but also that left to its own devices, the universe would –

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: entropy would come take over and really things would decay, things would be destroyed,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: but the only thing really preventing I think some of the entropy is really humans,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: these sort of sentient creatures that are aware of extinction like ourselves,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: is really one of the only forces in the universe that's counteracting the second law of thermodynamics,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: this entropy that's always increasing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Technically, we're actually still increasing it because we emit heat and we never have perfect capture of all of energy,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: but we're the only things really actively and consciously resisting it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Really, you could say life in general does this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Like ants do this when they build their big homes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: They're rearranging the universe to make a nice place for themselves and they're counteracting entropy,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: but we could actually do it in a way that would be at a large scale and for long term.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So the entropy goggles is just a way to realize how transient everything is

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: and just imagine everything that will decay or change in the room around you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So if anyone listening, if they're listening on a train or they're driving in their car

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: or wherever someone is listening right now, looking around everything can and will change.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But at first, it's terrifying to see that, oh my gosh, everything will decay and go away,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: but then I think it's actually liberating.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I think, wait, I can prevent it or I can affect it or I can improve the change that may occur all by itself, say naturally.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So I think it is, but is that awareness, again, of the frailty of life,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: the ever insistence in increasing entropy that you can address though?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Actually, I say the same thing to first year medical students. I teach them genetics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I point early in the course, I say, here's all these charts of how the human body decays over time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And I call it the inexorable march towards molecular oblivion,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: which the students often find, they kind of laugh at, because on all the charts, they're 22 years old,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: but older people do not laugh as much at the thought of molecular oblivion,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: but we're all marching towards it to a large degree.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So this is both a great thought experiment for the environment around you,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: so just looking at all the objects around you, that they will dissipate, they will disappear with time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But then it's also the thing you mentioned, which is how can I affect any of the world?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Like you're one little creature and it's like your life is kind of,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: you get dropped into this ocean and you make a little splash.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And how do I make it so the splash lasts for a little bit longer?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Because ultimately, I suppose the wave will continue indefinitely,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: but it would be such a small impact that it's almost indetectable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And so how do I have that impact at all?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: On so many levels, I get to experience this as a human.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I recently had my cold storage hacked to where it was locked, essentially.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It wasn't hacked, it was locked.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And so you get to lose all your data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So for example, if you lose all your data, if you lose all your online presence, your social media, your emails,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: if you think of all the things you could lose in a fire, there's been a lot of fires in the United States,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: if you lose your home, it makes you realize, wait a minute,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: this is exactly a nice simulation of what will happen anyway, eventually.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And that eventually comes pretty quickly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And so it allows you to focus on how can I actually affect what matters, what lasts, and what brings me joy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I suppose that the ultimate answer is nothing lasts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So you have to focus on the things in the moment that bring you joy and that have a positive impact on those around you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Focusing on something that's long lasting is perhaps, I don't know, it's complicated, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Because like...

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Well, it used to be foolhardy to say, I want to think, legacy is often what people think of as they approach the end of their life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: What is my legacy? What have I done?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Even younger in life, but it used to be really foolhardy to say I could affect something that would...

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: People would build the building, architects would say, I put my name on this building and there I'll have some sense of immortality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But that's a fleeting dream.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: You can't reach immortality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And if you could, it would be resource taxing on everyone else, if you really were.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But I think it's okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I mean, the books are the next 500 years, but I presume I'll be dead for the vast majority of that time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But that is actually the liberating state of mortality, is you know that you don't have forever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So it means what can you do that is the most impactful?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But you can build things that you say, I want to pass this on to the next generation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Again, the most obvious thing we do with this is if people have kids, but they don't think of this as an intergenerational responsibility.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Think of it as, well, I was at the bar one night and met this hot girl and then things happened.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Sometimes it's more planned than that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But there's no overarching sense of, wait, I could have something that three or four generations from the beginning of my life,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: that someone will receive this gift that was planned for them long before they were born or gestating.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And I think we have that capacity and that can be a version of legacy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But it's even okay if no one knows exactly who started it, but that the benefit was brought by people,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: hundreds or even thousands of years after you got it started.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I think this is something that is only really people that are economically secure can even begin to do this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Or you can say, think of Maslow's hierarchy of needs where you need to satisfy your physical needs, all your structural needs and have shelter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And so I'm sitting from a position of great privilege to be able to pontificate about what I hope I could do for things for people that come 200 years from now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But nonetheless, more and more people can do that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Humanity has never been in a better state quantifiably to be able to start to think about these intergenerational responsibilities.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Yeah, that's an interesting balance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Because it seems that if you let the ego flare up a little bit, that's good for productivity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Like saying I can somehow achieve immortality if what I do is going to be pretty good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But then that's actually being kind of dishonest with yourself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Because it won't, in the long arc of history, won't matter in terms of your own ego.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But it will have a small piece to play in a larger puzzle.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And help people many generations from now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And that they said there are all these people who were looking after me before I was ever born.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I think it's because it's a bit of just even just knowing what if when you go to a campsite,
