metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: there's a camping rule that you always leave the campsite better than you found it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So if the fire pit was somewhat damaged and you got there, you fix it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: If there was no wood, you leave a few bits of logs for the next person who comes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And this ethos is something that just picked up from camping.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And so I think if we did that as people, the world would be a better place and the world coming ahead would also be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: That said, with these entropy glasses, how can you see through the fog?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: 500 years is a long time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: First of all, why 500 years?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Most people, this is so refreshing because most colleagues and friends I talk to are don't have the guts to think even like 10 years out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: They start doing wishy washy kind of statements about, well, you don't know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But it's so refreshing to say, all right, I know there's so many trajectories that this world can take,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: but I'm going to pick a few and think through them and think what it's the well, it's the quote, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Plans are useless, but planning is essential.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So why 500 years?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So 500 was a little bit of what I felt like I could see clearly through the entropy goggles.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I feel like I can't see.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Which is a contradiction in terms of.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Right, right, right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I can see.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I mean, for example, if you said, Chris, what's going to happen in a million years?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Well, I'll start to describe what happens to the moon will be farther away because it moves several inches away every year.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And so then eventually you can't have a full lunar eclipse after a while.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I think about structures of the continental change and things like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I could describe some things, but it starts to become so vague.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It's just not a useful exercise.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I think it's too far out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: If it's too soon, that's not that much different from what people just do with the news and say,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I think this is what the economy might look like over the next year or two years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Economists are notoriously not held accountable when they have really bad predictions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: You can make really awful predictions and no one seems to care.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: You can just make another one next week.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So too short is, I think, not necessarily as helpful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But 500, I actually, when I was first working on the book and thinking about time, I thought, well, do I do a thousand or two?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I kept thinking about the main idea was if I were to pick this up 500 years from now, what would it look like?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I changed the number if I pick up a thousand years from now or a hundred.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And I kept trying to think of what are some time frames where really large scale changes have happened?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So in some sense, you could argue that humans been mostly the same for about three or four thousand years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And the best example is this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: You looked at some of the Homer's poems or the Greek tragedies and Oedipus, for example.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Humans are really almost identical.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: We're still petty and people have affairs and people do things they shouldn't.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Saying all those things is bad.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It's astounding and in some sense soothing that the Greek tragedies of 2300 years ago are very relatable to what happens in every high school.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So that's why you read them in high school.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Like, oh, that's really a clear part of the human condition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So on that sense, some things are really permanent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But I want to think of a few reasons I chose 500 is that it's a time frame where I could foresee clear development of some biotechnology that will get us to a new place,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: including missions to Mars that are planned that will be there and that would sort of have settlements there on the moon and Mars.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And I could see also that by that time, I think we would have enough knowledge of biology and technology and space medicine to start to prepare for an interstellar mission,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: to actually send people on a craft that would have what's called a generation ship.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: People live and die on the same spacecraft on the way towards a destination.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But I think we need that much time to actually perfect the technology and to learn enough about physiology to be able to make it for that distance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And the book is kind of focused on the human story, a specific slice of the possible futures.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: There could be sort of AI systems, there could be other technologies that kind of build up the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So much of the world might be lived in virtual reality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So you're not touching any of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: You're sticking to biology or not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: You're you're touching a little bit, but focused on what the cells that make up the human body.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: How do they change?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: How do we design technologies to repair them?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And how do we protect them?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And as they travel out into the cosmos?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Absolutely. And it's something that is part of the duty.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: If your duty is to keep life safe, you have to consider all means to do so.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And engineering life to save itself is definitely on that list.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And I think we can imagine in that time frame, 500 years, that we would, you know, there will be AI that is continually advancing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And I actually say that I'm matter agnostic towards cognition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So if your matter is carbon atoms and cells and tissues and you have cognition, bravo.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Good for you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: If you're if you're silicon based and you're in chips and you're an AI, that's all virtual.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But we reach a state of well beyond the Turing test and really clearly intelligent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Congratulations to you, too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So I feel like this sense of duty is is applicable regardless of what the state of matter your cognition is based in.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So I would imagine that AI platforms that are really intelligent might also get a sense of this duty.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Or I hope they would. I wrote the book.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: They can carry that flame of whatever makes humans special.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So but why nevertheless is so much of your focus on this human meat vehicle?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Do you think it's essential?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It doesn't have to be meat. No, it definitely does not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It could be. I'm hoping that the AI platforms that we've built or that would become that would start to build themselves would also carry the sense of duty, because at that point they would be life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And so whichever means that life, whatever form life takes, it should have this duty, I think.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Will it have the lessons of genetics, genomics, DNA and RNA and proteins and the squishy stuff that makes us human?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Are those lessons a temporary thing that will discard or will those lessons be carried forward?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I mean, like if the machines completely take over, let's say, and it's all not necessarily completely take over.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But either completely take over or merge with humans in some interesting way, where we, as opposed to figuring out how to repair cells and protect cells, we start having some cyborg cells.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I think we will. They'll definitely be a blending and blending has already happened.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: There's prosthetic limbs, there's cybernetic limbs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: There's, you know, neural link, you know, progress being made to blend the biology and cybernetics and machines for sure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But I think the in the long term, you know, we'll see that they are fairly in the biology be useful because it's a manufacturing system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: All of life is a way to create copies of things or to replicate information, including storage of information.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Actually, the hard drives are probably one of the worst ways for long term storage.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: DNA might end up being the best way to have millennia or even longer scale storage where you want something that has redundancy that's built in and it can store and can be put at really cold temperatures and survive even cosmic rays.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So I think it DNA might be the best hard drive of the future potentially.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: This is really interesting. OK, what is DNA? What is RNA? And what are genes?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Yes, we should because most I presume the audience knows about some might just be first time listeners.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: There's a person right now who's like in Brazil smoking a joint sitting on the beach and just wants to learn about DNA.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So please explain it to DNA. The D X E ribonucleic acid is the recipe for life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It is what carries the instructions in almost all of your cells. You have a copy of your genome.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It's actually the reason I became a geneticist is because the day I learned that as an embryo, we started just a single cell.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But all the instructions that are to make every single type of cell in your body, I was and still am endlessly fascinated by that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: That is extraordinary. That is to me the most beautiful thing in the entire universe that is a complete from one single embryo.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Everything is there to make the entire body, which aspect of that is most beautiful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So is it that there is this information within DNA that stored efficiently and it also stores information on how to build, not just what to build.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Yeah. And so from all of that is what's the sexiest, what's the most beautiful aspect?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Is it the entire machinery or is it just the information is there?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It's the fact that the machinery is the information like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: They basically it becomes its own manufacturer is is what is extraordinary.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Imagine if you if you took a one two by four and you threw on the ground and you said I'll be back in a day and then a whole house was made when you came back.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I mean, we would all lose our minds.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: A lot of people would poop their pants. People have to wear adult diapers. It would be a big scene.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Yes. If that happened and then we're actually getting close to that people having autonomous house building.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It's not quite there yet, but there are people trying to make robots that will build entire houses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But you need much more than the block of wood. Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: That's that's the extraordinary thing is it just for one one piece of wood then say I'll just leave it there for a few days and I'll come back.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: That's basically what embryos do. OK, it takes nine months, a little bit longer, but still that is nothing short of magic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Right. So I think that's what I love about the fact that DNA carries that information.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Now the information is static.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So to actually read that information and to actually put into motion is where RNA comes in.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So this ribonucleic acid, so it just has one other oxygen added to it versus DNA, but is the transcribed version.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It's like if you look at a book and you say you have in your hands, but then you start to read it aloud, it becomes the active form of the recipe for life is the RNA.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And then as RNA is also then get translated to become proteins that become active forms like enzymes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: You think of like your hair or think of other ways you digest food.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: There's all these active proteins going around that are copying your DNA, making RNA, making sure your DNA is safe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: That's all these built in systems to keep your cells in check and working.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And these are often in protein form.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And so genes are the really these constructs, basically what are the instruction sets, like how many versions of instructions do you have in your genome?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So the genome is the collection of all the DNA of a person for humans, about three billion letters of genetic code.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So just three billion A, C, G and T's, these nucleotides that are the recipe for life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And that's it. That is the entire instruction set to go from that one embryo up to a full human, which is pretty efficient to say.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It's actually not that much information. And in that three billion letters are snippets of the genes,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: which are independently regulated, autonomous instruction sets, if you will, these really active forms of the instructions from your DNA to say, make a protein, make this RNA or turn off some other part of a cell.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: All those instructions are there in our DNA. And there's about 60,000 of these genes that are in our genome.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So how do those all lead up to you? Having a personality, good memory and bad memory, some of the functional characteristics that we at the human level are able to interpret the the way your face look, the way you smile.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: You're good at running or jumping, whether you're good at math and all those kinds of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: There's an age old debate of nature versus nurture. So like most things, given two options, you can of course have both.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So almost every trait that we know of in humanity has mixtures of nurture and nature. Some of them are purely nurture.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So most people probably are familiar with twin studies, but twin studies are one of the best ways to gauge how much is something nurture versus nature, how much of it is really ingrained and has probably less ability to change versus how much can you really train.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So height, for example, is one of the most obvious inheritable traits, but it doesn't have one gene.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It probably has at least 50 or 60 genes that contribute to height. So it's not like a gene for height.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Some people think of like the gene for cystic fibrosis. Now that's in that case. That's true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: There is one gene that if you have mutations, you get cystic fibrosis as a disease.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But for other other traits, they're much more complicated. They can have dozens or even hundreds of genes that influence your risk and what appears.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But from twin studies, you take monozygotic twins, twins that are identical, and you can clearly tell they look at the same facial structure, similar intonation, similar even to the face.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And you compare them to dizygotic twins. Or when you have fraternal twins, you can have a male and female, for example, in the same uterus.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And those are dizygotic twins or two zygotes. So in that case, they share 50% of their DNA, but they share the same womb.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And then what you can look at is what's the difference between identical twins versus fraternal twins and calculate that difference for any trait.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And that gives you an estimate of the heritability or what's called H squared.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So that's what we've been doing for almost every trait in humanity for the past 100 years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: We've been trying to measure this. And religion is one that's a negative control.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So if you separate people and see what religion they become, there's no gene for religion or what religion you choose.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So that often is their correlation there is zero because it should be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It's a nurture trait of what religion you end up taking is not encoded in your DNA.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Religion meaning Islam, Judaism, Christianity, but there could be aspects of religions that-

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Good question. There is religiosity as a trait that's been studied in twins.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And that has a heritable component to some degree.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So if things like boredom susceptibility is a trait, one of my favorite papers just looked at how likely is it that people get bored?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And they looked at identical twins and fraternal twins. And there's a heritability of about 30%.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So it's mostly not heritable. It's mostly environmental.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But that means to some degree, whether or not you're bored, you can say, well, it's a little bit of my genes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Not a lot, but most of them have some degree.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And they're probably overlapping with other traits.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Your boredom susceptibility versus risk seeking behavior are interrelated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So how likely are you to say, I want to go cliff jumping or I want to do free basing or I want to do some else that's risky behavior?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So speaking of twin studies, Scott Kelly spent 340 consecutive days out in space.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: You analyzed his molecular data, DNA, RNA, protein, small molecules.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: What did you learn about the effect of space on the human body from Scott?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: We learned that space is rough on the human body, but that the human body is amazingly and monstrously responsive to adapt to that challenge.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It can rise to the occasion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So we can see Scott had, as almost all astronauts do, a bit of puffiness and spikes in his bloodstream of these what are called cytokines,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: these inflammation markers where the body is clearly saying to itself, holy crap, I'm in space.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And liters of fluid move to the upper torso and they get a puffy face, what's called the astronaut face that is very common.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But it goes away after a few days.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And some astronauts maintain high levels of stress for their whole mission, as measured by cortisol or some of these other inflammation markers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Whereas Scott actually had a little spike, but then he was cool as a cucumber for most of the mission.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But he had spent, at that time, that was the longest ever mission for a US astronaut.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: A few cosmonauts have gone a little bit longer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But there had never been a deep molecular analysis of what happens to the body after about a year in space.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So it was the first study of this kind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And what we found is when he got back, we saw all the same markers of stress on the body and changes spiked up to levels we'd never seen for any other astronaut before.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So it seemed like going to space for a year wasn't so hard as much as returning to gravity after a year.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It was much harder on the body.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: He notoriously broke out in a rash all over his body.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And really even the weight of clothing on his skin was too heavy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It created all this irritation because his body had not felt the weight of just a simple t-shirt.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It wasn't really, it had zero weight, of course, so it went up in space.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So that led to all this inflammation, all these changes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: He was much more comfortable just to walk around nude.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: In that case, it was for medical reasons.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Some people do this recreationally.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: He was doing it for medical purposes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I do it for medical reasons as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: All the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I mean, people say…

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I have a prescription.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: The doctor told me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So he was allergic to Earth, he said, which is fascinating to think about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: How quickly did his body adapt there?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So there it was about three to four days he got back to normal, at least in terms of the inflammation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But what's extraordinary is that we measured a lot of other molecules, genes, structural changes, tissue, looked at his eyeballs, looked at his vasculature.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It took him even six months after the mission, a lot of the genes that had become activated in response to spaceflight were still active.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So things like we could see his body repairing DNA.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: He was being irradiated by cosmic rays and by the radiation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It's the equivalent of giving three or four chest X-rays every day just in space.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And we could see his body working hard at the molecular level to repair itself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And even in his urine, we could see bits of what's called 8-oxoguanazine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It's a form of damaged DNA that you could see coming out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And we see it for other astronauts as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So it's very common.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: You can see damaged DNA, the response of the body to repair the DNA.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But even though he'd been back on Earth for six months, that was still happening even six months later.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: How do you explain that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So some of this has to do with when you have a gene get activated, you might think, oh, it's like a light switch.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I look at my wall, just flip a light on or off.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And sometimes turning a gene on or off is that simple.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Sometimes you just flip it on because the gene is already ready to go.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Other cases, though, you have to reprogram even the structure of how your DNA is packaged.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It's called an epigenetic rearrangement.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: In that case, we could see that a lot of these genes had been in these cells had changed the structure of how DNA was packaged.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And it remained open even months after the mission.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Now, after about a year, it was actually almost all back to normal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Ninety-nine percent of all the genes were back to where they were in pre-flight levels.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So it means that eventually you'll adapt.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But there's almost a lag time, kind of like jet lag for the body, but jet lag for your cells to repair all the DNA.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: What was the most surprising thing that you found in that study?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: There are several surprises.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: One is just that he, that the repair, as I just mentioned, that the repair took so long.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I thought maybe a week or a few days he'll be back to normal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But to see this molecular echo in his cells of his time and space still occurring was interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: His telomeres was one that was really surprising.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: The caps and the ends of your chromosomes, which keep all your DNA packaged,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: and you get half your chromosomes from your mother and half from your father, and then you go on and make all your cells.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Normally, these shrink as you get older, and telomeres, just length is just an overall sign of aging getting shorter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: His telomeres got longer in space.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And so it was really surprising because we thought the opposite would happen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So that was genetically one surprise.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And also some of the mutations we found in his blood, he had less mutations in blood.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: As if his body was almost being, like a low dose of radiation was sort of cleansing his body.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Maybe the cells that were about to die is one of our main theories on what's happening.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And of course, you can't really, you have theories, but you can't, because the number of subjects in the study is small.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Right. It's notoriously one of the lowest powered studies in human history, yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But what you lack in subjects, you can make up for in the number of sampling times.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So we did basically 260 samples collected over the course of three years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So we really, almost every few weeks, had a full workup, including in space.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So that was the way we tried to make up for it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But we've tried in other model organisms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: In mice, we've seen this. We've looked now in 59 other astronauts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And in every astronaut that we've looked at, their telomeres get longer in space.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Does that indicate anything about lifespan, all those kinds of things?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Or no, you can't make any of those kinds of jumps?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Not yet. I want to make that jump yet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But it does indicate that there is a version of cleansing, if you will, that's happening in space.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: We see this actually clinically at our hospital.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: You can do a low dose of radiation with some targeted therapies to kind of activate your immune cells.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It's even tried clinically.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So this idea of just a little bit of stress on the body, or what's called hormesis,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: may prime you into active cleansing, things that were about to die.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And that includes stress caused by space.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Yes, apparently.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: How do we adapt the human body to stress of this kind for periods of multiple years?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: What lessons do you draw from that study and other experiments in space

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: that give you an indication of how we can survive for multiple years?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I think we know that the radiation is one of the biggest risk factors.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And this has been well described by NASA and many other astronauts and researchers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And so there we don't have to just measure the radiation or just look at DNA being damaged.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: We can actually actively repair it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: This happens naturally in all of our cells.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: There's little enzymes, little protein, and really many machines that go around and scan DNA for nicks and breaks and repair it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: We could improve them. We could add more of them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Or you can even activate them before you go into space.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: We have one set of cells in my lab where you activate them before we irradiate them

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: to actually prepare them for the dose of radiation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Now that is what's called epigenetic CRISPR therapies,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: where you can actually instead of adding or taking away a gene or modifying a cell,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: you just change kind of how it's packaged.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Like I was just describing, the genes are still there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: We're just changing how they get used.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And so you can actually preemptively activate DNA repair genes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And we've done this for cells.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: We haven't done this yet for astronauts, but we've done it for cells.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And a similar idea to this is being used to treat sickle cell disease and beta thalassemia.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: You can reactivate a gene that was dormant as a therapy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So should we make human genes resilient to harsh conditions,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: or should we get good at repairing them?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I want to get good at repairing them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Okay, start to interrupt.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I think every time I ask this question, you have taught me that there's always a third option to say both.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I will say both.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I know for copy, it's good to just have one big statement,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: but you want to do both or a third option.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I would want to do electromagnetic shielding.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I would want to do a fourth option of maybe some other kind of physical defenses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Outside of the human body.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So we're taking the same passion to keep astronauts safe that's outside them

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: and just putting it in their cells is what I propose.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Now, it's a bit radical today because we're just starting this in clinical trials to treat diseases on Earth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So it's not ready, I think, to do in astronauts, but in the book I proposed by about the year 2040,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: that's when we'd reach this next phase where I think we'll have known enough about the clinical response.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: We'll have the technology ironed out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: That's about when it's time, I think, to try it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So what are some interesting early milestones?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So you said 2040.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: What do we have to look forward to in the next 10, 20 years, according to your book, according to your thoughts?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: A lot of really exciting developments where if you really want to activate genes,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: like I was just describing, or repair a specific disease gene, you can actually crisper it out and modify it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: This has been already published and well documented.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But as I was alluding to, more and more we'll see people that just want to temporarily change your gene's functions and change their activity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So the best example, this is for beta thalassemia.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: We all have hemoglobin in our blood that carries oxygen around.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And when you're an adult, it's a different version.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It's a different gene.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: One gene when you're a fetus called fetal hemoglobin, when you're an adult you have a different gene,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: but they both are making a protein that carries oxygen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: After you're born, the fetal hemoglobin gene gets just turned off.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It just goes away and you replace it with adult hemoglobin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But if your gene for hemoglobin is bad as an adult, one of the therapies is,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: well, let's turn back on the gene that you had when you were a fetus.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And it's actually already led to cures for sickle cell and beta thalassemia in this past year.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So it's this extraordinary idea of like, well, you already have some of the genetic solutions in your body.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Why don't we just reactivate them and see if you can live?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And indeed, you can.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So I think we'll see more of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: That's for severe disease, but eventually you could see it for more, I think, work-related purposes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Like if you're working in a dangerous mine or in a high radiation environment,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: you could basically start to prime it for work safety, basically.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: We need to genetically protect you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Now, it would have to be shown that that genetic option is safe, reliable, that it's better,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: at least as good, or if not better, than other shielding methods.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But I think we'll start to see that more in the next 10, 20 years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And eventually, as I described in the book, you can get to recreational genetics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: You could say, well, I want to turn some genes on just for this weekend because I'm going to a high altitude,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: so I'd like to prepare for that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And so instead of having to take weeks and weeks for acclimation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: you could just do some quick epigenetic therapies and have a good time in the mountains

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: and then come back and turn them back off.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So this is stuff to do on Earth across thousands of humans,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: and then you start getting good data about what the effects on the human body are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: How do we make humans survive across an entire lifetime for, let's say, several decades in space?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: If it's just in space, it'll be hard because you'll need basically some gravity at some point.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I think you'd need orbital platforms that give you at least some partial gravity, if not 1G.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: If you're on Mars, it's actually, even though the gravity is 38% of Earth's,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: just having that gravity would be enough.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And if you could get under the surface into some of the lava tubes

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: where you have some protection above you from the radiation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I think that would be, you probably could survive quite well there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So I think it's just in space parts that's hard.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: You'd need some gravity. You need some additional protection from the radiation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Can you linger on the lava tubes on Mars? What are the lava tubes on Mars?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Yes, so they are a bit like what they sound like.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: They were large masses of lava at one point on the planet pushing really quickly through the environment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And they created these basically small caverns,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: which you could go in theory and build a small habitat and then puff it up kind of like blowing up a balloon

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: and have a protective habitat. Basically, it's a little bit underground.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So one of the next helicopter missions being planned at the Jet Propulsion Lab

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: is to see if you can get a helicopter to go into the lava tube,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: which is just, as it sounds, kind of like take out a big worm that has burrowed into the landscape

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: and leave out the hollow column that's left.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And that's what your tubes look like.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So one of the future helicopters might even go explore one of them as a mission being planned right now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So they're accessible without significant amount of drilling?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Yeah, that's the other advantage.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Yeah, you can get to them because some of them are exposed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: You could do a little bit of drilling and then see essentially this entire cavern.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And that takes you a little bit from the radiation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Right, because you have some soil above you basically, which would be regolith, which would be nice.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: What about source of food? What's a good...
