metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So that's part of biology, how you power this whole thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: What about source of food across decades?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: In space, we'd have to...

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Plants have been grown in flight and you can get some nutrients,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: but right now it is very reliant on all the upmass being sent up, all the freeze-dried food that gets rehydrated,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: which doesn't taste awful, but is not self-reliant.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So I think those would have to be small bioreactors.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It would have to be a lot of work on fermentation, a lot of work on essentially prototrophic organisms,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: the organisms that can make all of the 20 amino acids that you would need to eat.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I described a little bit in the book, what if we did a prototrophic human where you could have...

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Like right now we need to get some of our amino acids because we can't make them all, which I think is kind of sad.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So what if we could make all of our own amino acids or all of our own vitamins?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I also think that's one case where another adaptation could be to activate the vitamin C gene.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Right now you'd have to have limes or some other source of vitamin C in space,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: but we actually carry the gene inside of our genome to make vitamin C.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Look at dogs and cats, for example. They have these kind of wet noses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: You don't see them going out and getting margaritas.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Dogs can drink beer and get drunk. They don't need vitamin C.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: They have no risk of scurvy because they can make the vitamin C all by themselves.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So can other wet-nosed primates called strepsyrines, but we are dry-nosed primates, and we lost this ability.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Sometimes 10 or 20 million years ago, we no longer make our own vitamin C,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: but the gene for it is called GULO. It's still in our DNA.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It's what's called a pseudogene. It's just broken down.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It's like having a – like in our genome, we have these functional genes like nice BMW, a nice car that works well,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: but we also have this like junkyard of old cars, old genes, old functions in our DNA that we could bring back.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And so vitamin C is one of them that would be very easy to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So then you could activate the gene, repair it basically, repair it so we can make our own vitamin C.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Now we'd have to do it again carefully because what if we lost vitamin C?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: The production of vitamin C as a species, what if it was a good reason that we lost it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Maybe it was helping in some other way that we can't see now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But you'd start slowly, do it in cells, then do it potentially in animal models and other primates, and then try it in humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But that's something else I'd like to see so we wouldn't have to make as much food in orbit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: You could actually start to make as much of your own food in your own cells.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So the input to the system in terms of energy could be much more restricted,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: doesn't have the diversity we currently need as humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But I don't want to be a robot. Humans love, as I do, texture.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I realize that made me sound like I wasn't human, but humans love food and flavors and textures and smells.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: All that is actually attenuated in flight.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So you'd want to not forget our humanity and this love of all the benefits and wonder of food and cooking and smells.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Well, speak for yourself because for me, I eat the same thing every single day.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I find beauty in everything and some beauty is more easily accessible outside of Earth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And food is not one of those things, I think.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: What about insects?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: The people bring that up, basically food that has sex with itself multiplies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So cockroaches and so on, they're a source of a lot of protein and a lot of the amino acids.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And bed bugs. There's a guy at the American Museum of Natural History in New York.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: He loves bed bugs, Lou Sorkin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And he has a monthly meeting where he talks about which insects would be the best for eating.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And one month he gave a whole talk about bed bugs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: They're pretty gross, but in terms of the value of what you can get for protein, they're really good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So they're a good candidate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I think you'd have to, if you could deep fry them, if you deep fry anything, you can pretty much eat it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So maybe you'd need a fryer up in space, but they're a candidate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: All right, what technical question, what are the major challenges of sex in space?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Asking for a friend for reproduction purposes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So like when we're looking about survival of the human species across generations, do we need gravity, essentially?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: For sex in space, we know that gestation can happen in space where the babies can develop, at least in mice.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: We know that it's possible for worms to replicate and fly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So it's possible for other invertebrates to show they can make babies in space.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But for humans, NASA's official stance on this is that there has never been sex in space officially.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I think, you know, if we all wonder about that, I think humans are very predictable in that regard.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Going back to the Greek tragedies, I think there's probably someone did something close to it at some point.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And so I think we know that sperm can be sent into space and brought back and be used for fertilization, for in vitro fertilization for humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But sex itself in space, you know, would be I think when we start to get bigger structures that have a bit more privacy, I think there'll be a lot of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And there should be, you know, this is a big question of who goes up into space.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It's now becoming more of regular, in quotes, people who have prosthetic limbs or cancer survivors like Haley Arsenault, who just went up on the Inspiration 4 mission.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So she's been a great researcher and helping with a lot of the science from that mission.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: We are doing the same analysis on them as we've been doing for the twin study and for other astronauts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: We're doing basically all the same molecular profile before, during an spaceflight.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So there we now know that other people can go into space.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So there's more and more regular Joes and Janes go up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I think we'll see a lot more of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But so far we have no data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: We have no video of it either way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: We have no real knowledge other than it would be it would need a lot of Velcro.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I think is my only real answer there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Well, I'm as a fan of Velcro and duct tape.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I think that's going to be those two are essential for anything, any kind of engineering out and anywhere, honestly, in all kinds of harsh conditions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But that is, I mean, on the topic of sex in general, just social interaction with humans is fascinating.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: The current missions are very focused on science and very technical engineering things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But there's still a human element that seeps in.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And the more we travel out the space, the more the humans, the natural human drama, the love, the hate that merges, it's all going to be right there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It's a Greek tragedy just in space.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I think it's going to be a reality show.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So what about the colonization of other planets?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: If you look at Mars, when you first of all, do you think it's a worthy effort looking at this particular one planet to put humans on Mars and to start thinking about colonizing Mars?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It's one of the closest options.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It's not the best option, though, by far.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: We put in the book measures of Earth similarity index or something called ESI is how close is the gravity, the temperature, the solar incidence on the surface?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: How close is it to Earth is a calculation many astronomers make when they look for exoplanets.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And Mars is pretty far away from an ESI of about 0.7.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I mean, Earth is one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So the best you can get is one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Earth is just like Earth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It gets a score of one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Anything above some of the best exoplanets that are in the habitable zone where there's liquid water that could be there start to get above 0.8 or 0.9.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But most planets are very low.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: They're 0.1, 0.2.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: They're either way too big and we have crushing gravity or way too small, too close to a sun.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But Mars is, even though it's not that great on the ESI scale, it is still very relatively close galactically.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And Venus is just too hot right now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So I think Venus would also be a great candidate, but it is much easier to survive in a place where it's very cold, but you can be sealed and survive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Whereas going on, we probably just have no technology to survive anywhere except in the clouds of Venus.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So it's just currently our best option, but it's not the best option for sure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So over time, the ESI changes across millennia.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It does.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So Venus is going to get cooler and cooler.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: OK.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But what are the big challenges to you in colonizing Mars?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: From a biology perspective, from a human perspective, from an engineering perspective?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: There are several big challenges to Mars.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And even the first one is even just the word colonize.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So I think there's even a social challenge.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Like a lot of people, Daniel Wood actually studies this at MIT, is we shouldn't even use the word colonize.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But then we probably shouldn't use the word settle either because there are settlements that have some other baggage to that word as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And then maybe we just use the word explore.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But at some point, you didn't say we're going there to survive there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And so colonization still is the word most people use.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But I try to say go explore and build or settle.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But I think the first challenge is social.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I think getting people to think that this will not be like the colonization efforts of the past.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: The hope is that this will be a very different version of humanity exploring.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: That's my hope.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: History, you could say, has proved me wrong every single time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Like every time humans have gone somewhere, it's usually been a tale of exploitation, strife, and drama again, and then and often murder, genocide.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Like it's actually a pretty dark history, if you think of just all the colonization efforts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But I think most of it was done in a really dark area of humanity where the average life expectancy was more than half less than it was today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It was life was brutish and short, as Hobbes famously said.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So it was a rough existence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So I think some of the ugliness of humanity in prior colonization times was a consequence at the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: At least that's my hope. I think that now we would have it be much more inclusive, much more responsible, much less evil, frankly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: We'd go there and you would need commercialization.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: You need efforts to do mining, for example, bring things back.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But it'd have to be some degree where there are some areas that are viewed as as as commons or that are untouchable, like places that are parks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: We do this today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Even if there's a lake, for example, the first several hundred feet of a lake are all for public property and everything that you can own property, but just not certain barriers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So I think we'd have to make sure we do that so that it's not completely exploited.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But the so that's on the social, the human side, the technological.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: We've talked a little bit about where you'd have to live.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: You want to be underground with engineering and modifying even human cells to make sure you survive the soil.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Those are a lot of pro chlorides, which is a problem for growing them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But there's ways to extract them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: There's a fair amount of water.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: There's actually a beautiful image of all the known water on Mars that NASA posted about a year ago.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And there's water everywhere.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Not not lots of it everywhere, but almost everywhere you look, there's at least a little bit of water just a few feet under the surface.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And by the caps, there's a lot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So I think we could get some water and we could also do self generating reactors, machines that could make food, start to even make beer if you go long enough down the path.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But the technical challenges are definitely the engineering and the manufacturing are going to be hard because you have to build the buildings basically out of the soil that's there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So you have to really go there and try and build with whatever you can.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So that has to be perfected still.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But then once you're in those those buildings, those structures, you need to create all the biology that will feed the populace feed them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So which we don't have the technology for yet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: We have bits of it, but I think that's going to be the biggest challenges making Mars really truly independent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But that'll probably take, as I say in the book, several hundred years before I think we'd get there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It's interesting because we're also exploring ways to motivate society to take on this challenge.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It's the JFK thing and then the Cold War that inspired the race to space.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And I think as a human species, we're actually trying to figure out different ideas for how to motivate everybody to work on the same project together.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But yet compete at the same time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Well, that's one idea and that's worked well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Competition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Competition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It's not necessarily the only idea, but it's the one that worked well so far.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So maybe the only way to truly build a colony in on Mars or a successful sort of human civilization on Mars is to get like China to get like competitive about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And they are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: They've announced they want to have boots on the red planet by 2033, which is two to four years earlier than when NASA supposed to do it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So we'll see if they if they get their first.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But I think it's a space race to point out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But it's not just the US and Russia this time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It's China.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It's India.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It's the UAE.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It's Europe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Yes, a JAX has the Japanese Space Agency and there's the US.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So now it went from just a two person race to a whole field that the whole field of runners, if you will, on the track trying to get to Mars first.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And I think I mean, it's going to be like anything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: If you start to have settlements and construction projects and places to visit on Mars, I think the true mark of of someplace being actually settled is when you start to be able to pick.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: You're like, well, I want to go to this destination at this one because they have better Martian cocktails here, but this one's not as good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So then this idea of innovating and competing will continue to drive, I think, humans as it always has.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: You write this fascinating thing, which is, quote, People living on Mars will have developed entirely new cultures, dialects, products and even new religions or variations of current religions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: For example, a Martian Muslim will need to pray upward toward the dusty sky.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I love that you've thought through the geometry of this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: For example, Martian Muslim will need to pray upward toward the dusty sky since Earth and therefore Mecca will sometimes be overhead.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Or when Mecca is below the Martians feet, the prayer direction to Allah will stay downward toward the 38 percent gravity floor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Perhaps a second Mecca will be built on the new planet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And that's never been done before. We've never seen the structure of the skin and how it changes in response to microgravity and also the microbes that change.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And so these beautiful images of even the structure of skin changing and the inflammation that we've seen in, like for Scott Kelly, for example, we now have a molecule by molecule map of what happens to skin, which has never been done before.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So what are the interesting surprises there?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So one of the things we can see the part of what's driving inflammation is we can actually see macrophages and there's other dendritic cells pieces like cells that are part of the immune system kind of creeping along towards the surface of the skin, which is now we know it's actually physically driving the immune system is these cells going and creating this inflammation, which is what leads to some of the rashes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But we didn't see as much in them as we saw, for example, some of the signatures of Scott Kelly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Axiom missions are a bit more complicated. There's docking, you're up in the space station to shared atmosphere.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So you have to follow all the ISS protocols.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: What's interesting about the Dragon capsule and the Inspiration4 and some of these are called free-flyer missions, you can just launch into space.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: You basically have your own little mini space station for a few days. It's not that big, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But I think that's what we'd probably see him do first because we're going to see a lot more tests of those in the next two, three years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But they've already been demonstrated to be safe. And then you're not trying to go for 10 to 20 days or months or years at a time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It's just up in space for a few days, but you're in proper space. It's an orbital flight. It's not just a suborbital flight.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: You could do a podcast from there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: 2026, I wonder how the audio works. See, also, can you comment on 2026? I'll start getting ready.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I'll start pushing him on this. I'm quite serious. It's a fascinating kind of...

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Axiom 2 still has room. You could go on that mission if you wanted to.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So I'll ask you about Axiom. How strict are these?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So this seems surreal that civilians are traveling up. So how much bureaucracy is there still in your experience for the scientific...

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I mean, I know it's a difficult question to ask a scientist because you get to... you don't want to complain too much.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But how much... there's sometimes bureaucracy with NSF and DOD and the funding and all those kinds of things

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: that kind of prevent you from being as free as you might sometimes like to do all kinds of wild experiments and crazy experiments.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Now, the benefit of that is that you don't do any wild and crazy experiments that hurt people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And so it's very important to put safety first. But it's like a dance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: A little too much restrictions of bureaucracy can hamper the flourishing of science.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: A little too little of that can get some crazy scientists to start doing unethical experiments.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: That said, NASA and just spaceflight in general is sort of famously very risk averse.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So what's your sense currently about even doing a podcast?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: A podcast, unless it's... I think with mixed martial arts is a pretty safe activity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Unless you're doing the octagon version of your podcast.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I mean, just getting there and back is the only real risky part, which is still risky.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But I think you're not asking to do open heart surgery in space. You're just saying, what if I do a podcast?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And I think...

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Well, fun. You're trying to ask to have fun. And I feel like fun sounds dangerous. Any kind of fun.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: That's what's been extraordinary is that traditionally, yes, I think most of the space agencies have been very, by definition, bureaucratic

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: because they're coming from the government. But they've been that way for a really good reason.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Is that safety... In the early 60s, we know almost nothing about the body in space,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: except for some of the work that pilots have done at really high altitudes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So we really didn't know what at all to expect.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So it's good that there were decades of resolute focus on just safety.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But now we know it's pretty safe. We know the physiological responses. We know what to expect.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: We can also treat some of it. Hopefully soon we'll treat a lot more of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But if you just want to go up there, it's actually not just a question of cost.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Like imagine... I think the way you can view a lot of the commercial spaceflight companies is that

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: if you have the funds, you can basically plan the mission.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: All the training they'll do is to help you get prepared for how you run some of the instrumentation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: how you can fly the rocket to a limited degree, and how to use some of the equipment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But fundamentally, it's no longer a question of years and years of training and selection,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: this impossible odds task of becoming an astronaut.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It's frankly just a question of funds.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Expensive plane rides. So how much... you mentioned Axiom.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Is it known how much it costs for the plane ride?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: There is no official number, and it depends on the mission, of course.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So if you ask them... often they'll say, well, how serious are you?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: They don't just want to give out random numbers to people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But the numbers... because for example, we propose one mission.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: We want a new twin study where someone goes up and stays up there for 500 to 550 days.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But it's basically going to be up there for the longest time ever,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: to similar the time it would take to get to Mars and back for the shortest possible duration, about 550 days.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Because if you went there and immediately turned around, you could maybe make that mission.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Otherwise, it's a three-year mission.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And there, you're looking at the ranges of... it's 50 to 100 million dollars in that ballpark range.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But the reason it's so variable is it depends. What are you doing up there?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: If you're up there, for example, for two years, basically, almost two years,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: that's a long time to just be in one spot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So could you be doing some things where your time is valuable?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So you can do experiments and people pay for those and that defrays the cost.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Or you could build something or you could do podcasts and maybe fundraise on the podcast.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And so as long as you... the reason the cost is variable is because it depends, well, do you have all the money?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And you say, I want to go and just sit in space for two years and do nothing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Well, then you have to pay for all that time that you're up there if you want to do things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Yeah, I see the official X1 mission was 55 million for a trip to the ISS.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Not that bad. It could be worse.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Wait, Sergey just posted a $35,000 price tag per night per person on the ISS. Is that real? I don't know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: That sounds about right. That's why...

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: That's like a real hotel site. So to stay... oh, so interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And then I'm sure there's costs with the docking and all those kinds of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: That's from the perspective of Axiom, the private company or SpaceX or whoever is paying the cost in the short term and in the long term.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Yeah. And the thing about a lot of that cost is rocket fuel. A lot of it is the ride.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So I've been on calls where Axiom's like, hey, SpaceX, give us to make it a little cheaper.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: We can make it cheaper in our end. It's the cost. That is the rocket.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So SpaceX is giving Axiom a ride. Right. In this case, what is Axiom Space? Can you speak to this particular private company?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: What's their mission? What's their goal? And what is the Axiom 1 mission that you just went on?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Yeah. So the Axiom Space is a private spaceflight company that's building the first private space station.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Actually, I've seen the videos and footage and hardware being put together. So they're in the process of constructing it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: The hope is that by 2024, one of the first modules will be up and connected to the ISS, eventually will be expanded.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And then by 2028, the plan is it'll be completely detached and free floating.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And it will be maybe even a little bit sooner, depending on how fast it goes. But they're building the world's first private space station.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So if you want to have a wedding up there, you just have to multiply the number of guests times the number of nights and you could have a wedding up there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It'd be very expensive. But if you want to do it, you can do it. It's like you can have a lab up there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: If you want to do experiments, you can do experiments. You figure out the cost. If you want to have a beer up there, you can make your own brewery and beer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And so this is the first beer made in space. For some reason, you want to do it, you can pay for it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So it's opened up this space where if you can find the funds for it, you propose it. You can probably just do it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: OK, cool. So what is the Axiom 1 mission that just went up? Can you tell me what happened?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Axiom 1 is the first commercial crew to go to the space station. So Inspiration 4 was the first commercial private crew to just go into space.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: They went into space and actually did an orbital mission for just about three days.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But Axiom 1 is the first, again, on the SpaceX rockets, but launched up, docked to the space station, and they're up there for about 10 days to do experiments, to work with staff, actually just take some pictures.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But it's a mission, actually doing a lot of experiments, doing almost 80 different experiments. So it's a lot of it's very science heavy, which I love as a scientist.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But it's the ability to show that you can fundraise and launch up a crew that's all privately funded and then go to the space station.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Yeah, it's four people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Yeah, four people. And the Axiom 2 will also likely be four people. The two that have been announced are John Schaffner and Peggy Whitson.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Peggy Whitson is an already prior NASA astronaut who has been at many times the many experiments. She knows the space station like her own house.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And we recently did a training with Peggy and John in my lab at Cornell to get ready for some other genomics experiments that we'll do on that mission.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So they're doing the experiments too. What does it take to design an experiment and to run a design experiment here on Earth that runs up there and then also to actually do the running of the experiment?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: What are the constraints? What are the opportunities? All that kind of stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: The biggest concern is what do you need for reagents or materials, the liquids that you might use for any experiment?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: What if it floats away? What if it gets in someone's eye? Because things always float away in space.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: There's notoriously panels in the space station where you don't want to look behind because it's got a little fungus or food has gotten stuck there and sometimes found months and months or years later.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So things float around. So the little things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And so if you have anything you need to do your experiment that's a liquid or a solid, whatever that is, it has to go through toxicity testing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And the big question is if this thing, whatever you want to use, gets in someone's eye, will they lose their vision or be really injured?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And if the answer is yes, it doesn't mean you can't use it. It just means if the answer is yes, you have to then go through multiple levels of containment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: There's a glove box on the space station where you can actually do experiments that have triple layers of containment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So you can still use some harsh reagents, but you have to do them in that glove box.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But you can propose almost anything. The biggest challenge is the weight. If it's heavy, it's $10,000 per kilogram to get something up into space.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So if you have a big heavy object, there's some cost you have to consider.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And that includes not just the materials, but the equipment used to analyze the materials.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: One of the ones we worked on actually with Kate Rubins was putting the first DNA sequencer in space called the biomolecular sequencer mission, also with Aaron Burton and Sarah Castor Wallace.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But there, the interesting thing is we had to prepare this tiny little sequencer. It sequences DNA. You can do it really quickly, within really minutes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And what's extraordinary is if you want to get a piece of machinery up there, you have to do destructive testing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So you have to destroy it and see what happens. How does it destroy it? Do little pieces of glass break everywhere?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: If so, that's a problem. So you have to redesign it and do fire testing. How does it burn? How does your device explode in a fire or doesn't it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: You have to test that and then you do vibration testing. So basically, if you want to fly one thing into space, you need to make four of them and destroy at least three of them to know how they die, how they destroy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Destructive, fire, and then vibration testing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I was just asking for a friend. How do you, from a scientific perspective, do destructive testing? And how do you do fire testing and how do you do vibration testing?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Vibration, like just large shakers. So that's mostly to simulate launch. They have a lot of machinery at NASA and at SpaceX to do just to make sure that it doesn't completely fall apart if it has a high vibrational, essentially force attached to it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So it's just kind of like a big shaker. Fire testing is just to simulate what would happen if there was a normal fire.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: That's something that gets up to, you know, the fire temperature is several hundred degrees Celsius. Open fire or are we talking like you put in a toaster? No, it's more like heat or is it actual flames? It's flames and heat.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But it's not like a kiln or anything like that. You don't want to know how does it burn in a kiln. It's more, is it flammable is the first big question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Like does it just start on fire? If it gets a little bit of flame on it, does it just light up like a Christmas tree? Is there a YouTube video of this? Did you film any of this?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Not, not, no. Aaron Burton might still have some of the videos. We're in the middle of doing some testing for the new sequencer called the Mark 1C. So I will make videos of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I would love to see that for anything for my private collection. This is very exciting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And the destructive testing is just often it can be something as simple as a hammer. It's really how does it shatter. You want to question is are there glass components and so.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So it's like office space. That scene with the fax machine. That's right. We blow into the dam. It feels good to be a gangster soundtrack. Yeah, that's a great scene.

body.input: So, you know, so for people who haven't seen 2001 Space Odyssey, HAL 9000 is very kind of focused on the mission,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: cares a lot about the mission and kind of wants to hurt the astronauts that try to get in the way of the mission.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I think he was doing it was programmed to do, which was just to follow the mission, but didn't have a sense of, you know, a broader duty.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: You could I mean, it was the broader duty, exactly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Maintaining the the well-being of astronauts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Yeah, or giving them another option. I think you viewed them as like completely expendable rather than say not completely.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It's a trade off.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So like a doctor has to make decisions like this, too. You're restricted on the resources.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: You have to make life and death decisions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So maybe HAL 9000 had a long term vision of what is good for the civilization back at home.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Maybe a deontogenic vision of what was the best duty for the genetics, you could say.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: What's deontogenic?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: It's a word I made up in the book is like, what is your genetic duties?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: When you think of your DNA, what are you supposed to do with it, which is kind of the value of life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But if HAL was a silicon based version of genetics, which is just his own maintenance of himself and self survival,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: you could argue he's doing the right thing for himself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: But I think a human in that circumstance might have tried to find a way to,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: even if the astronauts don't agree with the mission, to figure out somebody to get them on a different spacecraft to go away or something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And you have to at some point pick. But I think that's a false dichotomy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: I think HAL wasn't programmed to and didn't try to find a third solution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: Perhaps this is like Stuart Russell proposes this idea that AI systems should have self doubt.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: They should be always uncertain in their final decision.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And that would help HAL sort of get out of the local optimum of this is the mission.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: And then you're forced to kind of contend with other humans, with other entities on what is the right decision.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: So the worst thing about decisions from that perspective is if you're extremely confident

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

body.input: and you're stubborn and immovable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Mason: Space Travel, Colonization, and Long-Term Survival in Space | Lex Fridman Podcast #283
