metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: in the description.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: And now here's my conversation with Brian Greene.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: In your most recent book, Until the End of Time,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: you quote Bertrand Russell from a debate he had

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: about God in 1948.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: He says, quote, so far as scientific evidence goes,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: the universe has crawled by slow stages

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: to a somewhat pitiful result on this earth

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: and is going to crawl by still more pitiful stages

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: to a condition of universal death.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: If this is to be taken as evidence of purpose,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: I can only say that the purpose is one

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: that does not appeal to me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: I see no reason therefore to believe in any sort of God.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: That's quite a depressing statement.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: As you say, this is a bleak outlook on our universe

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: and the emergence of human consciousness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: So let me ask, what is the more hopeful perspective

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: to take on this story?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: Well, I think the more hopeful perspective

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: is to more fully understand

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: what was driving Bertrand Russell to this perspective.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: And then to see it within a broader context.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: And really that's in some sense what my book,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: Until the End of Time is all about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: But in brief, I would say that there's a lot of truth

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: to what Bertrand Russell was saying there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: When you look at the second law of thermodynamics,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: which is the underlying scientific idea

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: that's driving this notion that everything's gonna wither,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: decay, fall apart.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: Yeah, that's true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: Second law of thermodynamics establishes

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: that disorder, entropy, in aggregate is always on the rise.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: And that is indeed interpretable as disintegration

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: and destruction over sufficiently long time scales.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: But my view is when you recognize how special that makes us

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: that we are these exquisitely ordered configurations

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: of particles that only will last for a blink of an eye

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: in cosmological time like terms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: The fact that we're here and we can do what we do,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: to me, that's just really something that inspires gratitude

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: and wonder and a sense of deep purpose by virtue of being

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: these unique collections of entities that happen to rise up,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: look around and try to figure out where we are

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: and what the heck we should do with our time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: So it's not that I would disagree with Bertrand Russell

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: in terms of the basic physics and the basic unfolding,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: but I think it's really a matter of the slant

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: that you take on what it means for us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: So maybe we'll skip around a bit,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: but let me ask the biggest possible question then.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: You said purpose.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: So what's the meaning of it all then?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: Is there a meaning to life that we can take from this,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: from this brief emergence of complexity

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: that arises from simple things and then goes into a heat

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: death that is once again returns to simple things

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: as the march of the second law of thermodynamics goes on?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: I think there is,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: but I don't think it's a universal answer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: And so I think throughout the ages,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: there has been a kind of quest for some final way

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: of articulating meaning and purpose, whether it's God,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: whether it's love, whether it's companionship.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: I mean, many people put forward different ways

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: of taking this question on,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: and there is no one right answer when you recognize deeply

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: that the universe doesn't care.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: There is nothing out there that is the final answer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: It's not as though we need a more powerful telescope

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: and somehow if we can look deeply into the universe,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: all will become clear.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: In fact, the deeper we've looked,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: both literally and metaphorically,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: into the universe and into the structure of reality,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: the more it's become clear that we are just a momentary

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: byproduct of laws of physics that don't have

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: any emotional content.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: They don't have any intrinsic sense of meaning or purpose.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: And when you recognize that, you realize that searching

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: for the universal for this kind of a question

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: is a fool's errand.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: Every individual has the capacity to make their own meaning,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: to set their own purpose.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: And that's not some platitude, that is what we are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: Because there is no fundamental answer,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: it's what you make of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: And however much that may sound like a hallmark card,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: this really is the deep lesson of physics and science,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: more generally over the past few hundred years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: Well, there's some level where you can objectively say

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: that whatever we've got going on here is kind of peculiar.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: It's kind of special in terms of complexity

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: and maybe you can even begin to measure it

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: and like come up with metrics where whatever we've got

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: going on on earth, these like interesting

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: hierarchical complexities that form more and more

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: sophisticated biological system,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: that seems kind of unique when you look at the entirety

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: of the universe, the observable part that we can see

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: with our tools.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: I mean, so I have to ask, as you describe in your book

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: once again, Schrodinger wrote the book,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: What is Life?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: based on a few lectures he gave in 1944.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: So let me ask the fundamental question here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: What is life?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: This particular thing we've got going on here,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: this pocket of complexity that emerged

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: from such simple things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: Yeah, it's a tough question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: I asked that question even to Richard Dawkins once

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: and I already have my preconceived notion

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: which he pretty much confirmed,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: which is if one could give an answer to that question

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: that allowed you to sort of draw a line in the sand

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: between the not living and the living,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: then perhaps we would have the insight that we yearn for

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: in trying to say what is so special about life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: But the fact of the matter is it's a continuum.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: There's a continuum from the things

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: that we would typically call non-living inanimate

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: to the things that we obviously call animate

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: and full of the currents of life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: Somewhere in there, it is a question

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: of the complexity of the structure,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: the ability of the structure to take in raw material

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: from the environment and process it through a metabolism

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: that allows the structure to extract energy

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: and to release entropy to the wider environment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: Somewhere in those collections of biological processes

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: is the necessity or the necessary ingredients

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: and processes for life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: But drawing that line in the sand is not something

body.input: that we're able to do, but I would agree with you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: It's deeply peculiar.

body.input: It may in fact be unique,

body.input: but it may not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: It could be that the universe is such

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: that under fairly typical conditions,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: but in a way, when you think about it, doesn't matter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: in the sense that you are not eternal,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: the time scale hardly matters

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: because it's either the whole thing or not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: Because on the scales of eternity,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: on the scales of eternity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: And so maybe it won't be so hard for an artificial system

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: to feel that sense of mortality

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: because it will recognize the underlying physical laws

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: and recognize its own finitude.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: And then it'll be us and robots drinking beers,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: looking up at the stars and just,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Greene: Quantum Gravity, The Big Bang, Aliens, Death, and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #232

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: And this is back before,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: and cable and all that kind of stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: And so when we were there, they basically just said,

body.input: you're basically like, what happened?

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: And so I got home and I remember talking to my dad about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: the core American kind of talking points, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: Look, somebody from another country came here

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: and tried to kill Americans

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: and was successful in doing that.

body.input: And to some extent he just said,

body.input: and I'm willing to bet we're gonna go back after him.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: Did that wake you up a little bit to the idea

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: that there's evil out there,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: that even just the idea of terrorism,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: for many people that was,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: when it hits you on your own land,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: it really shakes up your mind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: In some sense, World War II,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: that's why World War II was fundamentally different

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: for Americans than it is for the people like in Russia,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: in England and France and in Europe in general,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: is there's something about when there's families,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: women, children dying on your own land, that's different.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: And that was one of the first times in America where like,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: on your, of course it's Pearl Harbor,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: but like this is like in recent history,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: it's like they hit us here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: That was like a profound idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: I think America was very, very good at exporting

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: the violence elsewhere for a long time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: And there was this element of complacency,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: but also this element of really just American superiority.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: That doesn't happen here, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: And I think that that woke people up not only to

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: kind of the idea that other places around the world

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: may not like the American ideals,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: may not like democracy and capitalism and that,

body.input: but also maybe we aren't as big, tough and secure

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: as we thought we were, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: And so obviously I think you see the kind of the over rotation

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: you know, kind of change that apparatus.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: But on top of that, I think that it really woke people up

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: to extremism around the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: And I don't know if necessarily there was a change

body.input: in the extremism as much as it just was an awareness thing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: I think that people kind of drew a line from,

body.input: was it 92 or 93 with the World Trade Center bombing

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: to deep levels of extremism and hatred of

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: kind of the American industrial complex,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: probably not that many.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: 2001, a lot of people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: And so I think that was, again, as a young kid,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: you don't understand a lot of this stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: You basically just, hey, somebody came here

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: and tried to kill Americans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: And so we should go fight back, right?

body.input: Was kind of the response I think that I had.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: in the context of money being able to buy time?

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: Or is happiness something else that is beyond all of this?

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: When people talk about this question,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: I think that they really focus on money

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: as a means to getting materialistic things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: So they want a big house, they want a boat,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: they want a fast car, they want whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: They think that's the stuff that will make them happy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: What I think about it is if you have resources,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: you can have time, and if you have time

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: and you spend it the way that you want to spend it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: then that's ultimately happiness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: So I always say to people,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: if you think that money doesn't buy you happiness,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: what if I told you that if you had more money,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: you could spend more time with your family?

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: It reframes it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: And now it's all about, I want to do certain things in life,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: but there's a lot of people who spend their life

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: not doing those things because they feel the need

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: to pursue economic means as a way to provide a living

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: or whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: And so I explained that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: I said, listen, in my opinion, again, it's my opinion,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: it's what makes me happy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: If I can leverage financial resources to create more time

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: to do the things I like, I'm happier.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: Might not work for everybody,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: but that's what works for me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: And so there's this element of,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: I don't care what other people think

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: if they like that or not, because they're not me, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: There's almost this element of,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: you gotta figure out what works for you,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: and if it works for me, then it's great.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: No, I think that will resonate with a lot of people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: I think that's a brilliant reframing of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: That said, you kind of imply there's a reason

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: behind this whole existence of ours, there's a meaning to it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: So let me ask, what is the meaning of life, Anthony?

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: Do you think about these ridiculous big questions

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: that have no answer every once in a while,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: or do you just enjoy the shit out of every day?

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: I answer it in a way that isn't meant to be accurate,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: it's meant to be the right answer for me,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: which is ultimately, and I talk to a lot of people

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: who always ask, what are you doing?

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: Why are you doing this?

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: I say, it's to be happy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: And the reason why I think of it that way

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: is I've got a friend, Jonathan Geller,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: who talks about enough being enough.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: And recently he talked about it in the context of Bitcoin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: And so Bitcoiners have two things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: Any Bitcoiner, if you talk to them,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: they believe the same two things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: One, they don't want the US dollar price to go up

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: because they actually want to acquire more Bitcoin, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: And then they go once they feel like they've got enough.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: But two is no matter how much they own,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: they think that they don't own enough

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: and they want to acquire more.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: And so at some point you say to yourself, what is enough?

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: And I think that the whole meaning of life

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: is to understand kind of what your level of satisfaction is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: And for some people that's a monetary thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: Some people that's a freedom of time thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: For some people it's an impact thing, whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: But just understanding that's important

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: and then going and accomplishing it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: And what I've found is that the people who I know

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: who have done this and been intentional about it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: they accomplish it on a much shorter timeline

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: than people who don't.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: There's some people who start thinking about it

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: as when they're 60.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: Naturally you're not going to accomplish it

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: before you're 60 if you just start thinking about it at 60.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: People who start thinking about it earlier can do it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: And so I think that's really it for me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: It's just like the meaning of life is to enjoy it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: The way I think about it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: that's because it's a really nice formulation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: I almost like to sort of oscillate back and forth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: So majority of the time is spent

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: at the mode of enough is enough of gratitude.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: Of basically being content with where you're at,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: like deeply appreciative of every moment

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: and all the Bitcoin, whatever Bitcoin you have

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: being deeply appreciative of it and that being enough.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: And then some fraction of time,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: perhaps it shrinks as you get older.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: Maybe there's an optimal trajectory there,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: but some fraction of time is spent

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: being deeply self-critical and nothing is enough.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: Nothing you've ever done is worth anything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: It's the, Marvin Minsky said the secret to success

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: is hating everything you've ever done.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: So that mode of just hating everything you've ever done

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: and just trying to improve, trying to make stuff better.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: Nothing is enough.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: It's never enough, that kind of stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: And then oscillating back and forth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: You don't have to have the same algorithm

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: operating throughout the day.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: You could just oscillate back and forth

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: and maybe reserve that gratitude part, the chill part

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: to when you're hanging out with family

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: and friends and loved ones.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: And then when you're alone or maybe at work,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: the madman comes out kind of thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: I also think it's kind of purpose-driven

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: in the sense of there's a lot of people

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: who have the, I need to do more,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: but in a somewhat altruistic way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: So there, take Elon as an example.

body.input: The idea of colonizing Mars, sure,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: if he is successful, he will be very rich.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: I don't think you or I or many people believe

body.input: he's doing it for the money, right?

body.input: There's a lot of other things he could do

body.input: that would be much easier that would make him tons of money.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: And so in some weird way, he has enough

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: because he's able to free himself from the constraints

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: of I need to acquire more resources.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: And he can focus on what is the thing

body.input: that I wanna work on regardless of money.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: And so in that pursuit that is non-economic,

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: you can be as selfish as you want

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: because ultimately you're not tied back

body.input: to this measurement tool.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: And so it's this, again, altruistic, non-monetary purpose.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: And I think that there's a lot of people

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: who spend their whole life looking for that

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: and they don't know what it is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: And so, again, some people may not think of it that way,

body.input: but if you can find something to do that, you win.

metadata.title: Podcast: Anthony Pompliano: Bitcoin | Lex Fridman Podcast #171

body.input: I don't think there's a better way to end it, Anthony.

body.input: I'm a huge fan.

body.input: Early on, you dreamed of AI systems

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: that self-improve recursively.

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: When was that dream born?

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: When I was a baby.

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: No, that's not true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: When I was a teenager.

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: And what was the catalyst for that birth?

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: What was the thing that first inspired you?

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: When I was a boy, I was thinking about what to do in my life

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: and then I thought the most exciting thing

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: is to solve the riddles of the universe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: And that means you have to become a physicist.

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: However, then I realized that there's something

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: even grander, you can try to build a machine

Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: So these long time lags, they translate into problem depth.

body.input: And most problems in this world are such

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: which is a logic programming language.

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: And the Japanese, they had this huge fifth generation AI

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: project, which was mostly about logic programming back then,

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: although neural networks existed and were well known back then.

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: And deep learning has existed since 1965,

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: since this guy in the Ukraine, Ivanknenko, started it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: But the Japanese and many other people,

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: they focused really on this logic programming.

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: And I was influenced to the extent

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: that I said, OK, let's take these biologically inspired

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: algorithms like evolution, programs,

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: and implement that in the language which I know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: which was Prolog, for example, back then.

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: And then in many ways, this came back later,

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: And without that, it would not be optimal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: Well, Markus Hutter's universal algorithm

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: for solving all well-defined problems

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: has a proof search on board.

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: But then on the other hand, because we

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: and suboptimal stuff, such as gradient-based search

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: and program space, rather than provably optimal things.

body.input: And are you optimistic about that future?

body.input: There's a lot of people concerned in the near term

body.input: about the transformation of the nature of work.

body.input: Are you optimistic about that future?

body.input: Are you nervous about that future?

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: And looking a little bit farther into the future,

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: there's people like Gailar Musk, Stuart Russell,

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: So in the near term, job loss in the long term existential

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: threat, are these concerns to you,

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: or are you ultimately optimistic?

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: So let's first address the near future.

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: We have had predictions of job losses for many decades.

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: For example, when industrial robots came along,

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: many people predicted that lots of jobs

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: are going to get lost.

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: And in a sense, they were right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: Because back then, there were car factories

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: and hundreds of people in these factories assembled cars.

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: And today, the same car factories

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: have hundreds of robots and maybe three

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: guys watching the robots.

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: On the other hand, those countries

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: that have lots of robots per capita, Japan, Korea, Germany,

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: Switzerland, a couple of other countries,

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: they have really low unemployment rates.

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: Somehow, all kinds of new jobs were created.

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: Back then, nobody anticipated those jobs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: And decades ago, I already said, it's

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: really easy to say which jobs are going to get lost,

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: but it's really hard to predict the new ones.

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: 30 years ago, who would have predicted all these people

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: making money as YouTube bloggers, for example?

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: 200 years ago, 60% of all people used

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: to work in agriculture.

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: Today, maybe 1%.

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: But still, only, I don't know, 5% unemployment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: Lots of new jobs were created.

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: And Homo ludens, the plain man, is

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: inventing new jobs all the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: Most of these jobs are not existentially necessary

metadata.title: Podcast: Juergen Schmidhuber: Godel Machines, Meta-Learning, and LSTMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #11

body.input: for the survival of our species.

body.input: There are only very few existentially necessary jobs,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: I mean, I think the thing that got me into computer science

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: and into artificial intelligence

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: was exactly this presupposition that

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: if we can get machines to think,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: or I should say this question,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: this philosophical question,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: if we can get machines to think,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: to understand, to process information the way we do,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: so if we can describe a procedure, describe a process,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: even if that process were the intelligence process itself,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: then what would be the difference?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: So from a philosophical standpoint,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: I'm not sure I'm convinced that there is.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: I mean, you can go in the direction of spirituality,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: you can go in the direction of the soul,

body.input: but in terms of what we can experience

body.input: from an intellectual and physical perspective,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: I'm not sure there is.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: Clearly there are different implementations,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: but if you were to say,

body.input: is a biological information processing system

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: fundamentally more capable than one we might be able

body.input: to build out of silicon or some other substrate,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: but is it really a far mystery

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: where a huge number of breakthroughs are needed

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: to be able to understand it,

body.input: or is it something that, for the most part,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: in the important aspects,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: echoes of the same kind of characteristics?

body.input: Yeah, that's interesting.

body.input: I mean, I think that studying-

body.input: What is the goal?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: Good, so I think there are a few goals.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: I think that understanding the human brain

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: and how it works is important for us

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: to be able to diagnose and treat issues

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: for us to understand our own strengths and weaknesses,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: both intellectual, psychological, and physical.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: So neuroscience and understanding the brain

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: from that perspective, there's a clear goal there.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: From the perspective of saying,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: I wanna mimic human intelligence,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: that one's a little bit more interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: Human intelligence certainly has a lot of things we envy.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: It's also got a lot of problems too.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: So I think we're capable of sort of stepping back

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: How do we want it to behave?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: Now, of course, it's somewhat of an interesting argument

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: because I'm sitting here as a human

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: the strengths and weaknesses of human intelligence

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: and say, gee, what is intelligence

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: and what do we really want out of it?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: And that in and of itself suggests that

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: human intelligence is something quite enviable,

body.input: that it can introspect that way.

body.input: And the flaws, you mentioned the flaws.

body.input: So humans have flaws.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: Yeah, I mean, I think that flaws that human intelligence has

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: is extremely prejudicial and biased

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: in the way it draws many inferences.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: Do you think those are, sorry to interrupt,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: do you think those are features or are those bugs?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: Do you think the prejudice, the forgetfulness,

body.input: the fear, what other flaws?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: List them all.

body.input: What, love?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: Maybe that's a flaw.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: You think those are all things that can be,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: get in the weight of intelligence

body.input: or the essential components of intelligence?

body.input: Well, again, if you go back and you define intelligence

body.input: as being able to sort of accurately, precisely,

body.input: rigorously reason, develop answers

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: and justify those answers in an objective way,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: yeah, then human intelligence has these flaws

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: in that it tends to be more influenced

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: by some of the things you said.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: And it's largely an inductive process,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: meaning it takes past data,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: uses that to predict the future,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: very advantageous in some cases,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: but fundamentally biased and prejudicial in other cases

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: because it's gonna be strongly influenced by its prior

body.input: is whether they're right or wrong

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: from some objective reasoning perspective,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Ferrucci: IBM Watson, Jeopardy & Deep Conversations with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #44

body.input: you're gonna favor them because those are the decisions

body.input: or those are the paths that succeeded in the past.

body.input: I think it requires training and teaching.

body.input: All right, so now here's the property thing. All right, so Locke says, if you look in the Bible

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: For us, that's the ball game. So what we write in our book and here we're just paying homage to the
