metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: death, thereafter anything is possible. And so you've got the stoics and you got the Epicureans

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: and then you got the Tibetan Book of the Dead and then you got like the medieval monks that

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: worked with like a skull on their desk. And the whole idea, I should back up a bit because,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: and just remind folks that our studies, when we remind people that they're going to die

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: You don't even know that death is on your mind. And so our point is that, and this is kind of

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: counterintuitive, and that is that the most problematic and unsavory human reactions to

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: death anxiety are malignant manifestations of repressed death anxiety. We try to make

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: to spend enough time entertaining the reality of the human condition, which is that you too will

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: like if you figure out death, somehow you won't die. So no, no. So my colleagues and good friends,

body.input: that I should just speak for myself, but I'm not going to lie. I'm not going to lie. I'm not going

body.input: very clear travelling

body.input: So when I first read The Denial of Death,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: I did construction work, I worked in a restaurant,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: and I was just like, well, wait a minute.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: in order to assuage death anxiety.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: And I was like, that's not acceptable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: Sure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: So how did he face his death?

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: Is there something interesting personal?

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: I think so.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: So interesting to me is Becker also from a Jewish family

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: claimed to be atheistic,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: did not identify ultimately as Jewish.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: I believe he converted to Christianity,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: but was himself a religious person.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: And he said he became religious

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: when his first child was born.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: Now religious, what does that mean?

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: Does he have a faith?

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: Well, let's talk more importantly is the afterlife.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: What's his view on the afterlife?

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: He was agnostic on that, but he did.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: Now, the denial of death is,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: there's a chapter devoted to Kierkegaard.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: And he talks about, for Kierkegaard,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: if you wanna become a mature,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: if you wanna become a mature individual,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: if you wanna learn something, you go to the university.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: If you wanna become a more mature individual,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: according to Kierkegaard,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: you gotta go to the school of anxiety.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: What Kierkegaard said is that we have to let

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: this vague dis-ease, put a hyphen between dis and ease,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: about death, Kierkegaard's point is

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: you have to really think about that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: You have to think about it and feel it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: You gotta let it seek in or seep into your mind,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: at which point, according to Kierkegaard,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: basically you realize that your present identity

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: is fundamentally a cultural construction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: You didn't choose the time and place of your birth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: You didn't choose your name.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: You didn't choose necessarily even the social role

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: that you occupy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: You might've chosen from what's available in your culture,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: but not from the full palette of human opportunities.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: And so what Kierkegaard said is that we need to realize

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: that we've been living a lie of sorts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: Becker calls it a necessary lie.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: And we have to momentarily dispose of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: And so now Kierkegaard says, well, here I am.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: I have shrugged off all of the cultural accoutrements

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: that I have used to define myself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: And now what am I or who am I?

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: This is like the ancient Greek tragedy

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: where the worst thing was to be no one or no thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: At this point, Kierkegaard said,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: you're really dangling on the precipice of oblivion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: And some people tumble into that abyss and never come out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: On the other hand, Kierkegaard said that what you can now do

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: metaphorically and literally is to rebuild yourself

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: from the ground up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: And in the New Testament, there's something

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: you have to die in order to be reborn.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: And Kierkegaard's view though,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: is that there's only one way to do that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: This is his proverbial leap into faith.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: And in Kierkegaard's case, it was faith in Christianity,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: that you can't have unbridled faith

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: in cultural constructions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: The only thing that you can have unequivocal faith in

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: is some kind of transcendent power.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: All right, but of course, this raises the question of,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: well, is that just another death denying belief system?

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: And at the end of the denial of death,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: Becker admits that there's no way to tell

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: while still advocating for what is ultimately

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: a religious stance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: Now, one of the things that I don't understand

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: and Becker has been the most singularly potent influence

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: in my academic and personal life,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: but a year or two ago,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: I started reading Martin Heidegger.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: I'm reading Being in Time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: And what I now wonder is why Becker,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: who refers to Heidegger from time to time in his work,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: why he didn't take Heidegger more seriously?

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: Because Heidegger is like a secular Kierkegaard.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: He has the same thing, which is death anxiety.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: Oh, and I should have pointed out

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: that what Kierkegaard says is that death anxiety,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: most people don't go to the school of anxiety.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: They flee from death anxiety

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: by embracing their cultural beliefs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: Kierkegaard says they then tranquilize themselves

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: with the trivial.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: And I love that phrase.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: Beautiful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: It's a beautiful phrase,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: because at the end of The Denial of Death,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: Becker's like, look, the average American

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: is either drinking or shopping or watching television.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: And they're all the same thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: Heidegger says the same thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: He says, look, and he acknowledges Kierkegaard.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: He says, what makes us feel unsettled,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: and evidently that's an English translation of angst,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: that we don't feel at home in the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: Heidegger says that's death anxiety.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: And one direction is the Kierkegaard one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: Heidegger calls it a flight from death.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: You just unself-reflexively cling

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: And Heidegger borrows the term tranquilized,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: but he points out that he doesn't care for that term,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: because tranquilized sounds like you're subdued,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: when in fact what most culturally constructed meat puppets do

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: is to be frenetically engaged with their surroundings

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: to ensure that they never sit still long enough

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: Heidegger says there's another way though.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: He's like, yo, what you can do is to come to terms

metadata.title: Podcast: Sheldon Solomon: Death and Meaning | Lex Fridman Podcast #117

body.input: with that death anxiety in the following way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: is just to run your shuffle a bunch of times

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: and see how many orientations of cards you get.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: You should get an equal distribution of all the cards.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: And with the naive method of shuffling, if you just look at the data,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: if you just brute force and say, OK, I don't know what's going to happen,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: you just write a program that does it a billion times

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: and then see what the buckets look like of the data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: And the Monty Hall problem is another example of that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: where you have three doors and somebody gives you information about another door.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: So the correct answer is you should always switch.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: And the Monty Hall problem, which is not intuitive

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: and it freaks people out all the time, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: But you can solve it with data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: If you write a program that does the Monty Hall game

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: and then never switches, then always switches, just compare,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: you would immediately see that you don't have to be smart, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: You don't have to figure out the answer algorithmically.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: You can just brute force it out with data and say,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: well, I know the answer is this because I ran the program a billion times

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: and these are the data buckets that I got from it, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: So empirically, you find it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: But what's the joy of that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: So for you, for you personally,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: outside of family, what motivates you in this process?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Well, to be honest, I don't really write a lot of code anymore.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: What I do at Discourse is like manager-y stuff,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: which I always kind of despised, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: As a programmer, you think of managers as people

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: who don't really do anything themselves.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: But the weird thing about code is you realize that language is code.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: The ability to direct other people lets you get more stuff done

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: than you could by yourself anyway.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: You said language is code?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Language is code. Meaning communication with other humans?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Yes, it is. You can think of it as systematic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: So what is it like to be...

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: What makes, before we get into programming,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: what makes a good manager? What makes a good leader?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Well, I think a leader, it's all about leading by example, first of all,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: like sort of doing and being the things that you want to be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Now, this can be kind of exhausting, particularly when you have kids,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: because you realize that your kids are watching you like all the time,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: like even in ways that you've stopped seeing yourself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Like the hardest person to see on the planet is really yourself, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: It's a lot easier to see other people and make judgments about them,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: but yourself, like you're super biased.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: You don't actually see yourself the way other people see you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Often you're very, very hard on yourself

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: in a way that other people really aren't going to be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: So, you know, that's one of the insights is, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: you've got to be really diligent about thinking like,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: am I behaving in a way that represents how I want other people to behave, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Like leading through example.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: There's a lot of examples of leaders that really mess this up, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Like they make decisions that are like, wow, that's why would, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: it's just it's it's it's a bad example for other people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: So I think leading by example is one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: The other one, I believe, is working really hard.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: And I don't mean like working exhaustively, but like showing a real

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: passion for the problem, like, you know, not necessarily your solution to the problem,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: but the problem itself is just one that you really believe in.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Like with discourse, for example, the problem that we're looking at,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: which is my current project, is how do you get people

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: in groups to communicate in a way that doesn't like break down

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: into the howling of wolves, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Like, how do you deal with trolling?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Not like technical problems of how do I get people to post paragraphs?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: How do I get people to use bold?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: How do people to use complete sentences?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Although those are problems as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: But like, how do I get people to get along with each other, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Like and solve whatever problem it is they set out to solve or,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: you know, reach some consensus on discussion or just like not hurt each other even.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Right. Like maybe it's a discussion that doesn't really matter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: But are people like yelling at each other? Right. And why? Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Like that's not the purpose of this kind of communication.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: So I would say, you know, leadership is about, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: setting an example, you know, doing the things that represent

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: what you want to be and making sure that you're actually doing those things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: And there's a trick to that, too, because the things you don't do

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: also say a lot about what you are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Yeah. So let's pause on that one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: So those two things are fascinating.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: So how do you have as a leader that self-awareness?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: So you just said it's really hard to be self-aware.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: So for you personally, or maybe for other leaders you've seen or look up to,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: how do you know the both of the things you're doing are the wrong things to be doing?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: The way you speak to others, the way you behave and the things you're not doing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: How do you get that signal?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: There's two aspects to that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: One is like processing feedback that you're getting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: So how do you get feedback?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Well, right. So are you getting feedback? Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: So one way we do it, for example, at Discourse, we have three co-founders

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: and we periodically talk about decisions before we make them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: So it's not like one person can make a mistake or like, wow, that's, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: there can be misunderstanding, things like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: So it's part of like group consensus of leadership is like, it's good to have.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: I think systems where there's one leader and that leader has the rule of absolute law

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: are just really dangerous in my experience.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: For communities, for example, like if you have a community that's run by one person,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: that one person makes all the decisions, that person is going to have a bad day.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Something could happen to that person, you know, something, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: there's a lot of variables.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: So like at first, when you think about leadership, have multiple people doing leadership

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: and have them talk amongst each other.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: So giving each other feedback about the decisions that they're making.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: And then when you do get feedback, I think there's that little voice in your head, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Like, or your gut or wherever you want to put it in your body.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: I think that voice is really important.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Like I think most people who have any kind of moral compass or like want to do,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: most people want to do the right thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: I do believe that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: I mean, there might be a handful of sociopaths out there that don't, but most people,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: they want other people to think of them as a good person.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: And why wouldn't you write?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Like, do you want people to despise you?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: I mean, that's just weird, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: So you have that little voice that sort of the angel and devil on your shoulder sort

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: of talking to you about like what you're doing, how you're doing, how does it make

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: you feel to make these decisions, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: And I think having some attunement to that voice is important.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: But you said that voice also for, I think it's a programmer situation too, where

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: sometimes the devil on the shoulders a little, a little too loud.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: So you're a little too self-critical for a lot of developers, especially when you

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: have introverted personality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: How do you struggle with the self-criticism or the criticism others?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: So one of the things of leadership is to do something that's potentially unpopular

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: or what people doubt you and you still go through with the decision.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: So what's that balance like?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: I think you have to walk people through your decision-making, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Like you have to, this is where blogging is really important.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Communication is so important.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Again, code language is just another kind of code is like, here is the program by

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: which I arrived at the conclusion that I'm going to reach, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: It's one thing to say, like, this is a decision, it's final deal with it, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: That's not usually satisfying to people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: But if you say, look, you know, we've been thinking on this problem for a while.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Here's some stuff that's happened.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Here's what we think is right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Here's our goals.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Here's what we want to achieve.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: And we've looked at these options and we think this of the available options is

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: the best option.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: People will be like, oh, okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: All right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Maybe I don't totally agree with you, but I can kind of see where you're coming

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: from and like, I see it's not just arbitrary decision delivered from a cloud

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: of flames in the sky, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: It's like a human trying to reach some kind of consensus about, you know, goals

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: and their goals might be different than yours.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: That's completely legit, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: But if you're making that clear, it's like, oh, well, the reason we don't agree

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: is because we have totally different goals, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Like how could we agree?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: It's not that you're a bad person.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: It's that we have radically different goals in mind when we started looking

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: at this problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: And the other one you said is passion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: So, or, uh, hard work, sorry.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Well, those are tied together to me in my mind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: I mean, let's say hard work and passion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Like for me, like, I just really love the problem discourse is sending out to

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: solve because in a way it's like, there's a, there's a vision of the world where it

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: all devolves into Facebook, basically owning everything and every aspect of

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: human communication.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: the table.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: So I would say smartphones have mostly a cultural shift more than a programming shift.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Now, your other question was about artificial intelligence and like,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: sort of devices predicting what you're going to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: And I do think there's some strength to that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: I think artificial intelligence kind of overselling it in terms of what it's doing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: It's more like people are predictable, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Like, let me give you an example.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: log in from New York City now, and then an hour later you log in from San Francisco.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: It's like, well, hmm, that's interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: How did you get from New York to San Francisco in one hour?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: So at that point you're like, okay, this is a suspicious login at that point.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: So we would alert you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: It's like, okay, but that's not AI, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: That's just a heuristic of like, how did you in one hour get 2000 miles, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: That doesn't mean you're not going to get it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: You grant, maybe you're on a VPN.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: There's other ways to happen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: But that's just a basic prediction based on the idea that people pretty much don't move

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: around that much.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Like they may travel occasionally, but like nobody, I mean, unless you're a traveling

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: salesman that's literally traveling the world every day, like there's so much repetition

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: and predictability in terms of things you're going to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: And I think good software anticipates your needs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Like, for example, Google, I think it's called Google Now or whatever that Google thing is

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: every day?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Well, that's probably where you work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: That kind of stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: I do think computers can get a lot better at that, but I hesitate to call it like full

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: blown AI.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: It's just computers getting better at like, first of all, they have a ton of data because

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: everybody has a smartphone.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: about like, you know, communication and feeding that into some, some basic heuristics and

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: maybe some fancy algorithms that turn it into predictions of anticipating your needs like,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: like a friend would, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Like, oh, hey, I see your home.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: of programming is better?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: I do think that is possible because there's a lot of repetition in programming, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: It looks like you're writing a for loop.

body.input: Um, but there are patterns in code, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Right. That's not AI per se.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: It's just, you know, building better Lego bricks, bigger Lego bricks that have more

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: So people don't have to worry about the low level stuff as much anymore.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Like WordPress, for example, to me is like a tool for somebody who isn't a programmer

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: to do something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: I mean, you can turn WordPress into anything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: It's kind of crazy actually through pro plugins, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: And that's not programming per se.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: It's just Lego bricks stacking WordPress elements, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: and less like actual programming.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: And that's a good thing, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: programming remaining with us for a long time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Like you said, Unix, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: You see ultimately, you know, this stuff's just being there out of momentum.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: I kind of do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: I mean, I was a big believer in windows early on and I was a big, you know, I was like

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Unix, what a waste of time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: But over time I've completely flipped on that where I was like, okay, the Unix guys

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: were right and pretty much Microsoft and windows were kind of wrong.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: At least on the server side, not on the desktop.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: You need a GUI, you know, that stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: And yeah, the two philosophies like Apple built on Unix, effectively Darwin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: And on the desktop, it's a slightly different story, but on the server side where

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: you're going to be programming.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Now it's a question of where the programming is going to be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: There's going to be a lot more like client side programming because technically

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: discourse is client side programming.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: The way you get discourse, we deliver a big ball of JavaScript, which is then

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: executed locally.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: So we're really using a lot more local computing power.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: But to the extent that a lot of programming is still going to be server side, I would

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: say, yeah, the Unix philosophy definitely won and there'll be different veneers

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: over Unix, but it's still, if you, if you peel away one or two layers, it's going

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: to be Unix-y for a long time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: I think Unix won.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: I mean, so definitively.

body.input: Cool.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: So what's the future hold for the Unix side?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: I mean, the discourse, continuing the discourse in trying to improve

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: conversation on the web.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: version.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: So we're still, you know, five years in, this is the part where it starts getting

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Atwood: Stack Overflow and Coding Horror | Lex Fridman Podcast #7

body.input: Like we have a good product now, discourse.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And now here's my conversation with Russ Tedjerk.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: What is the most beautiful motion of a animal or robot

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: that you've ever seen?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think the most beautiful motion of a robot

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: has to be the passive dynamic walkers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think there's just something fundamentally beautiful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: The ones in particular that Steve Collins built

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: with Andy Ruina at Cornell, a 3D walking machine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So it was not confined to a boom or a plane

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: that you put it on top of a small ramp,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: give it a little push.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It's powered only by gravity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: No controllers, no batteries whatsoever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It just falls down the ramp.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And at the time it looked more natural, more graceful,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: more human-like than any robot we'd seen to date,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: powered only by gravity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: How does it work?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Well, okay, the simplest model, it's kind of like a slinky.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It's like an elaborate slinky.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: One of the simplest models we used to think about it

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: is actually a rimless wheel.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So imagine taking a bicycle wheel, but take the rim off.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So it's now just got a bunch of spokes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: If you give that a push,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: it still wants to roll down the ramp.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But every time its foot, its spoke comes around

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and hits the ground, it loses a little energy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Every time it takes a step forward,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: it gains a little energy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Those things can come into perfect balance

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and actually they want to.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It's a stable phenomenon.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: If it's going too slow, it'll speed up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: If it's going too fast, it'll slow down

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and it comes into a stable periodic motion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Now you can take that rimless wheel,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: which doesn't look very much like a human walking,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: take all the extra spokes away, put a hinge in the middle.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Now it's two legs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: That's called our compass gait walker.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: That can still, you give it a little push,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: starts falling down a ramp.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Looks a little bit more like walking.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: At least it's a biped.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But what Steve and Andy and Ted McGeer

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: started the whole exercise, but what Steve and Andy did

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: was they took it to this beautiful conclusion

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: where they built something that had knees, arms, a torso.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: The arms swung naturally, give it a little push

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and that looked like a stroll through the park.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: How do you design something like that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I mean, is that art or science?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It's on the boundary.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think there's a science to getting close to the solution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think there's certainly art in the way that they,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: they made a beautiful robot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But then the finesse, because this was where

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: they were working with a system

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: that wasn't perfectly modeled, wasn't perfectly controlled,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: there's all these little tricks

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: that you have to tune the suction cups at the knees,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: for instance, so that they stick,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: but then they release at just the right time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Or there's all these little tricks of the trade,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: which really are art, but it was a point.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I mean, it made the point.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: We were, at that time, the walking robot,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: the best walking robot in the world was Honda's Asimo.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Absolutely marvel of modern engineering.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Is this 90s?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: This was in 97 when they first released,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: it sort of announced P2 and then it went through.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It was Asimo by then in 2004.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And it looks like this very cautious walking,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: like you're walking on hot coals or something like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think it gets a bad rap.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Asimo is a beautiful machine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It does walk with its knees bent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Our Atlas walking had its knees bent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But actually Asimo was pretty fantastic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But it wasn't energy efficient.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Neither was Atlas when we worked on Atlas.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: None of our robots that have been that complicated

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: have been very energy efficient.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But there's a thing that happens when you do control.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: When you try to control a system of that complexity,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But maybe instead of trying to take the forces

body.input: push us around and we go with the flow.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Yeah, but okay, so that sounds very Zen,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I don't know if it's thousands, but it's a lot.

body.input: It takes some patience.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: There's no question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So in that sense, control might help a little bit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: isn't the way we should.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Got it, so what about on the animal side?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: The ones that figured out how to move efficiently.
