metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: in the movement of any particular kind?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I do have a favorite example.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So it sort of goes with the passive walking idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So is there, how energy efficient are animals?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Okay, there's a great series of experiments

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: by George Lauder at Harvard and Mike Tranifilo at MIT.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: were these rainbow trout, because there was a phenomenon

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: well understood that rainbow trout,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: when they're swimming upstream at mating season,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: they kind of hang out behind the rocks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And it looks like, I mean, that's tiring work

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Maybe there's something energetically interesting there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So they tried to recreate that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: They put in this water tunnel, a rock basically,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: that you would see in a stream.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And they put a real fish behind this

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and watched how it swims.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And the amazing thing is that if you watch from above,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: what the fish swims when it's not behind a rock,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: it has a particular gate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: You can identify the fish the same way you look at a human

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: looking at walking down the street,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: you sort of have a sense of how human walks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: The fish has a characteristic gate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: You put that fish behind the rock, its gate changes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And what they saw was that it was actually resonating

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and kind of surfing between the vortices.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Now, here was the experiment that really was the clincher,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: because it wasn't clear how much of that

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: was mechanics of the fish,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: how much of that is control, the brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So the clincher experiment,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and maybe one of my favorites to date,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: although there are many good experiments.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: They took, this was now a dead fish.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: They took a dead fish, they put a string that went,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: that tied the mouth of the fish to the rock

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: so it couldn't go back and get caught in the grates.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And then they asked, what would that dead fish do

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: when it was hanging up behind the rock?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And so what you'd expect,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: it sort of flopped around like a dead fish

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: in the vortex wake until something sort of amazing happens.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And this video is worth putting in.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: What happens?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: The dead fish basically starts swimming upstream.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It's completely dead, no brain, no motors, no control,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: but it's somehow the mechanics of the fish

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: resonate with the vortex street

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and it starts swimming upstream.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It's one of the best examples ever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Who do you give credit for that too?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Is that just evolution constantly just figuring out

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: by killing a lot of generations of animals,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: like the most efficient motion?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Is that, or maybe the physics of our world completely,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: is like if evolution applied not only to animals,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: but just the entirety of it somehow drives to efficiency,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I don't know if that question even makes any sense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I understand the question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: That's the reason, I mean, do they co-evolve?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I mean, there are experiments that people do,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: to unusual situations and recover efficiency.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So there seems like at least in one direction,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think there is reason to believe

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: that the animal's motor system

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and probably its mechanics adapt

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: in order to be more efficient,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: but efficiency isn't the only goal, of course.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Sometimes it's too easy to think about only efficiency,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: not get eaten, and then all other things being equal,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: try to save energy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: By the way, let's draw a distinction

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: between control and mechanics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Yeah, I mean, I think part of the point is that

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: we shouldn't draw a line as clearly as we tend to,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: but on a robot, we have motors,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and we have the links of the robot, let's say.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: If the motors are turned off,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: the robot has some passive dynamics, okay?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Gravity does the work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: You can put springs, I would call that mechanics, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: If we have springs and dampers,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: which are muscles, are springs and dampers and tendons,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: but then you have something that's doing active work,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: putting energy in your motors on the robot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: The controller's job is to send commands to the motor

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: that add new energy into the system, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So the mechanics and control interplay

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: somewhere the divide is around, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: did you decide to send some commands to your motor,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: or did you just leave the motors off

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and let them do their work?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: or the control side?

body.input: So like, if you look at biological systems,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: or if, you know, we're living in a pandemic now,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: certainly with exercise, they evolve,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and it's my fifth metacarpal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: to address the new circumstances.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So the idea that somehow it's only our brain

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: that's adapting or evolving is not right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Maybe sticking on evolution for a bit,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: because it's tended to create some interesting things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Bipedal walking, do you, why the heck did evolution give us,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think we're, are we the only mammals that walk on two feet?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: No, I mean, there's a bunch of animals that do it a bit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: A bit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think we are the most successful bipeds.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think some, I think I read somewhere that the reason

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: the evolution made us walk on two feet is because

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: there's an advantage to being able to carry food back

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: to the tribe or something like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So like you can carry,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: it's kind of this communal cooperative thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So like to carry stuff back to a place of shelter

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and so on to share with others.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Do you understand at all the value of walking on two feet

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: from both a robotics and a human perspective?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Yeah, there are some great books written about evolution

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: of walking, evolution of the human body.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think it's easy though to make bad evolutionary arguments.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Sure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Most of them are probably bad, but what else can we do?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I mean, I think a lot of what dominated our evolution

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: probably was not the things that worked well sort of

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: in the steady state when things are good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But for instance, people talk about what we should eat now

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: because our ancestors were meat eaters or whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Oh yeah, I love that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But probably the reason that one pre-homo sapien species

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: versus another survived was not because of whether they

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: ate well when there was lots of food.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But when the ice age came, probably one of them happened

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: to be in the wrong place.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: One of them happened to forage a food that was okay

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: even when the glaciers came or something like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: There's a million variables that contributed

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and are actually the amount of information

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: we're working with in telling these stories,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: these evolutionary stories is very little.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So yeah, just like you said, it seems like if we study

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: history, it seems like history turns on these little events

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: that otherwise would seem meaningless.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But in the grant, like in retrospect, were turning points.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Absolutely.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And that's probably how, like somebody got hit in the head

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: back in the cave days and somebody get angry

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and that turned warring tribes combined with the environment,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: all those millions of things and the meat eating,

body.input: what your dietary processes are like,

body.input: but these days I've been eating only meat,

body.input: yeah, probably make evolutionary arguments and say,

body.input: But you're right, these evolutionary arguments

body.input: can be flawed, but is there anything interesting

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: The most, I mean, the reason I spent a long time

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: There are people that make pretty compelling arguments,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and so maybe that argument falls aside.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think so.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Maybe even that's a key to intelligence or something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But, okay, what if Newton and Galileo had deep learning,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and they had done a bunch of experiments,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and they told the world, here's your weights of your neural network.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: We've solved the problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Where would we be today?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I don't think we'd be as far as we are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: There's something to be said about having the simplest explanation for a phenomenon.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So I don't doubt that we can train neural networks to predict even physical,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: you know, F equals MA type equations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But I maybe I want another Newton to come along,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: because I think there's more to do in terms of coming up with the simple models

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: for more complicated tasks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Let's not offend AI systems from 50 years from now that are listening to this

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: that are probably better at, might be better coming up with F equals MA equations themselves.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Sorry, I actually think learning is probably a route to achieving this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But the representation matters, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And I think having a function that takes my inputs to outputs that is arbitrarily complex

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: may not be the end goal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think there's still, you know, the most simple or parsimonious explanation for the data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Simple doesn't mean low dimensional.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: That's one thing I think that we've, a lesson that we've learned.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So, you know, a standard way to do model reduction or system identification and controls

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: is to, the typical formulation is that you try to find the minimal state dimension

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: realization of a system that hits some error bounds or something like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And that's maybe not, I think we're learning that that was,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: that state dimension is not the right metric.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Of complexity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Of complexity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But for me, I think a lot about contact, the mechanics of contact.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: A robot hand is picking up an object or something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And when I write down the equations of motion for that, they look incredibly complex.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Not because, actually not so much because of the dynamics of the hand when it's moving,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: but it's just the interactions and when they turn on and off.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So having a high dimensional, you know, but simple description of what's happening out here is fine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But if when I actually start touching, if I write down a different dynamical system

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: for every polygon on my robot hand and every polygon on the object,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: whether it's in contact or not with all the combinatorics that explodes there,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: then that's too complex.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So I need to somehow summarize that with a more intuitive physics way of thinking.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And I'm very optimistic that machine learning will get us there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: First of all, I mean, I'll probably do it in the introduction,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: but you're one of the great robotics people at MIT.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: You're a professor at MIT.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: You teach a lot of amazing courses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: You run a large group.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And you have an important history for MIT, I think,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: as being a part of the DARPA Robotics Challenge.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Can you maybe first say what is the DARPA Robotics Challenge

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and then tell your story around it, your journey with it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Yeah, sure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So the DARPA Robotics Challenge, it came on the tails of the DARPA Grand Challenge

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and DARPA Urban Challenge, which were the challenges that brought us,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: put a spotlight on self-driving cars.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Gil Pratt was at DARPA and pitched a new challenge that involved disaster response.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It didn't explicitly require humanoids, although humanoids came into the picture.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: This happened shortly after the Fukushima disaster in Japan,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and our challenge was motivated roughly by that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: because that was a case where if we had had robots that were ready to be sent in,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: there's a chance that we could have averted a disaster.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And certainly after the – in the disaster response,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: there were times where we would have loved to have sent robots in.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So in practice, what we ended up with was a grand challenge,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: a DARPA Robotics Challenge, where Boston Dynamics was to make humanoid robots.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: People like me and the amazing team at MIT were competing first in a simulation challenge

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: to try to be one of the ones that wins the right to work on one of the Boston Dynamics humanoids

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: in order to compete in the final challenge, which was a physical challenge.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And at that point, it was already – so it was decided as humanoid robots early on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So there were two tracks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: You could enter as a hardware team where you brought your own robot,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: or you could enter through the Virtual Robotics Challenge as a software team

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: that would try to win the right to use one of the Boston Dynamics robots.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Which are called Atlas humanoid robots.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It was a 400-pound marble, but a pretty big, scary-looking robot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Expensive, too, at least at the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Okay, so how did you feel at the prospect of this kind of challenge?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I mean, it seems – autonomous vehicles, I guess that sounds hard,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: but not really from a robotics perspective. It's like, didn't they do it in the 80s?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It's the kind of feeling I would have when you first look at the problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It's on wheels, but humanoid robots, that sounds really hard.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So what – psychologically speaking, what were you feeling?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Excited, scared? Why the heck did you get yourself involved in this kind of messy challenge?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: We didn't really know for sure what we were signing up for,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: in the sense that you could have had something that, as it was described in the call for participation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: that could have put a huge emphasis on the dynamics of walking and not falling down

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and walking over rough terrain, or the same description,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: because the robot had to go into this disaster area and turn valves and pick up a drill,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: cut a hole through a wall, it had to do some interesting things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: The challenge could have really highlighted perception and autonomous planning,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: or it ended up that locomoting over complex terrain played a pretty big role in the competition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And the degree of autonomy wasn't clear?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: The degree of autonomy was always a central part of the discussion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So what wasn't clear was how far we would be able to get with it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So the idea was always that you want semi-autonomy,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: that you want the robot to have enough compute that you can have a degraded network link to a human.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And so the same way we had degraded networks at many natural disasters,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: you'd send your robot in, you'd be able to get a few bits back and forth,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: but you don't get to have enough, potentially, to fully operate the robot, every joint of the robot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And then the question was, and the gamesmanship of the organizers,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: was to figure out what we're capable of, push us as far as we could,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: so that it would differentiate the teams that put more autonomy on the robot

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and had a few clicks and just said, go there, do this, go there, do this,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: versus someone who's picking every footstep or something like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So what were some memories?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Painful, triumphant from the experience?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Like what was that journey?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Maybe if you can dig in a little deeper, maybe even on the technical side, on the team side,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: that whole process of from the early idea stages to actually competing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I mean, this was a defining experience for me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It came at the right time for me in my career.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I got tenure before I was due a sabbatical,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and most people do something relaxing and restorative for a sabbatical.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So you got tenure before this?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Yeah, yeah, yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It was a good time for me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: We had a bunch of algorithms that we were very happy with.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: We wanted to see how far we could push them,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and this was a chance to really test our mettle, to do more proper software engineering.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: The team, we all just worked our butts off.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: We're in that lab almost all the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Okay, so there were some, of course, high highs and low lows throughout that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Anytime you're not sleeping and devoting your life to a 400-pound humanoid.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I remember actually one funny moment where we're all super tired,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: so Atlas had to walk across cinder blocks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: That was one of the obstacles.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And I remember Atlas was powered down and hanging limp on its harness,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and the humans were there picking up and laying the brick down

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: so that the robot could walk over it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And I thought, what is wrong with this?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: We've got a robot just watching us do all the manual labor

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: so that it can take its little stroll across the terrain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But even the virtual robotics challenge was super nerve-racking and dramatic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I remember, so we were using Gazebo as a simulator on the cloud,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and there was all these interesting challenges.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think the investment that OSR FC, whatever they were called at that time,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Brian Gerke's team at Open Source Robotics,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: they were pushing on the capabilities of Gazebo

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: in order to scale it to the complexity of these challenges.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So up to the virtual competition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So the virtual competition was you will sign on at a certain time,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and we'll have a network connection to another machine on the cloud

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: that is running the simulator of your robot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And your controller will run on this computer,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and the physics will run on the other, and you have to connect.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Now, the physics, they wanted it to run at real-time rates

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: because there was an element of human interaction,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and humans, if you do want to tele-op, it works way better if it's at frame rate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Oh, cool.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But it was very hard to simulate these complex scenes at real-time rate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So right up to days before the competition,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: the simulator wasn't quite at real-time rate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And that was great for me because my controller was solving a pretty big optimization problem,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and it wasn't quite at real-time rate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So I was fine, I was keeping up with the simulator, we were both running at about 0.7.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And I remember getting this email, and by the way, the perception folks on our team hated that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: they knew that if my controller was too slow, the robot was going to fall down,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and no matter how good their perception system was, if I can't make my controller fast enough.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Anyways, we get this email like three days before the virtual competition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It's for all the marbles, we're going to either get a humanoid robot or we're not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And we get an email saying, good news, we made the robot, the simulator faster.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It's now at one point.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And I was just like, oh man, what are we going to do here?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So that came in late at night for me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: A few days ahead.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: A few days ahead.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I went over, it happened that Frank Pimentor, who's a very, very sharp,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: he was a student at the time working on optimization, he was still in lab.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Frank, we need to make the quadratic programming solver faster.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Not like a little faster, it's actually, you know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And we wrote a new solver for that QP together that night.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And you solve it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So there's a really hard optimization problem that you're constantly solving.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: You didn't make the optimization problem simpler?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: You wrote a new solver?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So, I mean, your observation is almost spot on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: What we did was what everybody, I mean, people know how to do this,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: but we had not yet done this idea of warm starting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So we are solving a big optimization problem at every time step.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But if you're running fast enough, the optimization problem you're solving

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: on the last time step is pretty similar to the optimization you're going to solve with the next.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: We, of course, had told our commercial solver to use warm starting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But even the interface to that commercial solver was causing us these delays.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So what we did was we basically wrote, we called it fast QP at the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: We wrote a very lightweight, very fast layer, which would basically check if nearby solutions

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: to the quadratic program, which were very easily checked, could stabilize the robot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And if they couldn't, we would fall back to the solver.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: You couldn't really test this well, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So we always knew that if we fell back to, if we, it got to the point where if for some reason

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: things slowed down and we fell back to the original solver, the robot would actually literally fall down.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So it was a harrowing sort of edge we were, ledge we were sort of on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But I mean, actually, like the 400 pound humanoid could come crashing to the ground if you,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: if your solver is not fast enough.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But we have lots of good experiences.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Can I ask you a weird question I get about idea of hard work?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So actually people, like students of yours that I've interacted with and just in robotics, people in general,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: but they have moments at moments have worked harder than most people I know in terms of,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: if you look at different disciplines of how hard people work, but they're also like the happiest,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: like just like, I don't know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It's the same thing with like running people that push themselves to like the limit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: They also seem to be like the most like full of life somehow.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And I get often criticized, like, you're not getting enough sleep.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: What are you doing to your body? Blah, blah, blah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Like this kind of stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And I usually just kind of respond like I'm doing what I love.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I'm passionate about it. I love it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I feel like it's it's invigorating.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I actually think I don't think the lack of sleep is what hurts you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think what hurts you is stress and lack of doing things that you're passionate about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But in this world, I mean, can you comment about why the heck robotics people are

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: willing to push themselves to that degree?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Is there value in that? And why are they so happy?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think I think you got it right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I mean, I think the causality is not that we work hard and I think other disciplines work very hard, too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But it's I don't think it's that we work hard and therefore we are happy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think we found something that we're truly passionate about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It makes us very happy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And then we get a little involved with it and spend a lot of time on it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: What a luxury to have something that you want to spend all your time on. Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: We could talk about this for many hours, but maybe if we could pick,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: is there something on the technical side, on the approach that you took that's interesting

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: that turned out to be a terrible failure or a success that you carry into your work today

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: about all the different ideas that were involved in making,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: whether in the in the simulation or in the in the real world, making the semi-autonomous system work?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I mean, it really did teach me something fundamental about what it's going to take

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: to get robustness out of a system of this complexity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I would say the DARPA challenge really was foundational in my thinking.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think the autonomous driving community thinks about this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think lots of people thinking about safety critical systems that might have machine learning in the loop

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: are thinking about these questions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: For me, the DARPA challenge was the moment where I realized, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: we've spent every waking minute running this robot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And again, for the physical competition, days before the competition,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: we saw the robot fall down in a way it had never fallen down before.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I thought, you know, how could we have found that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: We only have one robot. It's running almost all the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: We just didn't have enough hours in the day to test that robot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Something has to change. Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And I think that, I mean, I would say that the team that won was from KAIST,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: was the team that had two robots and was able to do not only incredible engineering,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: just absolutely top-rate engineering,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: but also they were able to test at a rate and discipline that we didn't keep up with.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: What does testing look like? What are we talking about here?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Like what's a loop of tests? Like from start to finish, what is a loop of testing?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Yeah. I mean, I think there's a whole philosophy to testing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: There's the unit tests and you can do that on a hardware.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: You can do that in a small piece of code.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: If you write one function, you should write a test that checks that function's input outputs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: You should also write an integration test at the other extreme of running the whole system together,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: that try to turn on all of the different functions that you think are correct.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It's much harder to write the specifications for a system-level test,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: especially if that system is as complicated as a humanoid robot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But the philosophy is sort of the same.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: On the real robot, it's no different, but on a real robot, it's impossible to run the same experiment twice.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So if you see a failure, you hope you caught something in the logs that tell you what happened,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: but you'd probably never be able to run exactly that experiment again.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And right now, I think our philosophy is just basically Monte Carlo estimation,
