metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: is just run as many experiments as we can, maybe try to set up the environment

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: to make the things we are worried about happen as often as possible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But really, we're relying on somewhat random search in order to test.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Maybe that's all we'll ever be able to, but I think, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: because there's an argument that the things that will get you are the things that are really nuanced in the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And it would be very hard to, for instance, put back in a simulation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Yeah, I guess the edge cases. What was the hardest thing?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Like, so you said walking over rough terrain, like just taking footsteps.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I mean, people, it's so dramatic and painful in a certain kind of way to watch these videos from the DRC of robots falling.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It's just so heartbreaking. I don't know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Maybe it's because for me, at least, we anthropomorphize the robot. Of course, it's also funny for some reason.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Like, humans falling is funny for some dark reason. I'm not sure why it is so, but it's also like tragic and painful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And so speaking of which, I mean, what made the robots fall and fail in your view?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So I can tell you exactly what happened on our...

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I contributed one of those, our team contributed one of those spectacular falls.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Every one of those falls has a complicated story.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I mean, at one time, the power effectively went out on the robot because it had been sitting at the door

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: waiting for a green light to be able to proceed and its batteries, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and therefore it just fell backwards and smashed its head to the ground.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And it was hilarious, but it wasn't because of bad software, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But for ours, so the hardest part of the challenge, the hardest task in my view, was getting out of the Polaris.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It was actually relatively easy to drive the Polaris.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Can you tell the story so I can interrupt the story of the car?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: People should watch this video. I mean, the thing you've come up with is just brilliant. But anyway, sorry.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Yeah, we kind of joke. We call it the big robot little car problem because

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: somehow the race organizers decided to give us a 400 pound humeroid.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And they also provided the vehicle, which is a little Polaris, and the robot didn't really fit in the car.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So you couldn't drive the car with your feet under the steering column.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: We actually had to straddle the main column of the...

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and have basically one foot in the passenger seat, one foot in the driver's seat, and then drive with our left hand.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But the hard part was we had to then park the car, get out of the car.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It didn't have a door. That was OK.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But it's just getting up from crouch, from sitting, when you're in this very constrained environment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: First of all, I remember after watching those videos, I was much more cognizant of how hard it is for me to get in and out of the car, and out of the car especially.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It's actually a really difficult control problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I'm very cognizant of it when I'm injured for whatever reason.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It's really hard.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So how did you approach this problem?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: You think of NASA's operations and they have these pre-launched checklists and the like.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: We weren't far off from that. We had this big checklist.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: On the first day of the competition, we were running down our checklist.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: One of the things we had to do, we had to turn off the controller, the piece of software that was running that would drive the left foot of the robot in order to accelerate on the gas.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Then we turned on our balancing controller.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: The nerves, jitters of the first day of the competition, someone forgot to check that box and turned that controller off.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: We used a lot of motion planning to figure out a sort of configuration of the robot that we could get up and over.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: We relied heavily on our balancing controller.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Basically, when the robot was in one of its most precarious configurations trying to sneak its big leg out of the side,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: the other controller that thought it was still driving told its left foot to go like this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: That wasn't good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It turned disastrous for us because what happened was a little bit of push here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Actually, we have videos of us running into the robot with a 10-foot pole and it will recover.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: This is a case where there's no space to recover.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: A lot of our secondary balancing mechanisms about take a step to recover, they were all disabled because we were in the car and there was no place to step.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: We were relying on our just lowest level reflexes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Even then, I think just hitting the foot on the floor, we probably could have recovered from it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: The thing that was bad that happened is when we did that and we jostled a little bit, the tailbone of our robot was only a little off the seat.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It hit the seat and the other foot came off the ground just a little bit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Nothing in our plans had ever told us what to do if your butt is on the seat and your feet are in the air.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Feet in the air.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Then the thing is once you get off the script, things can go very wrong because even our state estimation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: our system that was trying to collect all the data from the sensors and understand what's happening with the robot, it didn't know about this situation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It was predicting things that were just wrong.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Then we did a violent shake and fell off and our face first on out of the robot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But into the destination.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: That's true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: We fell in and we got our point for egress.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: That's interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Is there any hope for Atlas to be able to do something when it's just on its butt and feet in the air?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Absolutely.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: That is one of the big challenges.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think it's still true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Boston Dynamics and Animo and there's this incredible work on legged robots happening around the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Most of them still are very good at the case where you're making contact with the world at your feet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: They have typically point feet relatively.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: There are balls on their feet for instance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: If those robots get in a situation where the elbow hits the wall or something like this, that's a pretty different situation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Now they have layers of mechanisms that will make the more mature solutions have ways in which the controller won't do stupid things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But a human for instance is able to leverage incidental contact in order to accomplish a goal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: In fact, if you push me, I might actually put my hand out and make a brand new contact.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: The feet of the robot are doing this on quadrupeds.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But we mostly in robotics are afraid of contact on the rest of our body, which is crazy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: There's this whole field of motion planning, collision free motion planning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And we write very complex algorithms so that the robot can dance around and make sure it doesn't touch the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So people are just afraid of contact because contact is seen as a difficult...

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It's still a difficult control problem and sensing problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Now you're a serious person.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I'm a little bit of an idiot and I'm going to ask you some dumb questions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So I do martial arts, so like Jiu Jitsu, I wrestled my whole life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So let me ask the question, whenever people learn that I do any kind of AI or like I mentioned robots and things like that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: they say, when are we going to have robots that can win in a wrestling match or in a fight against a human?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So we just mentioned sitting on your butt, if you're in the air, that's a common position.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Jiu Jitsu, when you're on the ground, you're a near down opponent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Like how difficult do you think is the problem?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And when will we have a robot that can defeat a human in a wrestling match?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And we're talking about a lot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Like, I don't know if you're familiar with wrestling, but essentially...

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Not very.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It's basically the art of contact.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It's like, it's because you're picking contact points and then using like leverage, like to off balance, to trick people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Like you make them feel like you're doing one thing and then they change their balance and then you switch what you're doing and then results in a throw or whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So like it's basically the art of multiple contacts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Awesome. It's a nice description of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So there's also an opponent in there, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Very dynamic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Right. If you are wrestling a human and are in a game theoretic situation with a human, that's still hard.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But just to speak to the, you know, quickly reasoning about contact part of it, for instance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And maybe even throwing the game theory out of it, almost like a non-dynamic opponent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Right. There's reasons to be optimistic, but I think our best understanding of those problems are still pretty hard.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I have been increasingly focused on manipulation, partly where that's a case where the contact has to be much more rich.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And there are some really impressive examples of deep learning policies, controllers that can appear to do good things through contact.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: We've even got new examples of deep learning models of predicting what's going to happen to objects as they go through contact.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But I think the challenge you just offered there still eludes us, right, the ability to make a decision based on those models quickly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: You know, I have to think, though, it's hard for humans to when you get that complicated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think probably you had maybe a slow motion version of where you learned the basic skills and you've probably gotten better at it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And there's much more subtlety, but it might still be hard to actually, you know, really on the fly, take a model of your humanoid and figure out how to plan the optimal sequence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: That might be a problem we never solve.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Well, I mean, one of the most amazing things to me about the—we can talk about martial arts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: We could also talk about dancing. It doesn't really matter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think it's the most interesting study of contact.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It's not even the dynamic element of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It's like when you get good at it, it's so effortless.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Like I can just—I'm very cognizant of the entirety of the learning process being essentially like learning how to move my body in a way that I could throw very large weights around effortlessly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And I can feel the learning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Like I'm a huge believer in drilling of techniques.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And you can just like feel your—I don't know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: You're not feeling—you're feeling—I'm sorry.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: You're learning it intellectually a little bit, but a lot of it is the body learning it somehow, like instinctually.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And whatever that learning is, that's really—I'm not even sure if that's equivalent to like a deep learning, learning a controller.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think it's something more—it feels like there's a lot of distributed learning going on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Yeah, I think there's hierarchy and composition probably in the systems that we don't capture very well yet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: You have layers of control systems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: You have reflexes at the bottom layer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: You have a system that's capable of planning a vacation to some distant country, which is probably—you probably don't have a controller, a policy for every possible destination you'll ever pick.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But there's something magical in the in-between.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And how do you go from these low-level feedback loops to something that feels like a pretty complex set of outcomes?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: My guess is I think there's evidence that you can plan at some of these levels.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So Josh Tenenbaum just showed us—he just talked the other day.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: He's got a game he likes to talk about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think he calls it the pick three game or something, where he puts a bunch of clutter down in front of a person.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And he says, okay, pick three objects.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And it might be a telephone or a shoe or a Kleenex box or whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And apparently you pick three items and then you pick—he says, okay, pick the first one up with your right hand, the second one up with your left hand.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Now, using those objects, those now as tools, pick up the third object.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Right. So that's down at the level of physics and mechanics and contact mechanics that I think we do learning—we do have policies for, we do control for almost feedback.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But somehow we're able to still—I mean, I've never picked up a telephone with a shoe and a water bottle before.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And somehow—and it takes me a little longer to do that the first time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But most of the time we can sort of figure that out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So yeah, I think the amazing thing is this ability to be flexible with our models, plan when we need to, use our well-oiled controllers when we don't, when we're in familiar territory.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Having models, I think the other thing you just said was something about I think your awareness of what's happening is even changing as you improve your expertise.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So maybe you have a very approximate model of the mechanics to begin with.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And as you gain expertise, you get a more refined version of that model.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: You're aware of muscles or balance components that you just weren't even aware of before.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So how do you scaffold that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Yeah, plus the fear of injury, the ambition of goals of excelling, and fear of mortality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Let's see what else is in there as the motivations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Overinflated ego in the beginning, and then a crash of confidence in the middle.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: All of those seem to be essential for the learning process.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And if all that's good, then you're probably optimizing energy efficiency.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Yeah, right. So we have to get that right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So there was this idea that you would have robots play soccer better than human players by 2050.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: That was the goal. Basically, was the goal to beat a world champion team, to become a World Cup, beat like a World Cup level team?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So are we going to see that first or a robot? If you're familiar, there's an organization called UFC for mixed martial arts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Are we going to see a World Cup championship soccer team that have robots or a UFC champion mixed martial artist?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: That's a robot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I mean, it's very hard to say one thing is harder than one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Some problems harder than the other. What probably matters is who started the organization.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I mean, I think RoboCup has a pretty serious following, and there is a history now of people playing that game,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: learning about that game, building robots to play that game, building increasingly more human robots.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It's got momentum. So if you want to have mixed martial arts compete, you better start your organization now, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think almost independent of which problem is technically harder because they're both hard and they're both different.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: That's a good point. I mean, those videos are just hilarious.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Especially the humanoid robots trying to play soccer. I mean, they're kind of terrible right now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I mean, I guess there is RoboSumo wrestling.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: There's like the Robo One competitions where they do have these robots that go on the table and basically fight.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So maybe I'm wrong. Maybe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: First of all, do you have a year in mind for RoboCup? Just from a robotics perspective,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: seems like a super exciting possibility that like in the physical space. This is what's interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think the world is captivated. I think it's really exciting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It inspires a huge number of people when a machine beats a human at a game that humans are really damn good at.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So you're talking about chess and Go, but that's in the world of digital.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I don't think machines have beat humans at a game in the physical space yet, but that would be just.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Even soccer, right? I mean, as soon as there's contact or whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And there are some things that the robot will do better.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think if you really set yourself up to try to see, could robots win the game of soccer as the rules were written,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: the right thing for the robot to do is to play very differently than a human would play.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: You're not going to get the perfect soccer player robot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: You're going to get something that exploits the rules, exploits its super actuators,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: its super low bandwidth feedback loops or whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And it's going to play the game differently than you want it to play.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And I bet there's ways, I bet there's loopholes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: We saw that in the DARPA challenge that it's very hard to write a set of rules that someone can't find a way to exploit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Let me ask another ridiculous question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think this might be the last ridiculous question, but...

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I doubt it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I aspire to ask as many ridiculous questions of a brilliant MIT professor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: OK. I don't know if you've seen the black mirror.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It's funny. I never watched the episode.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I know when it happened, though, because I gave a talk to some MIT faculty one day on an unassuming Monday or whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I was telling them about the state of robotics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And I showed some video from Boston Dynamics of the quadruped spot at the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It was an early version of spot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And there was a look of horror that went across the room.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And I said, I've shown videos like this a lot of times. What happened?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And it turns out that this video, this black mirror episode, had changed the way people watched the videos I was putting out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: The way they see these kinds of robots.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So I talked to so many people who are just terrified because of that episode, probably, of these kinds of robots.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I almost want to say that you almost kind of like enjoy being terrified.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I don't even know what it is about human psychology that kind of imagine doomsday, the destruction of the universe or our society and kind of like enjoy being afraid.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I don't want to simplify it, but it feels like they talk about it so often.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It almost there does seem to be an addictive quality to it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I talked to a guy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So there's a guy named Joe Rogan, who's kind of the flag bearer for being terrified of these robots.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Do you have a two questions?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: One, do you have an understanding of why people are afraid of robots?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And the second question is in black mirror, just to tell you the episode, I don't even remember it that much anymore.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But these robots, I think they can shoot like a pellet or something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: They basically have. It's basically a spot with a gun.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And how far are we away from having robots that go rogue like that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: You know, basically spot that goes rogue for some reason and somehow finds a cut.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Right. So.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I mean, I'm not a psychologist.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think I don't know exactly why people react the way they do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think I think we have to be careful about the way robots influence our society and the like.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think that's something that's a responsibility that roboticists need to embrace.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I don't think robots are going to come after me with a kitchen knife or a pellet gun right away.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And I mean, they if they were programmed in such a way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But I used to joke with Atlas that all I had to do was run for five minutes and its battery would run out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But actually, they've got a very big battery in there by the end.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So it was over an hour.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think the fear is a bit cultural, though, because I mean, you notice that like I think in my age in the US, we grew up watching Terminator.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Right. If I had grown up at the same time in Japan, I probably would have been watching Astro Boy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And there's a very different reaction to robots in different countries.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Right. So I don't know if it's a human innate fear of metal marvels or if it's something that we've done to ourselves with our sci fi.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And the stories we tell ourselves through through movies, through just through popular media.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But if I were to tell you know, if you were my therapist and I said, I'm really terrified that we're going to have these robots very soon, that will hurt us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Like, how do you approach making me feel better?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Like, why shouldn't people be afraid?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: There's a I think there's a video that went viral recently.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Everything everything was spot in Boston, which goes viral in general.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But usually it's like really cool stuff like they're doing flips and stuff or like sad stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Be Atlas being hit with a broomstick or something like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But there's a video where I think one of the new productions bought robots, which are awesome.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It was like patrolling somewhere and like in some country and like people immediately were like saying like this is like the dystopian future, like the surveillance state for some reason.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Like you can just have a camera like something about spot being able to walk on four feet with like really terrified people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So what what do you say to those people?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think there is a legitimate fear there because so much of our future is uncertain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But at the same time, technically speaking, it seems like we're not there yet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So what do you say?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I mean, I think technology is complicated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It can be used in many ways. I think there are purely software.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Attacks somebody could use to do great damage. Maybe they have already.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think wheeled robots could be used in bad ways to drones.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I don't think that. Let's see.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I don't want to be building technology just because I'm compelled to build technology and I don't think about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But I would consider myself a technological optimist, I guess, in the sense that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think we should continue to create and evolve and our world will change.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And if we will introduce new challenges, we'll screw something up maybe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But I think also we'll invent ourselves out of those challenges and life will go on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So it's interesting because you didn't mention like this is technically too hard.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I don't think robots are I think people attribute a robot that looks like an animal as maybe having a level of self-awareness or consciousness or something that they don't have yet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Right. So it's not I think our ability to anthropomorphize those robots is probably we're assuming that they have a level of intelligence that they don't yet have.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And that might be part of the fear. So in that sense, it's too hard.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But, you know, there are many scary things in the world. Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So I think we're right to ask those questions. We're right to think about the implications of our work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Right. In the in the short term, as we're working on it for sure, is there something long term that scares you about our future with AI and robots?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: A lot of folks from Elon Musk to Sam Harris to a lot of folks talk about the existential threats about artificial intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Oftentimes, robots kind of inspire that the most because of the anthropomorphism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Do you have any fears? It's an important question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I actually I think I like Rod Brooks answer, maybe the best on this, I think.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And it's not the only answer he's given over the years, but maybe one of my favorites is he says it's not going to be he's got a book, Flesh and Machines, I believe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It's not going to be the robots versus the people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: We're all going to be robot people because, you know, we already have smartphones.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Some of us have serious technology implanted in our bodies already, whether we have a hearing aid or a pacemaker or anything like this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: People with amputations might have prosthetics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: That's a trend, I think, that is likely to continue.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I mean, this is now wild speculation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But I mean, when do we get to cognitive implants and the like?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Yeah, with neurolink brain computer interfaces.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: That's interesting. So there's a there's a dance between humans and robots.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It's going to be it's going to be impossible to be scared of the other out there, the robot, because the robot will be part of us, essentially.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It'd be so intricately sort of part of our society that it might not even be implanted part of us, but just it's so much of part of our.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Yeah, our society. So in that sense, the smartphone is already the robot we should be afraid of.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Yeah. I mean, yeah. And all the usual fears arise of the misinformation, the manipulation, all those kinds of things that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: That the problems are all the same.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: They're all they're human problems, essentially.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It feels like, yeah, I mean, I think the the way we interact with each other online is changing the value we put on, you know, personal interaction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And that's a crazy big change that's going to happen and rip through our has already been ripping through our society.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Right. And that has implications that are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Massive, I don't know if they should be scared of it or go with the flow, but I don't see some battle lines between humans and robots being.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: The first thing to worry about. I mean, I do want to just as a kind of comment, maybe you can comment about your just feelings about Boston Dynamics in general.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But, you know, I love science. I love engineering. I think there's so many beautiful ideas in it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And when I look at Boston Dynamics or legged robots in general, I think they inspire people curiosity and feelings in general excitement about engineering more than almost anything else in popular culture.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And I think that's such an exciting possibility, like responsibility and possibility for robotics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And Boston Dynamics is riding that wave pretty damn well. Like they found it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: They've discovered that hunger and curiosity in the people and they're doing magic with it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I don't care if that I mean, I guess is that their company have to make money. Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But they're already doing incredible work and inspiring the world about technology.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I mean, do you have thoughts about Boston Dynamics and maybe others, your own work in robotics and inspiring the world in that way?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I completely agree. I think Boston Dynamics is absolutely awesome.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think I show my kids those videos, you know, and the best thing that happens is sometimes they've already seen them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: You know, right. I think I just think it's a pinnacle of success in robotics that is just one of the best things that's happened.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I absolutely completely agree.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: One of the heartbreaking things to me is how many robotics companies fail, how hard it is to make money with the robotics company.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Like I robot like went through hell just to arrive at a Roomba to figure out one product.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And then there's so many home robotics companies like Jibo and Anki Anki, the cutest toy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: That's a great robot. I thought went down. I'm forgetting a bunch of them, but a bunch of robotics companies fail.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Rod's company, Rethink Robotics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Like, do you do you have anything anything hopeful to say about the possibility of making money with robots?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Oh, I think you can't just look at the failures you can.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I mean, Boston Dynamics is a success.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: There's lots of companies that are still doing amazingly good work in robotics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I mean, this is the this is the capitalist ecology or something, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think you have many companies, you have many startups and they push each other forward and many of them fail and some of them get through.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And that's sort of the natural way of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: The way of those things. I don't know that is robotics really that much worse?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I feel the pain that you feel too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Every time I read one of these, I sometimes it's friends and I definitely wish it went better, would differently.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But I think it's healthy and good to have bursts of ideas, bursts of activities, ideas.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: If they are really aggressive, they should fail sometimes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Certainly, that's the research mantra, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: If you're succeeding at every problem you attempt, then you're not choosing aggressively enough.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Is it exciting to you?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: The new spot? Oh, it's so good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: When are you getting them as a pet?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Yeah, I mean, I have to dig up 75k right now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I mean, it's so cool that there's a price tag you can go and then actually buy it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I have a Skydio R1. Love it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So, no, I would I would I would absolutely be a customer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I wonder what your kids would think about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I actually Zach from Boston Dynamics would let my kid drive in one of their demos one time and that was just so good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So good. And again, forever be grateful for that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And there's something magical about the anthropomorphization of that arm.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It has another level of human connection.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I'm not sure we understand from a control aspect the value of anthropomorphization.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think that's an understudied and under understood engineering problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: There's been a psychologist, a psychologist have been studying it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think it's part like manipulating our mind to believe things is a valuable engineering.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Like this is another degree of freedom that could be controlled.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I like that. Yeah, I think that's right. I think.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: You know, there's something that humans seem to do or maybe my dangerous introspection is

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think we are able to make very simple models that assume a lot about the world very quickly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And then it takes us a lot more time like you're wrestling.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: You know, you probably thought you knew what you're doing with wrestling and you were fairly functional as a complete wrestler.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And then you slowly got more expertise.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So maybe it's natural that our first first level of defense against seeing a new robot is to think of it in our existing models of how humans and animals behave.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And it's just as you spend more time with it, then you'll develop more sophisticated models that will appreciate the differences.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Exactly. Can you say what does it take to control a robot?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Like what is the control problem of a robot?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And in general, what is a robot in your view? Like how do you think of this system?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: What is a robot? What is a robot? I think I think it's ridiculous questions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: No, no, it's good. I mean, there's standard definitions of combining computation with some ability to do mechanical work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think that gets us pretty close.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But I think robotics has this problem that once things really work, we don't call them robots anymore.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Like my dishwasher at home is pretty sophisticated, beautiful mechanisms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: There's actually a pretty good computer, probably a couple of chips in there doing amazing things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: We don't think of that as a robot anymore, which isn't fair because then what roughly it means the robots robotics always has to solve the next problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And it doesn't get to celebrate its past successes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I mean, even factory room floor robots are super successful. They're amazing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But that's not the ones I mean, people think of them as robots, but they don't.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: If you ask what are the successes of robotics, somehow it doesn't come to your mind immediately.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So the definition of robot is a system with some level of automation that fails frequently.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It's the computation plus mechanical work and unsolved problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So from a perspective of control and mechanics, dynamics, what is a robot?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So there are many different types of robots.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: The control that you need for a Jibo robot, some robot that's sitting on your countertop and interacting with you, but not touching you, for instance,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: is very different than what you need for an autonomous car or an autonomous drone.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It's very different than what you need for a robot that's going to walk or pick things up with its hands.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: My passion has always been for the places where you're doing more dynamic interactions with the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So walking, now manipulation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And the control problems there are beautiful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think contact is one thing that differentiates them from many of the control problems we've solved classically.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Modern control grew up stabilizing fighter jets that were passively unstable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And there's amazing success stories from control all over the place.
