metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Power grid, I mean, there's all kinds of it's everywhere that we don't even realize, just like AI is now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So you mentioned contact. What's contact?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So an airplane is an extremely complex system or a spacecraft landing or whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But at least it has the luxury of things change relatively continuously.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: That's an oversimplification.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But if I make a small change in the command I send to my actuator,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: then the path that the robot will take tends to take a change only by a small amount.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And there's a feedback mechanism here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: That's what we're talking about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And there's a feedback mechanism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And thinking about this as locally like a linear system, for instance,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I can use more linear algebra tools to study systems like that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: generalizations of linear algebra to these smooth systems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: What is contact?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: The robot has something very discontinuous that happens when it makes or breaks,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: when it starts touching the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And even the way it touches or the order of contacts can change the outcome in potentially unpredictable ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Not unpredictable, but complex ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I do think there's a little bit of a – a lot of people will say that contact is hard in robotics, even to simulate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And I think there's a little bit of a – there's truth to that, but maybe a misunderstanding around that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So what is limiting is that when we think about our robots and we write our simulators,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: we often make an assumption that objects are rigid.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And when it comes down that their mass moves, stays in a constant position relative to each other itself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And that leads to some paradoxes when you go to try to talk about rigid body mechanics and contact.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And so for instance, if I have a three-legged stool with just – imagine it comes to a point at the leg.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So it's only touching the world at a point.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: If I draw my physics – my high school physics diagram of the system,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: then there's a couple of things that I'm given by elementary physics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I know if the system – if the table is at rest, if it's not moving, zero velocities,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: that means that the normal force – all the forces are in balance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So the force of gravity is being countered by the forces that the ground is pushing on my table legs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I also know since it's not rotating that the moments have to balance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And since it can – it's a three-dimensional table, it could fall in any direction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It actually tells me uniquely what those three normal forces have to be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: If I have four legs on my table, four-legged table,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and they were perfectly machined to be exactly the right same height,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and they're set down and the table's not moving,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: then the basic conservation laws don't tell me there are many solutions for the forces that the ground could be putting on my legs

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: that would still result in the table not moving.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Now the reason that seems fine – I could just pick one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But it gets funny now because if you think about friction,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: what we think about with friction is our standard model says the amount of force that the table will push back,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: if I were to now try to push my table sideways – I guess I have a table here – is proportional to the normal force.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So if I'm barely touching and I push, I'll slide.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But if I'm pushing more and I push, I'll slide less.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It's called Coulomb friction. It's our standard model.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Now if you don't know what the normal force is on the four legs and you push the table,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: then you don't know what the friction forces are going to be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And so you can't actually tell.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: The laws just aren't explicit yet about which way the table is going to go.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It could veer off to the left. It could veer off to the right. It could go straight.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So the rigid body assumption of contact leaves us with some paradoxes, which are annoying,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: for writing simulators and for writing controllers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: We still do that sometimes because soft contact is potentially harder numerically or whatever,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and the best simulators do both or do some combination of the two.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But anyways, because of these kind of paradoxes – there's all kinds of paradoxes in contact,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: mostly due to these rigid body assumptions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It becomes very hard to write the same kind of control laws that we've been able to be successful with

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: for fighter jets. We haven't been as successful writing those controllers for manipulation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So you don't know what's going to happen at the point of contact, at the moment of contact.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: There are situations absolutely where our laws don't tell us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So the standard approach, that's okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Instead of having a differential equation, you end up with a differential inclusion, it's called.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It's a set-valued equation. It says that I'm in this configuration. I have these forces applied on me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And there's a set of things that could happen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And those aren't continuous? I mean, what – so when you're saying non-smooth,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: they're not only not smooth, but this is discontinuous?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Non-smooth comes in when I make or break a new contact first, or when I transition from stick to slip.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So you typically have static friction, and then you'll start sliding,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and that'll be a discontinuous change in velocity, for instance, especially if you come to rest.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: That's so fascinating. Okay, so what do you do? Sorry, I interrupted you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: What's the hope under so much uncertainty about what's going to happen? What are you supposed to do?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I mean, control has an answer for this. Robust control is one approach.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But roughly, you can write controllers which try to still perform the right task,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: despite all the things that could possibly happen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: The world might want the table to go this way and this way, but if I write a controller that pushes a little bit more,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and pushes a little bit – I can certainly make the table go in the direction I want.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It just puts a little bit more of a burden on the control system, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And these discontinuities do change the control system because the way we write it down right now,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: every different control configuration, including sticking or sliding, or parts of my body that are in contact or not,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: looks like a different system. And I think of them – I reason about them separately or differently,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and the combinatorics of that blow up, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So I just don't have enough time to compute all the possible contact configurations of my humanoid.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Interestingly, I mean, I'm a humanoid. I have lots of degrees of freedom, lots of joints.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I've only been around for a handful of years. It's getting up there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But I haven't had time in my life to visit all of the states in my system,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: certainly all the contact configurations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So if step one is to consider every possible contact configuration that I'll ever be in,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: that's probably not a problem I need to solve, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Just as a small tangent, what's a contact configuration?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Just so we can enumerate, what are we talking about? How many are there?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: The simplest example maybe would be imagine a robot with a flat foot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And we think about the phases of gait where the heel strikes, and then the front toe strikes,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and then you can heel up, toe off. Those are each different contact configurations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I only had two different contacts, but I ended up with four different contact configurations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Now, of course, my robot might actually have bumps on it or other things,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: so it could be much more subtle than that, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But it's just even with one sort of box interacting with the ground already in the plane, has that many, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And if I was just even a 3D foot, then probably my left toe might touch just before my right toe, and things get subtle.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Now, if I'm a dextrous hand and I go to talk about just grabbing a water bottle,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: if I have to enumerate every possible order that my hand came into contact with the bottle,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: then I'm dead in the water. Any approach that we were able to get away with that in walking,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: because we mostly touched the ground with a small number of points, for instance,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and we haven't been able to get dextrous hands that way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So, you've mentioned that people think that contact is really hard,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and that that's the reason that robotic manipulation is problem is really hard.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Is there any flaws in that thinking?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So, I think simulating contact is one aspect.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I know people often say that one of the reasons that we have a limit in robotics

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: is because we do not simulate contact accurately in our simulators.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And I think that is, the extent to which that's true is partly because our simulators,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: we haven't got mature enough simulators.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: There are some things that are still hard, difficult, that we should change.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But we actually, we know what the governing equations are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: They have some foibles like this indeterminacy, but we should be able to simulate them accurately.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: We have incredible open source community in robotics,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: but it actually just takes a professional engineering team a lot of work

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: to write a very good simulator like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Now, where does, I believe you've written, Drake?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: There's a team of people. I certainly spent a lot of hours on it myself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Well, what is Drake, and what does it take to create a simulation environment

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: for the kind of difficult control problems we're talking about?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Right, so Drake is the simulator that I've been working on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: There are other good simulators out there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I don't like to think of Drake as just a simulator,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: because we write our controllers in Drake, we write our perception systems a little bit in Drake,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: but we write all of our low-level control and even planning and optimization.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So it has optimization capabilities.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Absolutely, yeah. I mean, Drake is three things, roughly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It's an optimization library, which is, sits on, it provides a layer of abstraction in C++ and Python.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: For commercial solvers, you can write linear programs, quadratic programs,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: semi-definite programs, sums of squares programs, the ones we've used, mixed integer programs,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and it will do the work to curate those and send them to whatever the right solver is, for instance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It provides a level of abstraction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: The second thing is a system modeling language, a bit like LabView or Simulink,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: where you can make block diagrams out of complex systems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Or it's like ROS in that sense, where you might have lots of ROS nodes that are each doing some part of your system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But to contrast it with ROS, we try to write, if you write a Drake system,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: then you have to, it asks you to describe a little bit more about the system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: If you have any state, for instance, in the system, any variables that are going to persist, you have to declare them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Parameters can be declared and the like.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But the advantage of doing that is that you can, if you like, run things all on one process,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: but you can also do control design against it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: You can do simple things like rewinding and playing back your simulations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: For instance, you get some rewards for spending a little bit more upfront cost in describing each system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And I was inspired to do that because I think the complexity of Atlas, for instance, is just so great.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And I think although, I mean, ROS has been an incredible, absolute huge fan of what it's done for the robotics community.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But the ability to rapidly put different pieces together and have a functioning thing is very good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But I do think that it's hard to think clearly about a bag of disparate parts, Mr. Potato Head kind of software stack.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And if you can ask a little bit more out of each of those parts, then you can understand the way they work better.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: You can try to verify them and the like.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: You can do learning against them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And then one of those systems, the last thing, I said the first two things that Drake is,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: but the last thing is that there is a set of multi-body equations, rigid body equations,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: that is trying to provide a system that simulates physics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And we also have renderers and other things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But I think the physics component of Drake is special in the sense that we have done excessive amount of engineering

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: to make sure that we've written the equations correctly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So basically every possible tumbling satellite or spinning top or anything that we could possibly write as a test is tested.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: We are making some, I think, fundamental improvements on the way you simulate contact.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: What does it take to simulate contact?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I mean, it just seems, I mean, there's something just beautiful the way you were explaining contact

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: or tapping your fingers on the table while you're doing it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Easily, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Easily. Just like, just not even like, it was like helping you think, I guess.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: You have this awesome demo of loading or unloading a dishwasher, just picking up a plate,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: grasping it like for the first time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: That just seems like so difficult.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: What, how do you simulate any of that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So it was really interesting that what happened was that we started getting more professional about our software development

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: during the DARPA Robotics Challenge.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I learned the value of software engineering and how these, how to bridle complexity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I guess that's what I want to somehow fight against and bring some of the clear thinking of controls

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: into these complex systems we're building for robots.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Shortly after the DARPA Robotics Challenge, Toyota opened a research institute, TRI, Toyota Research Institute.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: They put one of their, there's three locations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: One of them is just down the street from MIT.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And I helped ramp that up right as a part of my, the end of my sabbatical, I guess.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So TRI is, has given me the TRI Robotics effort, has made this investment in simulation in Drake.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And Michael Sherman leads a team there of just absolutely top notch dynamics experts

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: that are trying to write those simulators that can pick up the dishes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And there's also a team working on manipulation there that is taking problems like loading the dishwasher.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And we're using that to study these really hard corner cases kind of problems in manipulation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So for me, this, you know, simulating the dishes, we could actually write a controller.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: If we just cared about picking up dishes in the sink once, we could write a controller without any simulation whatsoever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And we could call it done.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But we want to understand like what is the path you take to actually get to a robot that could perform that for any dish

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: in anybody's kitchen with enough confidence that it could be a commercial product, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And it has deep learning perception in the loop.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It has complex dynamics in the loop.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It has controller. It has a planner.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: How do you take all of that complexity and put it through this engineering discipline and verification and validation process

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: to actually get enough confidence to deploy?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I mean, the DARPA challenge made me realize that that's not something you throw over the fence

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and hope that somebody will harden it for you, that there are really fundamental challenges in closing that last gap.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: During the validation and the testing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think it might even change the way we have to think about the way we write systems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: What happens if you have the robot running lots of tests and it screws up, it breaks a dish, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: How do you capture that? I said you can't run the same simulation or the same experiment twice on a real robot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Do we have to be able to bring that one-off failure back into simulation in order to change our controllers, study it, make sure it won't happen again?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Is it enough to just try to add that to our distribution and understand that on average we're going to cover that situation again?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: There's like really subtle questions at the corner cases that I think we don't yet have satisfying answers for.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: How do you find the corner cases? Do you think it's possible to create a systematized way of discovering corner cases efficiently?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: In whatever the problem is?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Yes. I mean, I think we have to get better at that. Control theory has for decades talked about active experiment design.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: What's that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: People call it curiosity these days. It's roughly this idea of trying to exploration or exploitation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But in the active experiment design is even more specific.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: You could try to understand the uncertainty in your system, design the experiment that will provide the maximum information to reduce that uncertainty.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: If there's a parameter you want to learn about, what is the optimal trajectory I could execute to learn about that parameter, for instance?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Scaling that up to something that has a deep network in the loop and a planning in the loop is tough.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: We've done some work with Matt O'Kelly and Amman Sinha.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: We've worked on some falsification algorithms that are trying to do rare event simulation that try to just hammer on your simulator.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: If your simulator is good enough, you can write good algorithms that try to spend most of their time in the corner cases.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: You basically imagine you're building an autonomous car and you want to put it in downtown New Delhi all the time, right, and accelerated testing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: If you can write sampling strategies which figure out where your controller is performing badly in simulation and start generating lots of examples around that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It's just the space of possible places where things can go wrong is very big. So it's hard to write those algorithms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Yeah, rare event simulation is just a really compelling notion. If it's possible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: We joked and we call it the black swan generator.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: The black swan.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Because you don't just want the rare events, you want the ones that are highly impactful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Those are the most profound questions we ask of our world. What's the worst that can happen?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But what we're really asking isn't some kind of computer science, worst case analysis.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: We're asking what are the millions of ways this can go wrong? And that's our curiosity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: We humans, I think, are pretty bad at... we just run into it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And I think there's a distributed sense because there's now 7.5 billion of us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And so there's a lot of them and then a lot of them write blog posts about the stupid thing they've done.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So we learn in a distributed way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think that's going to be important for robots too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: That's another massive theme at Toyota Research for robotics is this fleet learning concept.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: The idea that I as a human I don't have enough time to visit all of my states.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It's very hard for one robot to experience all the things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But that's not actually the problem we have to solve.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: We're going to have fleets of robots that can have very similar appendages.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And at some point, maybe collectively, they have enough data that their computational processes should be set up differently than ours.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It's this vision of just... I mean all these dishwasher unloading robots.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I mean that robot dropping a plate and a human looking at the robot probably pissed off.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But that's a special moment to record.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think one thing in terms of fleet learning, and I've seen that because I've talked to a lot of folks just like Tesla users or Tesla drivers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: They're another company that's using this kind of fleet learning idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: One hopeful thing I have about humans is they really enjoy when a system improves, learns.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So they enjoy fleet learning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And the reason it's hopeful for me is they're willing to put up with something that's kind of dumb right now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And they're like, if it's improving, they almost like enjoy being part of the... like teaching it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Almost like if you have kids, like you're teaching them something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think that's a beautiful thing because that gives me hope that we can put dumb robots out there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I mean the problem on the Tesla side with cars, cars can kill you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: That makes the problem so much harder.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Dishwasher unloading is a little safe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: That's why home robotics is really exciting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And just to clarify, I mean for people who might not know, I mean TRI, Toyota Research Institute.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So they're pretty well known for like autonomous vehicle research.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But they're also interested in home robotics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Yep. There's a big group working on... multiple groups working on home robotics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It's a major part of the portfolio.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: There's also a couple other projects, advanced materials discovery,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: using AI and machine learning to discover new materials for car batteries and the like, for instance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And that's been actually an incredibly successful team.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: There's new projects starting up too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Do you see a future of where like robots are in our home?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And like robots that have actuators that look like arms in our home?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Or like, you know, more like humanoid type robots?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Or is this... are we going to do the same thing that you just mentioned that, you know, the dishwasher is no longer a robot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: We're going to just not even see them as robots.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But I mean, what's your vision of the home of the future?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: 10, 20 years from now, 50 years if you get crazy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Yeah, I think we already have Roombas cruising around.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: We have, you know, Alexa's or Google Homes on our kitchen counter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It's only a matter of time till they spring arms and start doing something useful like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So I do think it's coming.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think lots of people have lots of motivations for doing it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It's been super interesting actually learning about Toyota's vision for it, which is about helping people age in place.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Because I think that's not necessarily the first entry, the most lucrative entry point.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But it's the problem maybe that we really need to solve no matter what.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And so I think there's a real opportunity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It's a delicate problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: How do you work with people, help people, keep them active, engaged, you know, but improve their quality of life and help them age in place, for instance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It's interesting because older folks are also...

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I mean, there's a contrast there because they're not always the folks who are the most comfortable with technology, for example.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So there's a division that's interesting there that you can do so much good with a robot for older folks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But there's a gap to fill of understanding.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I mean, it's actually kind of beautiful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Robot is learning about the human and the human is kind of learning about this new robot thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And it's also with...

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: At least with...

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Like when I talk to my parents about robots, there's a little bit of a blank slate there too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Like you can...

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I mean, they don't know anything about robotics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So it's completely like wide open.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: They don't have...

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: My parents haven't seen Black Mirror.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So like it's a blank slate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Here's a cool thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Like, what can you do for me?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So it's an exciting space.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think it's a really important space.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I do feel like, you know, a few years ago, drones were successful enough in academia.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: They kind of broke out and started an industry and autonomous cars have been happening.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It does feel like manipulation in logistics, of course, first, but in the home shortly after seems like one of the next big things that's going to really pop.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So I don't think we talked about it, but what's soft robotics?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: We talked about like rigid bodies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: If we can just linger on this whole touch thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Yeah. So what's soft robotics?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So I told you that I really dislike the fact that robots are afraid of touching the world all over their body.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So there's a couple of reasons for that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: If you look carefully at all the places that robots actually do touch the world, they're almost always soft.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: They have some sort of pad on their fingers or a rubber sole on their foot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But if you look up and down the arm, we're just pure aluminum or something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So that makes it hard, actually.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: In fact, hitting the table with your, you know, your rigid arm or nearly rigid arm is a has some of the problems that we talked about in terms of simulation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think it fundamentally changes the mechanics of contact when you're soft.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: You turn point contacts into patch contacts, which can have torsional friction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: You can have distributed load.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: If I want to pick up an egg, right, if I pick it up with two points, then in order to put enough force to sustain the weight of the egg, I might have to put a lot of force to break the egg.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: If I envelop it with contact all around, then I can distribute my force across the shell of the egg and have a better chance of not breaking it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So soft robotics is for me a lot about changing the mechanics of contact.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Does it make the problem a lot harder?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Quite the opposite.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It changes the computational problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think because of the, I think our world and our mathematics has biased us towards rigid, but it really should make things better in some ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It's a, I think the future is unwritten there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But the other thing is, sorry to interrupt, but you think ultimately it will make things simpler if we embrace the softness of the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It makes things smoother, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So the result of small actions is less discontinuous, but it also means potentially less, you know, instantaneously bad, for instance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I won't necessarily contact something and send it flying off.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: The other aspect of it that just happens to dovetail really well is that soft robotics tends to be a place where we can embed a lot of sensors too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So if you change your hardware and make it more soft, then you can potentially have a tactile sensor, which is measuring the deformation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So there's a team at TRI that's working on soft hands and you get so much more information.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: You can put a camera behind the skin roughly and get fantastic tactile information, which is super important.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Like in manipulation, one of the things that really is frustrating is if you work super hard on your head mounted, on your perception system for your head mounted cameras,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and then you've identified an object, you reach down to touch it, and the first, the last thing that happens right before the most important time,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: you stick your hand and you're occluding your head mounted sensors, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So in all the part that really matters, all of your off-board sensors are occluded.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And really, if you don't have tactile information, then you're blind in an important way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So it happens that soft robotics and tactile sensing tend to go hand in hand.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think we've kind of talked about it, but you taught a course on underactuated robotics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I believe that was the name of it, actually.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Can you talk about it in that context? What is underactuated robotics?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Right. So underactuated robotics is my graduate course. It's online mostly now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I mean, in the sense that the lectures are the versions of it, I think.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Right. The YouTube really great. I recommend it highly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Look on YouTube for the 2020 versions until March, and then you have to go back to 2019.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Thanks to COVID. No, I've poured my heart into that class.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And lecture one is basically explaining what the word underactuated means.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So people are very kind to show up and then maybe have to learn what the title of the course means

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: over the course of the first lecture.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: That first lecture is really good. You should watch it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Thanks. It's a strange name, but I thought it captured the essence of what control was good at doing

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and what control was bad at doing. So what do I mean by underactuated?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So a mechanical system has many degrees of freedom, for instance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think of a joint as a degree of freedom, and it has some number of actuators, motors.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So if you have a robot that's bolted to the table that has five degrees of freedom and five motors,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: then you have a fully actuated robot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: If you take away one of those motors, then you have an underactuated robot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Now, why on earth? I have a good friend who likes to tease me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: He said, Russ, if you had more research funding, would you work on fully actuated robots?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And the answer is no. The world gives us underactuated robots, whether we like it or not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I'm a human. I'm an underactuated robot, even though I have more muscles than my big degrees of freedom,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: because I have in some places multiple muscles attached to the same joint.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But still, there's a really important degree of freedom that I have,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: which is the location of my center of mass in space, for instance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I can jump into the air, and there's no motor that connects my center of mass to the ground in that case.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So I have to think about the implications of not having control over everything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: The passive dynamic walkers are the extreme view of that, where you've taken away all the motors,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and you have to let physics do the work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But it shows up in all of the walking robots, where you have to use some of the actuators

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: to push and pull even the degrees of freedom that you don't have an actuator on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: That's referring to walking if you're like falling forward.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Is there a way to walk that's fully actuated?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So it's a subtle point. When you're in contact and you have your feet on the ground,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: there are still limits to what you can do, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Unless I have suction cups on my feet, I cannot accelerate my center of mass towards the ground faster than gravity,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: because I can't get a force pushing me down.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But I can still do most of the things that I want to.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So you can get away with basically thinking of the system as fully actuated

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: unless you suddenly needed to accelerate down super fast.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But as soon as I take a step, I get into more nuanced territory.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And to get to really dynamic robots or airplanes or other things,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think you have to embrace the under-actuated dynamics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Manipulation, people think is manipulation under-actuated?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Even if my arm is fully actuated, I have a motor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: If my goal is to control the position and orientation of this cup,
