metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: then I don't have an actuator for that directly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So I have to use my actuators over here to control this thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Now it gets even worse. Like what if I have to button my shirt?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: What are the degrees of freedom of my shirt?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: That's a hard question to think about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It kind of makes me queasy thinking about my state space control ideas.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But actually those are the problems that make me so excited about manipulation right now,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: is that it breaks a lot of the foundational control stuff that I've been thinking about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: What are some interesting insights you could say about trying to solve

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: under-actuated control in an under-actuated system?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So I think the philosophy there is let physics do more of the work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: The technical approach has been optimization.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So you typically formulate your decision-making for control as an optimization problem,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and you use the language of optimal control, and sometimes often numerical optimal control,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: in order to make those decisions and balance these complicated equations in order to control.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: You don't have to use optimal control to do under-actuated systems,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: but that has been the technical approach that has borne the most fruit in our, at least in our line of work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And there's some, so in under-actuated systems when you say let physics do some of the work,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: so there's a kind of feedback loop that observes the state that the physics brought you to.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So like you've, there's a perception there, there's a feedback somehow.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Do you ever loop in like complicated perception systems into this whole picture?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Right. Right around the time of the DARPA challenge,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: we had a complicated perception system in the DARPA challenge.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: We also started to embrace perception for our flying vehicles at the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: We had a really good project on trying to make airplanes fly at high speeds through forests.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Surtosh Karaman was on that project, and it was a really fun team to work on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: He's carried it farther, much farther forward since then.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And that's using cameras for perception?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So that was using cameras.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: That was, at the time we felt like LiDAR was too heavy and too power heavy to be carried on a light UAV,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: and we were using cameras.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And that was a big part of it, was just how do you do even stereo matching at a fast enough rate with a small camera, a small onboard compute.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Since then, we have now, so the deep learning revolution unquestionably changed what we can do with perception for robotics and control.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So in manipulation, we can address, we can use perception in, I think, a much deeper way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And we get into not only, I think the first use of it naturally would be to ask your deep learning system to look at the cameras and produce the state,

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: which is like the pose of my thing, for instance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But I think we've quickly found out that that's not always the right thing to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Why is that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Because what's the state of my shirt? Imagine I've...

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Is it very noisy, you mean?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: If the first step of me trying to button my shirt is estimate the full state of my shirt, including like what's happening in the back here or whatever, whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: That's just not the right specification.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: There are aspects of the state that are very important to the task.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: There are many that are unobservable and not important to the task.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So you really need, it begs new questions about state representation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Another example that we've been playing with in lab has been just the idea of chopping onions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Or carrots, turns out to be better.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So onions stink up the lab and they're hard to see in a camera.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But...

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: The details matter, yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Details matter, you know?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So if I'm moving around a particular object, right, then I think about, oh, it's got a position or an orientation in space.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: That's the description I want.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Now, when I'm chopping an onion, okay, the first chop comes down.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I have now 100 pieces of onion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Does my control system really need to understand the position and orientation and even the shape of the 100 pieces of onion in order to make a decision?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Probably not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And if I keep going, I'm just getting more and more, is my state space getting bigger as I cut?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It's not right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So I think there's a richer idea of state.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It's not the state that is given to us by Lagrangian mechanics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: There is a proper Lagrangian state of the system, but the relevant state for this is some latent state is what we call it in machine learning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But, you know, there's some different state representation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Some compressed representation?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And that's what I worry about saying compressed because it doesn't...

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I don't mind that it's low dimensional or not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But it has to be something that's easier to think about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: By us humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Or my algorithms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Or the algorithms being like control, optimal control.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So, for instance, if the contact mechanics of all of those onion pieces and all the permutations of possible touches between those onion pieces, you know, you can give me a high dimensional state representation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I'm okay if it's linear.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: But if I think about all the possible shattering combinatorics of that, then my robot's going to sit there thinking and the soup's going to get cold or something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: So since you taught the course, it kind of entered my mind, the idea of underactuated as really compelling to see the world in this kind of way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Do you ever, you know, if you talk about onions or you talk about the world with people in it in general, do you see the world as basically an underactuated system?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Do you like often look at the world in this way?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Or is this overreach?

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Underactuated as a way of life, man.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Exactly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I guess that's what I'm asking.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I do think it's everywhere.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I think in some places we already have natural tools to deal with it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: You know, it rears its head.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: I mean, in linear systems, it's not a problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: We just, like an underactuated linear system is really not sufficiently distinct from a fully actuated linear system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It's a subtle point about when that becomes a bottleneck in what we know how to do with control.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: It happens to be a bottleneck.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: Although we've gotten incredibly good solutions now, but for a long time that I felt that that was the key bottleneck in legged robots.

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

metadata.title: Podcast: Russ Tedrake: Underactuated Robotics, Control, Dynamics and Touch | Lex Fridman Podcast #114

body.input: And now here's my conversation with Melanie Mitchell.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: The name of your new book is Artificial Intelligence,

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: subtitle, A Guide for Thinking Humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: The name of this podcast is Artificial Intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: So let me take a step back

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: and ask the old Shakespeare question about roses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: And what do you think of the term artificial intelligence

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: for our big and complicated and interesting field?

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: I'm not crazy about the term.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: I think it has a few problems

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: because it means so many different things

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: to different people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: And intelligence is one of those words

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: that isn't very clearly defined either.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: There's so many different kinds of intelligence,

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: degrees of intelligence, approaches to intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: John McCarthy was the one who came up with the term

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: artificial intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: And from what I read, he called it that

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: to differentiate it from cybernetics,

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: which was another related movement at the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: And he later regretted calling it artificial intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: Herbert Simon was pushing for calling it

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: complex information processing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: which got mixed, but probably is equally vague, I guess.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: Is it the intelligence or the artificial

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: in terms of words that is most problematic, would you say?

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: Yeah, I think it's a little of both.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: But it has some good size because I personally

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: was attracted to the field because I was interested

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: in phenomenon of intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: And if it was called complex information processing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: maybe I'd be doing something wholly different now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: What do you think of, I've heard that term used,

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: cognitive systems, for example, so using cognitive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: Yeah, I mean, cognitive has certain associations with it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: And people like to separate things like cognition

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: and perception, which I don't actually think are separate,

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: but often people talk about cognition as being different

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: from sort of other aspects of intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: It's sort of higher level.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: So to you, cognition is this broad, beautiful mess

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: of things that encompasses the whole thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: Memory, perception.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: I think it's hard to draw lines like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: When I was coming out of grad school in 1990,

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: which is when I graduated,

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: that was during one of the AI winters.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: And I was advised to not put AI, artificial intelligence,

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: on my CV, but instead call it intelligence systems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: So that was kind of a euphemism, I guess.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: What about to stick briefly on terms and words,

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: the idea of artificial general intelligence,

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: or like Jan LeCun prefers human level intelligence,

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: sort of starting to talk about ideas

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: that achieve higher and higher levels of intelligence

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: and somehow artificial intelligence seems to be a term

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: used more for the narrow, very specific applications of AI

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: and sort of what set of terms appeal to you

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: to describe the thing that perhaps we strive to create.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: People have been struggling with this

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: for the whole history of the field

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: and defining exactly what it is that we're talking about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: John Searle had this distinction between strong AI

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: and weak AI.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: And weak AI could be general AI,

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: but his idea was strong AI was the view

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: that a machine is actually thinking,

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: that as opposed to simulating thinking

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: or carrying out intelligent processes

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: that we would call intelligent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: At a high level, if you look at the founding

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: of the field, McCarthy and Searle and so on,

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: are we closer to having a better sense of that line

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: between narrow, weak AI and strong AI?

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: Yes, I think we're closer to having a better idea

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: of what that line is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: Early on, for example, a lot of people thought

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: that playing chess would be, you couldn't play chess

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: if you didn't have sort of general human level intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: And of course, once computers were able to play chess

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: better than humans, that revised that view.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: And people said, okay, well, maybe now we have to revise

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: what we think of intelligence as.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: And so that's kind of been a theme

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: throughout the history of the field is that

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: once a machine can do some task,

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: we then have to look back and say, oh, well,

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: that changes my understanding of what intelligence is

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: because I don't think that machine is intelligent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: At least that's not what I wanna call intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: Do you think that line moves forever

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: or will we eventually really feel as a civilization

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: like we crossed the line if it's possible?

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: It's hard to predict, but I don't see any reason

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: why we couldn't in principle create something

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: that we would consider intelligent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: I don't know how we will know for sure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: Maybe our own view of what intelligence is

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: will be refined more and more until we finally figure out

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: what we mean when we talk about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: But I think eventually we will create machines

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: in a sense that have intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: They may not be the kinds of machines we have now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: And one of the things that that's going to produce

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: is making us sort of understand our own machine-like

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: qualities that we, in a sense, are mechanical

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: in the sense that like cells, cells are kind of mechanical.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: I think it's difficult because of the world is so open-ended as to what kinds of things can happen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: So you have sort of what normally happens, which is just you drive along and nothing surprising happens.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: And autonomous vehicles can do, the ones we have now evidently can do really well on most normal situations,

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: as long as the weather is reasonably good and everything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: But if some, we have this notion of edge cases or things in the tail of the distribution,

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: we call it the long tail problem, which says that there's so many possible things that can happen

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: that was not in the training data of the machine that it won't be able to handle it

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: because it doesn't have common sense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: It's the old paddle moved problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: It's the paddle moved problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: Right. And so my understanding, and you probably are more of an expert than I am on this,

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: is that current self-driving car vision systems have problems with obstacles,

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: meaning that they don't know which quote unquote obstacles they should stop for and which ones they shouldn't stop for.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: And so a lot of times I read that they tend to slam on the brakes quite a bit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: And the most common accidents with self-driving cars are people rear-ending them because they were surprised.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: They weren't expecting the car to stop.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: Yeah. So there's a lot of interesting questions there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: Because you mentioned two things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: So one is the problem of perception, of understanding, of interpreting the objects that are detected correctly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: And the other one is more like the policy, the action that you take, how you respond to it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Melanie Mitchell: Concepts, Analogies, Common Sense & Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #61

body.input: So a lot of the cars breaking is a kind of notion of, to clarify,
