body.input: Where are the darkest places you've ever gone in your life?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: The following is a conversation with Karl Deisseroth,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: professor of bioengineering, psychiatry, and behavioral sciences at Stanford University.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: He's one of the greatest living psychiatrists and neuroscientists in the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: He's also just a fascinating human being.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: We discuss both the darkest and the most beautiful places that the human mind can take us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: He explores this in his book called Projections, A Story of Human Emotions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I highly recommend it. It's written masterfully.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: This is the Lex Friedman Podcast. To support it, please check out our sponsors in the description.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And now, dear friends, here's Karl Deisseroth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: You open your book called Projections, A Story of Human Emotions,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: with a few beautiful words that summarize all of humanity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: The book draws insights about the human mind from modern psychiatry and neuroscience.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So if it's okay, let me read a few sentences from the opening.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: You've got to give props to beautiful writing when I see it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Quote, In the art of weaving, warped threads are structural and strong and anchored at the origin,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: creating a frame for crossing fibers as the fabric is woven.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Projecting across the advancing edge into free space,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: warped threads bridge the formed past to the ragged present to the yet featureless future.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Yet featureless future. Well done. Well done, sir.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: The tapestry of the human story has its own warped threads, rooted deep in the gorges of East Africa,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: connecting the shifting textures of human life over millions of years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Spanning pictographs backdrop by creviced ice,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: by angulated forestry, by stone and steel, and by glowing rare earths.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: The inner workings of the mind give form to these threads, creating a framework within us,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: upon which the story of each individual can come into being.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Personal grain and color arise from the crossed threads of our moments and experiences,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: the fine weft of life, embedding and obscuring the underlying scaffold

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: with intricate and sometimes lovely detail.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Here are stories of this fabric fraying in those who are ill,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: in the minds of people for whom the warp is exposed and raw and revealing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: What have you learned about human beings, human nature, and the human mind

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: from those who suffer from psychiatric maladies for those for whom this fabric is warped?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: One thing we learn as biologists is that when something breaks,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: you see what the original unbroken part was for.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And we see this in genetics, we see this in biochemistry.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: It's known that when you have a mutated gene,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: sometimes the gene is turned up in strength or turned down in strength,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: and that lets you see what it was originally for.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: You can infer true function from dysfunction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And this is a theme that I thought needed to be shared

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: and needed to be made communicable to the lay public, to everybody,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: people who, which is, I think, almost all of us who think and care

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: about the inner workings of our minds, but who also care for those who have been suffering,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: who have mental health disorders, who face challenges.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But then more broadly, it's a very much larger story than the present.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: There's a story to be told where the protagonist really is the human mind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And that was one thing I wanted to share as well in projections, is that broader story,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: but still anchored in the moment of patients, of people, of experiences of the moment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Is there a clear line between dysfunction and function, disorder and order?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: This is always debated in psychiatry, probably more so than any other medical specialty.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I'm a psychiatrist. I treat patients still.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I see acutely ill people who come to the emergency room where there's no doubt

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: that this is not something that's working well, where the manifestation of disease is so powerful,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: where the person is suffering so greatly, where they cannot continue as they are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But of course, it's a spectrum.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And there are people who are closer to the realm of being able to work okay in their jobs

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: but suffer from some small dysfunction and everywhere in between.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: In psychiatry, we're careful to say we don't call it a disease or disorder

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: unless there's a disruption in social or occupational functioning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But of course, psychiatry has a long way to go in terms of developing quantitative tests.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: We don't have blood draws.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: We don't have imaging studies that we can use to diagnose.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And so that line ultimately that you're asking about between order and disorder,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: function and dysfunction, it's operational at the moment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: How are things working?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Can we just like linger on the terms for a second?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So this disease, dysfunction, how careful should we be using those words?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Can we just, even in this conversation, from a sort of technical perspective

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: but also a human perspective,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: how quick should we be in saying that schizophrenia, depression, autism,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: as we kind of go down across the spectrum of different maladies,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: just to use the word dysfunction and disease?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I would say to give ourselves license to capture the whole spectrum,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: let's say disorder, because that captures truly, I think, the essence of it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: which is we need to talk about it when it's not working, when there's disorder.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And that's the fairest and most inclusive term to use.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So is it fair to assume that basically every member of the human species

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: suffers from a large number of disorders then?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Well, we just have to pick which ones are debilitating for each person.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: You know, if you look at the numbers, there are,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: if you look at how our mental health disorders are currently defined,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: you can look at population prevalence values for all these disorders,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: and you can come up with estimates that somebody will have a lifetime prevalence

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: of having a psychiatric disorder that approaches 25% or so.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And so that's, and in some studies it could be more, some studies it could be less.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Now, what do we do with that number? What does that mean?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And in some ways, that's the essence of what I was hoping to approach with the book,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: is to reflect on this spectrum that exists for all the disorders.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: There is, taking nothing away from the severity and the suffering

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: that comes at the extreme end of these illnesses,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: nearly every one of them exists on a spectrum of severity,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: from nearly functional to completely dysfunctional, life-threatening, and even fatal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And so that number, 25%, more or less, it doesn't capture that spectrum of severity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: To linger that number, where do those numbers come from?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Is it self-reported? Is it people who show up and say, I need help?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Is it somebody else that points out that person needs help?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Or is it like estimates that even go beyond that for people who don't ask for help

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: or are suffering quietly alone?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: When you look at self-report numbers, then those numbers get even higher, beyond 25% or more.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Those, the most rigorous studies are done with structured psychiatric interviews

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: where people who are trained in eliciting symptoms

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: carefully do complete psychiatric inventories of individuals.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And these are time-consuming, laborious studies that are not often repeated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: When they're done, they're done well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But very often you'll see a report or something in the news of a very high number

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: for some disorder or symptom.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And very often, if it's shockingly high, that's coming from a self-report of a person.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And so that's another issue that we have, again,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: to take nothing away from the severity and reality and biological nature of these disorders,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: which are very genetic, very, you know, we understand that these are very biological.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And yet we lack right now the lab tests and the blood draws to make the diagnosis.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: We'll talk about it, just how biological they are, because it's a, that too is a mystery.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I mean, you know, in terms of from our perspective of how to probe into the disease,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: how to understand it, how to help it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Some of it could be neurobiological, some of it could be just the dance of human emotion and interaction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And it's like, is love when it works and is love when it breaks down biological or is it something else?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So we're going to talk about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But let me just like to linger in terms of disorder.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: What about genius?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: What sort of cliche saying like the madness and genius that they kind of dance together?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: What about if the thing we see as disorder is actually genius, unheard or misunderstood?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Well, here again, the numbers help us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And here's where being rigorous and quantitative actually really helps.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: If you look at disorders like autism and bipolar disorder and eating disorders, anorexia nervosa, for example,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: these, you know, particularly bipolar and anorexia, these can be fatal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: They can cause immense suffering, but they are heavily genetic, all three of these.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And what's very interesting is each one of these three is actually correlated positively,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: positively with measures of intelligence, of educational attainment, and even of income.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And so you look at this severe disorders in many cases causing quite an immense morbidity and mortality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And yet they are positively correlated at the population level with positive things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Can you say the three again? Autism, anorexia and bipolar disorder.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Bipolar, right. What's that book? I forgot the book name, but is intelligence a burden?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Well, you know, people can get into trouble when they think they're smarter than they are. I will say that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I don't know. Sometimes like in the deepest meaning of that statement, I think ignorance is bliss.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I'm a big fan of Prince Mishkin from The Idiot and Arlyosha from Brother Karamazov.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Optimism can be seen as naivety and dumbness, but I think it's a kind of deep intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Maybe inability to reason sort of about the mechanics of the world, but instead kind of feel the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And it seems like that's one of the paths to happiness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: There is how much you think versus how much you feel. This comes up all the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: In medicine, we encounter this all the time. When you're day after day, you encounter this, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: the abyss of suffering from patients. How much do you let yourself feel?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Or how much do you make it abstract and objective and try to make it clinical?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And that range, how you're able to move yourself on that spectrum is very important for survival as a physician.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And the way you protect yourself and your feelings turns out to be very important.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: You quote Finnegan's Wake, mad props for that James Joyce book.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I took a class on James Joyce in college. I think I read parts of Finnegan's Wake.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I might have been on drugs of some kind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I somehow got an A in that class, which probably refers to some kind of curve where nobody understood anything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: The only thing I understood and really enjoyed is his short stories, The Dead.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And then Ulysses, I kind of, I think, read a few Cliff Notes that kind of got to the point.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And Finnegan's Wake was just a hopeless...

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: For people who haven't looked at it, maybe you can elucidate to me better,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: but I felt like I was reading things, words, and the words made sense, like standing next to each other.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But when you kind of read for a while, you realize you didn't actually understand anything that was said.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Right. But did you have a feeling though? That's one thing I found interesting about Finnegan's Wake.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I never fully understood it, but the words caused feelings in me, which I found fascinating.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And sometimes I couldn't predict it from the semantic black and white context of what I was seeing in front of me on the page.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But the rhythm or the melody would make me feel certain ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And that was what I always was intrigued by with Joyce.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Of course, that was his... He existed on a spectrum too. And he wrote, as you say, more accessible works.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I learned a lot about Irish history from Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: He could be as objective as he wanted to be, but then when he let himself loose,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: he was in this realm where the words had their own purpose separate from semantic meaning, from their dry dictionary definition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: There's a funny story that was told, doesn't matter if it's true or not,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: but they said that James Joyce, when he was young, when he was in his teen years,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: would go around sort of Ireland drinking and so on and telling everybody that he's going to be one of, if not the greatest writers of the 20th century.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And he turned out to be that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So I always think about that little story that somebody told me, because I have a lot of people come up to me, including myself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I'm a bit of a dreamer. You get into certain moods where you say I'm going to be the greatest anything ever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: You get people tell you this, especially young people, and it kind of makes me feel all kinds of ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But that story reminds me that you just might be one of the greatest writers of the 21st century, for example, if somebody were to tell me that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And don't immediately disregard that, because one of the people that say that, that's almost like a precondition, that's a good requirement just to believe in yourself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Maybe it's not a full requirement, but it's an interesting story.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I think when someone tells you that, then it creates, one sees an opportunity, and then it would be a tragedy if the opportunity weren't captured.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And so then that creates some impetus, some motivation to do something good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I think the mind, I guess that's what books or whatever, I don't even know if it's a book, The Secret plugs into.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: They kind of make a whole industry out of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But there is something about the mind believing something, making it a reality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: It is just time and time again with Steve Jobs, like your belief in yourself, your belief in an idea, sort of embracing the me versus the world,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: embracing the madness of this idea and making it a life pursuit, somehow morphs reality around for some tiny fraction of the population.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: For everybody else, you descend into all the beautiful ways that failure materializes in our lifetime.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: You mentioned love earlier.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: That's a great example of how belief in something makes it real.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: It's not reasonable on the face of it, but because you believe it's reasonable, then it actually does become reasonable and then it is real.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And so that's a good example. That doesn't happen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I'm also in a bioengineering department. We don't imagine that a bridge is soundly built and then it is soundly built.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: That's something that doesn't come up in too many realms of human existence, but love is one of them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And the ability to have a fixed idea and to say it's true and then it is true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: A bridge is a kind of manifestation of love.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So maybe it does work a little bit, but it can break down like Chernobyl did.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: You can't just say it's safe. You have to also prove it's safe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But on Finnegan's Wake, I think, maybe correct me if I'm wrong,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: you're using Finnegan's Wake to give one perspective on what madness is, of what's going on in the mind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: How much of that is that we're simply unable to communicate with the person on the other side of their mind?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: There's almost like a little person inside the brain and they have some circuitry that's used to communicate emotion,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: communicate ideas to the outside world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And there's something about that circuitry that makes it difficult to communicate with the little person on the other side.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So if you look at what shows up in schizophrenia with many cases, what we call thought disorders,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: what we call the individual speech symptoms of schizophrenia, Finnegan's Wake is loaded with them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And it's just full of them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: There's something about clang associations in schizophrenia where the word that is said echoes in some way the previous word.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And we call that a clang association because there's no other reason than the similarity of the sound,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: like a clang of a garage door being hit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And sometimes it's not even a word.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And we call that a neologism, a new word being created.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And of course, Finnegan's Wake is full of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And then we also in schizophrenia, there's what we call loose associations or tangential thought processes,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: of course, full of that where things just go off in directions that are not linear or logical.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And you can't read Finnegan's Wake, I think, without certainly as a psychiatrist, you can't read it without thinking about schizophrenia.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And then when we look at the families of people with schizophrenia, and Joyce was no exception,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: there very often are people within the family who are on the spectrum.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Some have it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Some are able to see it from a distance, from a safe distance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: There's an association between schizophrenia and what we call Schizotypal Personality Disorder,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: where people are not quite in this severe state of schizophrenia, but have some magical thinking, have some unusual thought patterns.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Very often those are family members of people with schizophrenia.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So this points to this, again, to this idea that there is a range, even along this very severe, very genetic biological illness

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: that human beings dwell on different spots along that spectrum.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I should mention that we have my friend Sergey pulling up stuff, young Sergey or old Sergey, I don't know what to call you,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: but there's drafts of Finnegan's Wake.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Yeah, I actually saw pictures of this from, I think it was on Instagram or something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: These are early drafts of Finnegan's Wake.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And it's so beautiful to see, for people who are just listening, there's just random paragraphs and writing all over the page with stuff crossed out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And it's great to see that Joyce himself was thinking in this kind of way as you're putting it together.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: How much do you think he was thinking about the schizophrenic mind?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I think a lot. I think it's known that his daughter suffered from schizophrenia.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And what's depicted here on the page is something that I'm sure he either felt himself

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: and some level was able to access this non-linearity of processing or had seen enough in family that he knew what it was

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: and was able to reflect it down in black and white on the paper.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So what he was able to do was quite authentic in that sense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Of course, I don't want to pigeonhole him. He was doing much more than that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: It was much more than talking about altered human thought processes and thought disorders.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But that was an aspect that he was so good at representing that it had to be intentional to some extent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: On a tiny tangent, what does your own writing look like for this book? Because it's extremely well written.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: How many edits? Did you just drink some whiskey? And like I'm imagining Hemingway style.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: The writing is very different. I mean, it's really, really well written, which was like...

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I was reading it. It makes you realize...

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Because I was expecting sort of a science kind of which it is like, you know, elucidating something about the human mind kind of thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But you could also probably write really strong novels. So maybe that's in the future.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But anyway, what is your... How many edits? What's your style? Does it look like that? Is it more structured, organized?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Unfortunately, I used a laptop, so I didn't have this sort of beautiful record of the process.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: No typewriters, cigarette, and whiskey.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I did explore which was their particular altered state that would help me to be most creative.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And I found actually I actually did the best while sober, but slightly disinhibited in the late hours of the night or early morning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Yeah, particularly late hours of the night there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I have a friend who would tell me that she thought that very early in the morning her inner critic was still asleep and she could write more effectively before her inner critic woke up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And I actually found that outstanding advice for me that I often found that I was looser and could write more in the morning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But the other interesting thing is each chapter, each story, it's about a different human being with a different class of psychiatric disorder.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: That's what each story, each chapter is anchored in.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But I'm trying to use words and style of writing and diction that captures the feeling of the disorder.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And so it's different in each story.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: In the story about mania, which is a very expansive, exuberant, at least briefly uplifting state where the words come out on a torrent

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: and they're complex and pressured and elaborate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I try to capture that feeling with the words used in that chapter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And then in the schizophrenia or psychosis chapter where things slowly fragment over time and become looser and separated, I tried to capture that in the writing too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So for each, it wasn't as if there was a single mode I could be in for the whole book.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: For each chapter, I had to put myself into a different mode to capture that inner feeling of the disorder.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: When you put yourself in that mode, does that change you?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Yeah, I couldn't turn it on and off right away.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: First, I would start by thinking about the person or the people, one or two people based on real patients and the stories that are put forth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: The symptom descriptions are real. They're from the patients.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Of course, all details change to protect privacy, but the actual symptom descriptions are real.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And I would sit with them and really try to inhabit the space of the mind of that person that I knew.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And that's not instantaneous. It would take some time. I needed quiet. I needed to be still.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: That's another reason late at night is good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Sergey posted that drowsiness gives creativity boosts according to Andrew Huberman.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Thank you, Andrew.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: He's not wrong. He's not wrong.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Why projections? Instead of putting words into your mouth, because I can imagine a lot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: To me, I will start putting words in your mouth despite what I just said.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So to me, projections, working on neural networks, for example, from an artificial neural networks, from a machine learning perspective, it's often that's exactly what you're doing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: It's an incredibly complex thing, and you're trying to find simple representations in order for you to make sense of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So I was kind of thinking about it in that way, which is like this incredibly complex neural network that is kind of projecting itself onto the world through this low bandwidth expression of emotion and speech and all that kind of stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And the way it's we only have that window into your soul, the eyes and the speech and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So that in that way, we're when there's any kind of disorder, we get to only see that disorder through that narrow window as opposed to the full complexity of its origins.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: The word projections definitely serves that purpose here, but it's got a few other really appropriate other connotations as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So the first thing is a projection in terms of neuroscience is this long range connection that goes from one part of the brain to another.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And so it's what binds two parts of our brain together. There are projections, long range connections of axons.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: These are the outgoing threads that connect one part of the brain to another part.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: There's a projection that links, for example, auditory cortex where we hear things to reward centers where we can feel where feelings of pleasure and reward are initiated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And it's been shown that if you have reduced connectivity along that dimension, you are less able to enjoy music.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And so these connections, these projections matter. They define how effectively two parts of the brain can engage with each other and join together to form a joint representation of something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So that's one meaning. It's pure neuroscience. The word projection is used all the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And it happens to be something that optogenetics, a technique that we maybe we'll talk about a little later, it works particularly well with.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: We can use light to turn on or off the activity along these projections from one spot of the brain to another.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And this is particularly referring to the long range connections.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: It's particularly straightforward along these long range projections that connect different parts of the brain, but it works over shorter range too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But then there's this other meaning of projections, which you were bringing up, which is very relevant, which is at some point you can reduce something from one level of dimensionality to another.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: You can project down into a lower dimensional space, for example.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And then finally, there's a psychiatric term projections, which comes up all the time, which is we very often will look at our internal states and to understand somebody else will project them onto somebody else.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: We'll try to understand someone else's behavior and make sense of it by projecting our own inner feelings, our own sort of narrative onto them and use that as a way to help us understand them better.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And we'll do the reverse too. We'll take things we see in the outside world and we'll bring them into ourselves and see how well they map, how well they align.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: That's called introjection. So projections turns out to be a really rich word.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And then finally, of course, there's the very common sense of it as a projector that illuminates by conveying information across space with light.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So for English language, perfect word to use for this book. But what was funny is not every...

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: There are a lot of international translations now and all those rich connotations aren't captured in other languages.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And so for some translations, connections is used instead of projections. In fact, even in England, the British version is connections instead of projections because apparently projections doesn't have the full connotation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: You have to sacrifice some of the rich ambiguity of meaning of the connections. That's interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Words are so interesting. They have so many meanings. I love language and how much is lost in translation. I'm very fortunate enough to be able to speak.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I'm not good at languages. I was just, I guess, forced to by life circumstance to learn two languages, Russian and English.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And it's just so interesting to watch how much of culture, how much of people, how much of history is lost in translation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: The poetry, the music, the history, the pain, the way the scientists actually express themselves, which is funny.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I mean, it's so sad to see how much brilliant work that was written in Russian.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: There's a whole culture of science in the Soviet Union that is now lost.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: It makes me wonder in the modern day how much incredible science is going on in China that is lost in translation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And I'll never, I mean, that makes me very sad because I'll never learn Chinese in the same way that I've learned English and Russian.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Maybe whenever I say stuff like that, people are like, well, there's still time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Yeah, that's actually fair that I think the 21st century, both China and US will have very important roles in the scientific development.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And we should actually bridge the gap through language. And that doesn't just mean convincing Chinese to speak English.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: That means also learning Chinese.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Well, we need these bridge people who can do both. Nabokov, for example, writing in English beautifully.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: One of my favorite poets, Borges, who I mentioned earlier, he wrote both in English and in Spanish, I think beautifully in both.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: We need those people who can serve as bridges across cultures. He really can do both.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: You mentioned Borges, so you open your book with a few lines from a poem by Jorge Luis Borges, a love poem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I'm going to read parts of it because it's a damn good poem. It's called Two English Poems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I mean, there's I'd like to understand why you used it and the specific parts you used, which is interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But then when I read the full thing, so I think you used it as a sort of beautiful description of what it means to delve deep into understanding,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: offering yourself to the task of understanding another human being.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But if you look at the full context of the poem, it's also a damn good description of being hit by love and overtaking by it and sort of in trying to try to figure out how to make sense of the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Now that you've been stricken by it, it says a bunch of things about chatting and significantly with friends and all those kinds of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And then the poem reads, the big wave brought you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: This is the moment, I guess, of the universe where the two people you fall in love.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Maybe I'm totally misreading this poem, by the way. Doesn't matter. You can't miss read a poem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So it goes on, words, any words, your laughter and you so lazily and incessantly beautiful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: We talked and you have forgotten the words.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: The shattering dawn finds me in a deserted street of my city.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Your profile turned away.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: The sounds that go to make your name.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: The lilt of your laughter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: These are the illustrious toys you have left me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So these little memories of these peculiar little details he remembers, those are the illustrious toys.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I apologize to mix my own words with the poem, but you should definitely read it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I turn them over in the dawn. I lose them. I find them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I tell them to the few stray dogs and to the few stray stars of the dawn.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Your dark, rich life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I must get at you somehow.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I put away those illustrious toys you have left me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I want your hidden look.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Your real smile.
