body.input: Optogenetics is a way of causing things to happen. It's a way of determining what actually matters in terms of the activity of the brain for the amazing things it does, sensation, cognition, action.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And what it does is it provides activity. It's a way of playing in, if you will, activity patterns into precisely defined cells.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And the way we do it is pretty cool, I think. Right away there's a problem. If you think about how do we do this, how could we play in well defined activity patterns and provide a stream of activity into this cell and that cell and that cell, but not these other cells?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Just for context, we're talking about the brains of mice, monkeys, humans. And then the goal is to try to control accurately the behavior of a single neuron and then to be able to monitor single collection of single neurons to then say, well, to draw some deeper insight about the origins.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: First of all, the function of different parts of the brain, different neurons, different kinds of neurons, but also the origins of the big things, the flap of the butterfly wing that leads to an actual behavioral thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Yeah. Exactly. So if you could turn on or off the brain or parts of the brain or cell types or individual cells at the natural rate and rhythm and timing of normal brain activity, that would be immensely valuable because you could determine what actually mattered, what could cause complex things to happen, and what could prevent complex things from happening in a specific way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But right away, you've got a problem if you want to do this. And neuroscientists have wanted to do this for a long time. Francis Crick of Double Helix of DNA fame, he wrote a famous paper in 1999.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: He got interested in neuroscience later in life. And he said, what we need in neuroscience is a way that we could turn on or off the activity of individual types of neurons in a behaving animal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And he even said the ideal signal would be light because it would be fast, it could penetrate through the brain to some extent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And he had no idea how to do it. He said this would probably be very far-fetched, but it would be a good thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And so that's what you're actually saying. Like if you want to do this kind of thing, and imagine like, how do I get inside the brain? It's pretty difficult.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: It's pretty difficult. And then even once you get in, it's hard because all brain cells are electrical. All neurons are electrically activated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And so if you wanted to use electricity as what you were putting in, you won't have any specificity at all.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: If you have an electrode, a wire, and you put it in the brain and you send current through it, all the cells near the electrode will be stimulated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: That's like trying to control fish by spraying them with water.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Yeah, right. Because there's already a lot of electricity going around anyway, and you're adding more.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But there's no specificity even among the different kinds of cells either because all around the wire that you've put in,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: there are going to be so many different cells doing totally different things, many of them in opposition to each other.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: We know that's one way the brain is set up. There are parts of the brain where neurons side by side are doing completely different things and maybe even antagonistic to each other.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So what do you do? How do you play in activity with any kind of specificity?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Well, what you do is use what we found is what you can do is make some cells responsive to light.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Now, normally, no cells deep in the brain really respond to light. They're not built for that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: There's no reason for them to respond to light in there, which is a great situation to start with because any light sensitivity you can provide to some cells

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: will be a huge signal above the noise. And so that's what we do with optogenetics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: We take genes, bits of DNA from microbes, single-celled organisms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And these single-celled organisms like algae, they make little proteins that sit in the surface of their cells that receive light,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: capture a photon of light and open up a little hole in the membrane of the cell and let charged particles, ions like sodium and potassium, flow across the membrane of the cell.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And these algae and bacteria, they do this for their own reasons because that helps them move. It helps them make and use energy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But that's a beautiful thing for neuroscience because movement of ions, charged particles across the membrane of the cell is exactly the kind of electricity that neurons work with.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So if we can take this bit of DNA that encodes this beautiful protein that turns light into electricity from algae,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: and if we can put it into some neurons, but not other neurons, which we can do using genetic tricks,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: then you've got a situation, then you can shine on the light and only the cells that have the gene and that are expressing the gene will be the initial direct cells that are activated by the light.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And so that's the essence of optogenetics is the ability to do that. We get that initial specificity that you could never get with an electrode.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: First of all, let me say that this is the recently got the Alaska Prize for this is a brilliant idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So I talked to Andrew Huberman, who's a friend of yours, friend of mine, not to jinx things, but he believes that he deserves the Nobel Prize for this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So I do too, but what my votes? Anyway, the thing is, it doesn't matter prizes will be all forgotten.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: All of us will be forgotten when the cool idea is a cool idea. It's a really powerful idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: It's actually the origins of it you might be interested in are even are very deep.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: There was a botanist in St. Petersburg named Andre Fomenson in 1866.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: He published a paper on the single celled green algae, and he was the botanist who first noticed that they moved in response to light.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: These are tiny single celled algae that have flagella, so they swim through the water.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And he noticed this. He was a botanist, and he published this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: It was a paper he wrote in German, but he published it in a French journal, and he was doing it from St. Petersburg.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So it was a very international effort. But you have to go back to 1866.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And that I just I like to highlight how far back that discovery goes is back to Andre Fomenson.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And this is a it highlights the value of just pure basic science discovery that always originates somewhere in the Eastern European block.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But I don't think he expected the splicing of genetic material from the algae into the human brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And one of the cool things we've been able to do now with modern methods is to really study these proteins.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And so we we've discovered some of these proteins. Other other groups have as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: We've dived deep into their structure, just like the double helix structure of DNA was uncovered with X-ray crystallography.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: We use the same method, X-ray crystallography, to see how these beautiful little proteins work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: We re-engineered them for all kinds of function. We can make them instead of responding to blue light, we can make them respond to red light.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: We can speed them up, slow them down. We can make them with genetic engineering.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: We can make them have different ions flow through them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And so it's this convergence, as you said, like the botanist in 1866 couldn't have predicted what we could do with this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And the fact that we've been able to discover how these beautiful proteins work and then apply them to neuroscience is really a thrilling story.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Is it possible to achieve scale, do you think, with this? Meaning like greater like what is the progress of the next 50 years, 100 years looks like in terms of the precision and the scale of control using light?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: It's going so fast, it's hard to predict. I'll give you a sense of it, though.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: In the first paper we published in 2005, that was just in cultured neurons, by 2007. So that was in a dish.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: By 2007, we had it working in behaving mice. By 2009, we had it pretty general.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So we had methods to really make it a versatile method. It could be applied to essentially any cell.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: By 2012, we could get to single cell resolution. We used light guidance strategies to target individual cells in the brain of a living mouse.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: By 2019, we were able to control up to 20 to 50 individually specified single cells in the brain of a mouse and in ways that specifically changed its behavior, that could bias its decisions one way or the other.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: In fact, we could take a mouse and without any visual stimulus at all, we could make it act as if it had seen a particular visual stimulus by playing in, using the single cell resolution optogenetics,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: a specific pattern of activity into 20 or 25 individually specified cells.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: That's 2019. To your question of scale, now in 2022, we're controlling hundreds of individually specified single cells over all of visual cortex of a mouse, all the part of the brain that is the initial direct target of the incoming information from the retina.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Are you constrained to specific types of cells currently? Like you mentioned long range is a little easier. Is there constraints on which cells?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Now there really isn't. Now that we have this individual cell guidance, we can target any individual kind of cell very reliably.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And so now to your question of scale, how far can we go? Well, things are moving quickly. It's hard to say.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: We can access individual cells across the entire brain now. If you look 10, 20 years in the future, I think we'll surprise ourselves.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But the fact that we're already able to cause specific perceptions to happen and specific actions means we're essentially where we want to be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And now it's a matter of just more experiments, more discoveries, but the basic principles are clear now. The basic capability is there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Is there a pathway to doing the same for humans?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Optogenetics is primarily it's a discovery tool that really is well suited for use in mice and rats and monkeys because it involves putting in a gene and also delivering light.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And those are two things that you can do in human beings, but you'd want to do in a very careful way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Now that said, there is actually just less than a year ago, my friend Botan Roska in Switzerland, he did the first human optogenetics therapy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And he published this in the journal Nature Medicine. So about 10, 12 years ago, he and I published a paper together where we gave him one of our optogenetic tools,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: one of these light activated regulators of ion flow. These are called microbial opsins, by the way, opsins.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And he put one of those into an extracted retina from a human being who had died.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So it was a cadaveric retina and he was able to show that optical control in this paper was able to turn on or off individual cells in the human retina.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So that was a while back. He spent about 10 years of going through all the regulatory hoops and hurdles and going through primate studies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And finally, he was able to take a human being with a retinal degeneration syndrome, so someone who was blind in both eyes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And he gave one of these opsins into one eye of this human being who was blind and with the goal of conferring light sensitivity onto this retina that was not able to see light.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And he was able to make this person see through that eye. So he took a blind person and the blind person could see now, could reach for objects selectively on a table.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And he published this in Nature Medicine. And it was, you know, that's an amazing thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Do you know the title of the paper? What's his name again?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Roska. R-O-S-K-A.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Can you look up the Nature paper?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Nature Medicine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Nature Medicine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So that's sort of proof of principle. Now, the retina is very accessible. It's near the surface. You can use natural light or you can use brighter natural light.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I'm myself, I see optogenetics as a discovery tool. It's a way to figure out the principles by which the brain works and how it operates.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Partial recovery, visual function in a blind patient after optogenetic therapy. So he went through the full process of doing primates studies and then going, well, that's dedication and that's really exciting to see.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Yeah. As beautiful as that is, and I'm glad he did all that work, there are so many other ways that optogenetics could help with therapies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Once you know the principles, then any kind of therapy can become more powerful. Once you know the causal cells in a symptom, like in lack of motivation or inability to enjoy things or altered sleep or altered energy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Once you know the cells that are causal, then you can make medications that address those cells. You could address brain stimulation treatments that might address those cells.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Also diagnosis. You need to be very effective systematic way of diagnosing or at least providing you rich data to some of these deep questions about schizophrenia, about bipolar, all those kinds of things that are the tools are low resolution currently for

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: determining what night the degree to which you have a thing and whether you have a thing at all.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Yeah, and exactly. And so the hope is, you know, that's a, this is a great example of how you can cure or you can, you know, provide some relief for a symptom of a person who has a serious degenerative disease.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But, but the principles are what we're after. And that's why I spend, even though I'm a psychiatrist, even though I still see patients, I'm not myself trying to drive any clinical trials in the lab.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I'm trying to discover and then any kind of therapy could result from that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: What do you think about my friend Elon Musk and his efforts with Neuralink? So this is another, there's a lot of things to say about that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: There's a lot of things to say here because there's a lot of ideas under the umbrella of Neuralink.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But one of them is to use electrical signals to stimulate and you also record, you collect electrical signals from the brain at a higher and higher resolution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And you go implant surgically the methods by which you do the stimulation and the data collection.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So it's possible for the ideas of optogenetics to play well with this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And we can even zoom out outside of just Neuralink and just the whole idea of brain computer interfaces.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: What are your thoughts? Well, I think the engineering that they've done is actually pretty cool.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So I like the robots. Yeah. From the, from the design perspective.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And it wasn't, it was a design approach that wasn't being taken in academia and it's great that they did it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And I think it's pretty cool. So I'll say that also there are many ways that you can record from many thousands of neurons.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And that's not the only way. It's a very interesting way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: We and others are using brain penetrating electrodes that actually get quite deep.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: The whole structure of the brain is very interesting. We there's the surface cortex where it's the most recently emergent part of the brain and evolution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Mammals have it. Reptiles have something a little bit like it, but it's not really the full thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: It's a, this is a very recent thing. That's what we can access with some of these, you know, like the Neuralink approach and with some of these short electrodes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: This part of the brain, the cortex is only a few millimeters thick. There's so much that's deep though. That's so important.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: There's the striatum, there's the thalamus. There are the parts of the brain that drive motivation, that drive hunger and thirst and social interaction and parenting and flight and fear and anxiety.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: All these things are, there's so much that's deep that these surface approaches are not getting to.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And so we and others are using these very long electrodes that help us get deep. And we can still record for many cells, many thousands of cells.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: We can have multiple of these at once in the same animal. And so there's a diversity of methods to get to this goal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I think it's great that people coming from, you know, the outside academia will bring ideas that weren't being worked on, at least approaches.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: How did the manic state unleash this religiosity?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But you see that in other realms of psychiatry too, OCD can manifest as religiosity also.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: You can take people who never really had a religion, never played a powerful role in their life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But then when their obsessive compulsive symptoms become severe, they can manifest in this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I think I'm in that group. So I'm a bit OCD.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: We have, there's, I think these subreddits, one is oddly satisfying things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So there's certain things that are really satisfying to my OCD, my mild OCD.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I think it's pretty much a religious experience.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So I understand that there's, if it's not direct, it's at least rhymes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So maybe can you speak to the, as Sergey is probably desperately scrambling to pull up, oddly satisfying.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Thank you. People can check it out themselves.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: It is, as the subreddit promises, oddly satisfying.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Can we talk about bipolar and maybe depression?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Well, let's talk about, I mean, I don't know if there's a nice way to discuss the differences in the full landscape of suffering that's here,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: but maybe what is depression and what are the types of depression?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: What kind of depression have you seen and experienced and researched?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And how can people overcome it? How can humans overcome it and deal with it, live with it and overcome it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So this is my clinical specialty.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I see patients in my outpatient clinical work with treatment resistant depression.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So very hard to treat severe illness where medications haven't been working.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I also see patients with autism spectrum disorders.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: These are my two clinical focal areas, but then I do emergency room work as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But the depression, why do I focus on that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: It's so, one feels tantalizingly close to helping these people who are suffering so deeply.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And that's why I focused on it is these are people who, there may not even be anything situational that's difficult or challenging in their life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: You can have people who seem to have everything that you would want.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: They have every objective measure of the life is fine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And yet they can be just hit with this unstoppable hopelessness and inability to see into the future,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: a discounting of the value of their own action.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Anything they can imagine themselves doing seems worthless or they are unable to enjoy things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I call this anhedonia. There's no reward, no pleasure, not in food, social interaction, movies, books, anything that they would enjoy, positivity gone.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: They can have a profound negative internal state, psychic pain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And these things can seem and in the severe cases are inescapable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So what is going on? Why is this state part of the human existence?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: It's got a strong biological genetic link. We know that it's been linked to certain genes, certain regions of the chromosome and twin studies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: There's a clear genetic link. Doesn't explain everything, but it's a big part of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Genetics are a strong contributor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And although you can have depression without anything terrible going on in your life, the symptoms can be made worse by stressors, by trauma.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But at a very deep level, there's nothing we can measure in a person objectively.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So we don't have, there's not a known chemical, not a known structure that's different, not a known brain activity pattern that we can pick up with EEG.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: A lot of people are exploring this, but right now we have no objective measures.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: All we do is talk to people and we elicit these symptoms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: We explore them, distinguish them from other possible causes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And then what do we do? Well, we have a range of treatments.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: We have medications that can help people, do help people, but not everybody.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And if they don't work, then we can go to brain stimulation methods.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: We can do things even like electroconvulsive therapy, which is a very effective, but it's sort of the final thing we go to in the end.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And so we have treatments. They work for some people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: They don't do everything we'd like.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But here's the problem is at a very deep level, we don't understand really what's going on in the brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: We don't have a physical interpretation of the problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: We have all these symptoms, but we can't yet point to a set of cells or a set of circuits or an activity pattern that is causing major depression, this disease state per se in human beings.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Why do you think you can't yet from an optogenetics perspective?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Is it because there's so many possible causes? Is it so much so many things involved?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So I think the answer is there are many things involved and all these different symptoms that I've mentioned, those we can study and those we can fix the individual symptoms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And we can do this in animals to be clear.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So in a mouse, for example, we can instantaneously and precisely turn up or down the motivation of an animal to overcome a challenge.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: We can turn up or down its ability to be motivated by or we think experience reward from situations or actions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: We can increase its apparent energy level, its drive to meet challenges.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: We can turn up or down social interaction, all these individual features of depression, individual symptoms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: We now can point to exact projections and cells that are causal in meeting these.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But we don't know is why all these different symptoms show up together in major depression in the human disease syndrome.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And that's the mystery.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: It's sort of in other fields of medicine, someone with congestive heart failure who comes into the clinic, they have very different symptoms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: They have shortness of breath and they have swollen feet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Okay, couldn't be two more different across the body sets of symptoms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Neither one obviously related to the heart, but they're both happening because the heart is not working as a pump.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Okay, and now thankfully in cardiology, we understand these disparate symptoms that seem totally unrelated can be completely understood because there's an altered pump action of the heart.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: That's what we are hoping for in psychiatry and in the study of depression or any disease.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: These different symptoms, the inability to enjoy things, the hopelessness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: What's the unifying principle?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Is there some truth to that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: The Tolstoy quote that all happy families are alike and each unhappy family is unhappy in its own way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So basically, this is the human condition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: The physicists long to find the theory of everything. Isn't understanding depression essentially require you to really have the big theory of everything for the human mind?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I think it would certainly be nice to have a theory of everything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Don't get me wrong.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I don't think we need an understanding of the century.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: It would be nice.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: It's also a good question if it's possible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Yeah, well, that I have some thoughts on too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But to this specific question, I don't think we need a theory of everything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I think there will be unifying principles we can get to.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But even shy of that, we can treat symptoms and that's a big step.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And as you say, different unhappy families are different.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Different unhappy people are different.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: If we have somebody who comes to the clinic and I see someone with a profound anhedonia as one of their main symptoms, inability to enjoy things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And if I know based on optogenetics work and animal work that a particular medication can treat anhedonia, even if it doesn't fix major depression in everybody, if I treat that one symptom in that one person, that's a good thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And so we don't need the theory of everything and we don't even need the unifying principle to help people with insights that come from optogenetics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: How much does talking help for diagnosis and for treatment, would you say, for depression?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: It's a big part of what we do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Every good psychiatrist should be pretty adept in these verbal communications and talk therapy as part of what they do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I give medications, I deliver brain stimulation treatments, but a big, big part of everything I do with every patient is talk therapy because it works so well together with these other modalities.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Even alone, it can help people with moderate or mild depression by itself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: People with severe depression, people with other psychiatric illnesses that are severe, you don't want to do talk therapy alone.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: It's not going to do it, but it still is crucial to do together with the others.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And it's critical because it's part of how you reshape cognitions, complex activity patterns, and you won't get to that with a medication or brain stimulation treatment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Do you have advice for people who suffer from mild forms of depression or feel as they might both for those people?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And do you have advice for people who love the people who suffer from depression and want to help?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Yeah. One of the incredibly frustrating things about depression is the very nature of it makes it hard for the people who suffer to get treatment because they're hopeless.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So they don't think treatment will help.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: They have low energy, so they're not motivated to participate in treatment in many cases.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Sometimes they're actively suicidal. That certainly doesn't help.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: They have all these things that seem to prevent treatment from being effective.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So that's where the loved ones are so important is helping them overcome these barriers to treatment, the motivation, the safety, and the insight.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: That's critical, and particularly for the severe cases.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: For the mild cases where people still have some insight and motivation and energy to get something done, there are many things you can do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Exercise is extremely important in mood, maintenance, regulation of sleep, and getting sufficient and regular enough sleep is very important.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And talk therapy can be helpful in those mild or moderate cases, just looking at cognitions, looking at patterns of thought that people may have fallen into,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: where they catastrophize, where they spiral from small things into big things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: A little bit of talk therapy, 10, 12 sessions, can help people identify those patterns they may have in themselves that are taking occasional negative thoughts,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: which everybody has, and magnifying those into more persistent negative states.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: If you work at this, and it's kind of like homework, this is what we call cognitive behavioral therapy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: It's very structured, very organized, you work hard, it requires insight and motivation, and you have to be motivated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But if you are, then you can identify these triggers that send you down particular pathways and work to intercept them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And that is amazingly very effective in mild to moderate cases.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So you basically have to train yourself to see the world as a collection of triggers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And you have to first understand, collect the data, basically see every experience as a thing that creates a follow-on emotion, a feeling.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I've learned this on social media, where early on, like all of us, I'll say something, I kind of respond to negativity with negativity,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: and then you observe the result of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And then over time, you think, wait a minute, this thing that I've been doing where when somebody says you suck and you say, no, you suck,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: that never produces the result you thought it might.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So I might not want to just don't say you suck back.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And I do this through a lot of things in life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I'm very fortunate to not suffer from depression, but I first of all have had and have people in my life who do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And also, all of us have depression who don't suffer from depression, have depression out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Like it's always knocking on the door.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And so you have mild, I mean, if you're very careless with the triggers all around you,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: then you're just, I think all of us have the capacity to really suffer from that kind of chemical or psychological or philosophical existential crisis.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But then it raises the question, why are we built this way?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: It seems like it doesn't make sense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And here's where some of us thinking about where we came from as the human family is kind of interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: It doesn't make sense that somewhere on that spectrum that it's good to detect that there's an array of adverse forces out there in the world right now at this moment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And to withdraw, to hunker down, to not fight, not strive, not try to meet the challenge and outweigh these negative forces that are present out there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And that makes a lot of sense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And all animals that have been studied in one form or another show this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Even the worm that I mentioned earlier, C. elegans with 302 neurons.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: They can effectively give up in challenging situations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: We've done this with zebrafish, tiny little transparent fish.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: You can give them a challenging situation and they will give up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But then if you stimulate a couple of very specific brain regions in particular ways, you can motivate them to overcome the challenge.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And if you inhibit those regions, they give up much more easily than they would otherwise.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: You can do this in mice, you can do this in rats.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So this is an ancestral conserved pattern to detect that things are pretty bad out there and to conserve energy, to hunker down, to wait out the storm.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So as use, unfortunately, many of our maladies have useful roots that contribute to our survival.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So both depression and motivation have uses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Sometimes it's nice to just shut the hell up and huddle with the penguins versus, for some unknown reason, venture out on your own into the mountains like a David Goggins type character.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: They're neighbors. Psychoanalysis is relatively, it's not nearly done as much as the talk therapy like the cognitive behavioral therapy I mentioned.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: The psychoanalysis is a little more niche now and partly because it's not data isn't in terms of actual treatment of actual therapeutic effects,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: A lot of people still do it to gain insight into themselves.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And in general, it's a good sort of conversation starter. Those methods, they're good for getting things out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: We don't focus on dreams typically these days in psychiatry, but they're great conversation starters.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: They're great ways to get things out if people have, and so we like to use those methods just to get the ball rolling sometimes, get people to open up a little bit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But the actual treatment tends not to involve these psychoanalytic approaches where you are really probing the unconscious mind and its manifestation through dreams, for example, as the goal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: That's not the goal. Modern talk therapy, we're really focusing on treatment, how to get people to feel better.

body.input: See, I use that as a conversation opener, the Freudian thing where I try to delve at a bar of the deep sexual desires in a person's subconscious.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I like both, but they're very different. I like conversation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: We call it first break when someone experiences
