body.input: their first disruption of reality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: They can have a completely typical life up until that point.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So you might have a, and I've seen just heartbreaking cases

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: like this in the Stanford emergency room

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: where a kid who's come there has been extremely high functioning

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: in that sense of academic achievement and athletic

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: and interpersonal and then comes to college.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Usually in men, it's around 18, 19 when the first break happens.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Some terrifying paranoia hits or some auditory hallucinations start.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: They're getting screamed at by a voice in their head.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So devastating.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: With women comes on also often a little later, sometimes in the 20s.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And it can be progressive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: If it's not treated, it just progresses and progresses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: The voices become overwhelming.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: The delusions and paranoia extend and expand.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: The thought, the negative symptoms particularly become more and more severe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So one can't even maintain thoughts in any sort of ordered fashion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And then eventually, you know, it can be fatal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: It can lead to suicide.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: It can lead to erratic behavior that leads to accidents.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Now, it can be treated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: There are medications that help, fortunately.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: They have side effects, so they're not perfect.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: They can have movement problems and actually a whole host of different side effects

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: that come from the medications.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But we can help people now with schizophrenia very, very significantly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But the amazing thing, and this is emblematic of where psychiatry stands,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: we don't have the deep understanding.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Just like with depression, we don't have that heart as a pump level of understanding

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: that we'd like to have with schizophrenia, despite it being so biological,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: so genetic in its nature.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So is there a way to return to the other side of the first break?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So when you have a break with reality, is there a way to kind of stitch it together?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Yeah. So some people, that works.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But we don't really know how.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So medications, antipsychotic medications, we call them,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: they block a particular neurotransmitter receptor called the serotonin 2A receptor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And they modulate dopamine as well and other neurotransmitters.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: These can take someone who's actively hallucinating, actively paranoid,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: put them back in a completely normal state, and some people stay that way indefinitely.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So you can bring people back from that back to the other side, have it stitched together.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: More typically, you'll end up in some intermediate state where symptoms are reduced powerfully,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: but there might be still something there and you've got a drop down in functioning

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: that may be persistent for a while.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But concepts, what physically is going on?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: My idea is that it's communication within the brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: One part of the brain is not able to tell other parts of the brain what it's doing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And so the auditory hallucinations are very interesting in this regard.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: They often have this conversational inner monologue-like quality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: As we're walking along the street, we may have an inner monologue, thoughts about what's going on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: If we see somebody we don't like, we may have a thought,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I wish somebody would punch that guy, something like that, or maybe I should punch that guy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But these are so far below where we would ever act or even think of acting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But they're just things that come up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And in people with schizophrenia, those inner thoughts, that inner monologue is not recognized

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: as the inner monologue of the self.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And so it's perceived as something coming from the outside or from inside, but from another entity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Another entity. I thought you meant another room inside the same building.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Another room inside there, yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And so it could be conceptualized as a communication within the brain problem,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: notifying another part of the brain what's going on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And there's some evidence consistent with that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I don't know if you can help with this, but I sometimes,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: because I've been talking to quite a few homeless folks recently,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: it's what I do is I hang out at night and talk to interesting people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And I've known people in the past who suffer from schizophrenia,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: and some of them like self will describe that as something they suffer from.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And they seem to understand something deeply about this world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I don't know if it's correlated or maybe it's another aspect of depression,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: all those things that I've encountered in my own life,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: is maybe just the struggle and the suffering has taken you through a life where you think deeply about life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: There's self-reflection that society forces on you because it's a disorder of some kind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: It's interesting. I guess my only sort of anecdotal observation is people who suffer from schizophrenia

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: seem to be very interesting and very thoughtful in a nonlinear way about the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I've noticed that it's not always positive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: The unusual ways they view the world, but it's always interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: It could be conspiratorial thinking too, but the theories they have about the way the world functions,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: often very well read, which is also interesting,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: because they're almost looking for helpful answers from somewhere.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And so they might be citing some very interesting literature and then using that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: there's a stickiness in their mind to different models of the world and trying to make sense of that world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And those models could include conspiracy theories.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: They're very attuned to complexity and they come up with unlikely explanations,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: which is one of the things that makes it hard for them to function in the world is how unlikely their explanations are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But you're right, there's a depth of consideration of the complexity of the world and a concern about it

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: and an impulse to work to understand it that is actually quite refreshing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But the first case in the medical literature, there was a classical schizophrenia.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: There was a patient named James Tilly Matthews who had this, he sketched out for his doctor the experiences he was sensing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And he drew himself as a cowering figure on the ground controlled by a loom,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: a weaving device that was sending threads, long threads, projections across space from the loom to him,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: to his arms and to his body and controlling him from afar.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And he called this the heirloom, a loom in the heir.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And it was such an evocative thing because this was the start of the Industrial Revolution or MID

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: and it was where really industrial strength looms and weaving devices were really kind of the emblematic

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: of the most complex, powerful technological achievements of the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And so that was the explanation available to him to explain how his body was seemingly moved without his volition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And these days, of course, people with schizophrenia will have more technology appropriate interpretations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: They'll have delusions of satellite or alien control or beamed information,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: very, very common to have this delusion of a government agency sending electromagnetic

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: or radio frequency information to control their limbs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But it's the same thing, whether it's a thread from an Industrial Revolution loom or RF radiation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: it's the same thing just adapted to the moment trying to explain the world they live in and their relationship to the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But unconstrained by sort of the thing that's socially acceptable, which is both refreshing and dangerous.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I wrote down a question. Why do we cry?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Are tears a window to some depths that we ourselves don't know?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I almost want to make fun of myself for that question, but you do talk seriously about crying in the book.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: In fact, the whole first chapter really, really tussles with crying as a why do we do it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: What does it mean? Why is it involuntary? It seems like a weakness, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: It's because it's so involuntary and it's reflecting something true and inside at the level of the individual.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: That seems like a problem, right? Wouldn't it be better if we could control it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: if we could not show that emotion when it's not useful, show it when it's useful, but it's not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: It's largely involuntary.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And so there's a value to it, I think, as an honest reporter of a need, of hope and frailty at the same time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I am a human being. There's a frailty to myself or my situation where I need social help.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I need help from my community. I have hope that that is possible, but I'm not enough for myself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I need the community. That I think is what the social signal of crying is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Now, people have studied crying. You can quantify the extent to which the presence of tears on a face

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: triggers reactions in onlookers. And you can show the same face in the presence or absence of tears

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: and show that to people under quantifiable and rigorous psychological conditions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And tears are much more powerful at stirring the desire to help in viewers than any other facial feature,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: which is pretty interesting that it's the honest one that's also the most powerful, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: It kind of indicates there's a certain logic to our design as social beings that we have an honest report.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: That's hard to control. But is it well understood how that connects to the internal state of emotion?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Yeah, there are long-range projections that come. So where is crying generated?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: This is the confusing thing about it. So we have a little tear duct, the lacrimal gland,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: that leads to the release of fluid. It ejects fluid and it comes out and knows, of course,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: that whole system was designed to keep the eye clean, to wash out particulate irritants.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So it's a long-standing, as long as we've had eyes and have been out of the water in our evolution,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: we've needed this sort of thing. So long-standing biological structure recently co-opted,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: it seems, by our evolution as social primates. Now, how could that happen?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Well, the lacrimal gland is controlled by structures in the pons,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: which is a structure deep in our, just above our neck, between our neck and our head,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: and reflecting its ancient origin, right? As you go farther down toward the spinal cord,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: these are the more basic early evolved structures. And in the pons, that's where breathing is controlled,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: tear duct contraction. And what we found, and with optogenetics, we helped sort this out,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: there are long-range projections from fear and anxiety regions in the forebrain that project all

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: the way to the pons in and around those areas. The reason those are there, we think, is to regulate

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: the respiratory rate changes, the breathing changes of fear and anxiety. So we know when we're in a

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: state of fear and anxiety, we need, we cope better if we have elevated heart rate, elevated

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: respiratory rate, more blood pumping around, more oxygenated blood, we're ready to meet the

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: threat if it happens. All those cells are down there in the pons too, right next to the lacrimal

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: duct, the tear gland neurons. And so almost certainly this fear anxiety induced crying

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: arose from a very slightly misdirected long-range projection that was there to regulate breathing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: and a little twist, just a little misdirection, a little missing of one sign post to stop here,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: going on a little farther, getting to the lacrimal gland neurons gave us crying.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And that's, and we just have it, that peculiar sort of structure, neuronal structure that resulted

body.input: present to allow cells to fuse together into a joint representation?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Just so I understand, because it feels close to some very, very deep idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: So there's a bunch of semi-distributed signals going on in the brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And you're saying there could be something like a theory of everything if one to exist,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: is to understand why, how and why signals close to each other start becoming

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: relevant to each other. That's right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: As part of some very much bigger signal that they're producing. How they coordinate essentially.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Because it's very distributed. I mean, that's a kind of within a distributed system, how is order

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: achieved? And this is a very specific kind of distributed system that is one of the most

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: intelligent that we're aware of in the known universe. And that will maybe be something also

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: an understanding of the full conscious experience too. That's what we're talking about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Two, that this kind of coordination, how does the coordination between different neurons that are

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: responsible for sense of self, how do they begin to form a big picture that we see as a human

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: experience? That's really, really interesting. So uniting the small and that's actually literally

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: theory of everything. Uniting the small, the sort of the theory of the neuron, the function of the

body.input: neuron with the big, just the functioning of the entire mind. That's right. And I think keeping a

body.input: toehold in both at the cellular level of resolution and the brain wide resolution will be critical.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: If you lose touch with either, I think you'll miss the big insight. So that's what we're trying to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Keeping grounded in the cellular resolution, trying to keep the broadest brain wide perspective

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: and meet in the middle. Do you think you'll see it in your lifetime? A major breakthrough in that

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: dimension. I have hope. I have hope. It's very hard to predict what will happen with big things

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: like this. If we don't get there, there'll be plenty of other exciting stuff. So it's okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: But the other aspect of this whole thing is that your life is pretty short. That's true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: That's true. So first of all, you can die any day. I tend to try to think about that, that

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: it ends, it can get in any moment because it really, really can. And if not, it'll be

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: soon anyway. Do you think about that? Do you think about your mortality?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I do. Yeah. It comes back to what we talked about earlier. I never think I've done enough and it's

body.input: relevant to that for sure. There's a deadline. Do you think there's ever going to be a feeling

body.input: where you sit back and you're really proud of yourself? I hope so. Like I've done enough. I've

body.input: done everything there is. Because the thing is a warrior has some number of battles in them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And at a certain point, if you're deeply honest, it's like, well, that was a pretty good run.

body.input: As far as runs goes, that was pretty good. And you can hang up your helmet and then go sort of

body.input: drink some ale, listen to some music with the old lady and say, I did pretty good. You think you'll

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: get there? Nature always has surprises for us. The curious mind is always after more. But biology

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: gives us other rewards, children and family, community, and one can feel good about those

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: things. Biology is full of rewards. But do you think about those rewards? What do you think is

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: the why of those rewards? What's the meaning of life and this existence? What's the why of biology?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: What does it want from us? Why are all these cells very busy putting together an organism that seems

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: to want to just be in a hurry to do stuff and survive, but it also just doesn't, it's not happy

body.input: being survived. Like you said, it's curious. It keeps wanting to get into more trouble. Why?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Yeah. We're clearly designed for that, right? We're clearly designed to ask why and to answer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: And that I think is, I don't know the meaning of all life. I think a meaning of our lives is that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: and this is the Aristotelian happiness. An organism is happy, an animal's happy if it's

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: performing to its design, right? If it's doing what it was made for.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Yeah. Well, you have to understand what's the design and who is the designer and what were they

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: up to and how hard is it? Do you have to build the whole universe? And does the design even know

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: what the hell they're doing? Because maybe the designer built humus to find out

body.input: about themselves. That's what I would do. Like if I had the power to build clones,

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I'll build a lot of clones and I'll get them into different trouble to understand

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: what's this body designed to do. How far can I go that way?

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: Exactly. And then I dissociate myself completely from having anybody that I know that person.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: That's good. I mean, I suppose you could do that in a single way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

body.input: I mean, I suppose you could do that in a single person's body, but dissociation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Karl Deisseroth: Depression, Schizophrenia, and Psychiatry | Lex Fridman Podcast #274

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: just observing as an outsider, because so much beautiful, such a beautiful world is possible

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: when everybody's well informed. My question for you is how hard is it to be well informed about

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: anything, whether it's healthcare or any kind of purchasing decisions or just life in general in

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: this world? Oh, information, it varies hugely. I mean, there's more information at your fingertips

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: than ever before in history. The trouble is, first of all, that some of that information isn't true,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: so it's really hard. And then some of it is just too hard to understand. So if I'm buying a car,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: I can actually probably do a pretty good job of looking up, going to consumer reports, reviews,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: you can get a pretty good idea of what you're getting when you get a car. If I'm going in for

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: surgery, first of all, fairly often it happens without you being able to plan it. But also,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: there's a, medical school takes many, many years and going on the internet for some advice is not

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: usually a very good substitute. So speaking about news and not being able to trust certain

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: sources of information, how much disagreement is there about, I mentioned utopia, perfection,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: in the beginning, but how much disagreement is there about what utopia looks like,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: or is most of the disagreement simply about the path to get there?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: Oh, I think there's two levels of disagreement. One, maybe not utopia, but justice. What is a

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: just society? And there are different views. I teach my students that there are, broadly speaking,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: two views of justice. One focuses on outcomes. A just society is the one you would choose if you

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: would choose to live in if you didn't know who you were going to be, that's kind of John Rawls.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: And the other focuses on process. A just society is one in which there is no coercion except we're

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: absolutely necessary. And there's no objective way to choose between those. I'm pretty much a Rawlsian

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: and I think many people are. But anyway, so there's a legitimate dispute about what we mean by a just

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: society anyway. But then there's also a lot of disputes about what actually works. There's a

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: range of legitimate dispute. Any card-carrying economist will say that incentives matter,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: but how much do they matter? How much does a higher tax rate actually deter people from working? How

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: much does a stronger safety net actually lead people to get lazy? I have a pretty strong view

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: that the evidence points to conclusions that are considerably to the left of where most of our

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: politicians are, but that there is legitimate room for disagreement on those things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: So you've mentioned outcomes. What are some metrics you think about that you keep in mind,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: like the Gini coefficient, but really anything that measures how good we're doing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: whatever we're trying to do, what are the metrics you keep an eye on?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: Well, I'm actually, I'm not a fan of the Gini coefficient, not because-

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: What is the Gini coefficient?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: Yeah, the Gini coefficient is a measure of inequality. And it is commonly used because

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: it's a single number. It usually tracks with other measures, but the trouble is there's no sort of

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: natural interpretation of it. If you ask me what does a society with a Gini of 0.45 look like as

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: opposed to a society with a Gini of 0.25? And I can kind of tell you, 0.25 is Denmark and 0.45 is

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: Brazil, but there's no sort of easy way to do that mapping. I mean, I look at things like what is

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: the income of the median family? What is the income of the top 1%? How many people are in poverty by

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: various measures of poverty? And then I think you want to look at questions like how healthy are

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: people? How is life expectancy doing? And how satisfied are people with their lives? Because

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: there is, that sounds like a squishy number, not so much happiness. It turns out that life

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: satisfaction is a better measure than happiness. But life satisfaction, that varies quite a lot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: And I think it's meaningful if not too rigorous to say, look, according to that kind of, according

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: to polling, people in Denmark are pretty satisfied with their lives and people in the United States,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: not so much so. And of course, Sweden wins every time. No, actually Denmark wins these days.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: Denmark and Norway tend to win these days. Sweden doesn't do badly, but none of these are perfect.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: But look, I think by and large, there's a bit of a pornography test if you

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: know a decent society, well, you kind of know it when you see it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: Right. Where does America stand on that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: We have a remark, our society, there are a lot of virtues to America, but there's a level of

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: harshness, brutality, an ability for somebody who just has bad luck to fall off the edge

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: that is really, shouldn't be happening in a country as rich as ours. So we have somehow managed to

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: produce a crueller society than almost any other wealthy country for no good reason.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: What do you think is lacking in the safety net that the United States provides? You said

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: there's a harshness to it. And what are the benefits and maybe limits that you think

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: are the benefits and maybe limits of a safety net in a country like ours?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: Well, every other advanced country has some universal guarantee of adequate healthcare.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: The United States is the only place where citizens can actually fail to get basic healthcare because

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: they can't afford it. It's not hard to do, everybody else does it, but we don't. We've

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: gotten a little bit better at it than we were, but still that's a big deal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: We have remarkably weak support for children. Most countries have substantial safety. Parents

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: of young children get much more support elsewhere. They get often nothing in the US. We have limited

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: care for people. Long-term care for the elderly is a very hidden thing. But I think that the really

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: big issues are that we don't take care of children who make the mistake of having the wrong parents,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: and we don't take care of people who make the mistake of getting sick. And those are things

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: that a rich country should be doing. Sorry for sort of a difficult question,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: but what you just said kind of feels like the right thing to do in terms of a just society.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: But is it also good for the economic health of society to take care of the people,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: the unfortunate members of society? By and large, it looks like doing the right

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: thing in terms of justice is also the right thing in terms of economics. If we're talking

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: about a society that has extremely high tax rates that deter, remove all incentives to provide a

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: safety net that is so generous that why bother working or striving, that could be a problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: But I don't actually know any society that looks like that. Even in European countries

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: with very generous safety nets, people work and innovate and do all of these things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: And there's a lot of evidence now that lacking those basics is actually destructive,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: that children who grow up without adequate healthcare, without adequate nutrition

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: are developmentally challenged. They don't live up to their potential as adults. So the United

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: States actually probably pays a price. We're harsh, we're cruel, and we actually make ourselves poorer

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: as a society, not just the individuals, by being so harsh and cruel.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: Okay. So invisible hand, Smith, where does that fit in? The power of just people acting selfishly

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: and somehow everything taking care of itself to where the economy grows,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: there's no cruelty, no injustice that the markets regulate themselves.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: Is there power to that idea and what are its limits?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: There's a lot of power to that. There's a reason why I don't think sensible people want the

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: government running steel mills or they want the government to own the farms. The markets are a

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: pretty effective way of getting incentives aligned, of inducing people to do stuff that works.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: And the invisible hand is saying that farmers aren't growing crops because they want to feed

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: people, they're growing crops because they can make money by it, but it actually turns out to be a

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: pretty good way of getting agricultural products grown. So the invisible hand is an important part,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: an important part, but there's nothing mystical about it. It's a mechanism, it's a way to organize

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: activity, which works well given a bunch of preconditions, which means that it actually

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: works well for agriculture, it works well for manufacturing, it works well for many services,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: it doesn't work well for healthcare, it doesn't work well for education.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: So having a society which is kind of three quarters invisible hand and one quarter visible hand seems

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: to be something on that order, seems to be the balance that works best. You don't want to

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: romanticize or make something mystical out of it. This is one way to organize stuff that happens to

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: have broad but not universal application. So then forgive me for romanticizing it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: but it does seem pretty magical that I kind of have an intuitive understanding of what

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: happens when you have like five, 10, maybe even a hundred people together, the dynamics of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: But the fact that these large society of people, for the most part, acting in a self-interested way

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: and maybe electing representatives for themselves, that it all kind of seems to work,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: it's pretty magical. Oh, sure. The fact that right now there's

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: a wide assortment of fresh fruit and vegetables in the local markets up and down the street.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: Who's planning that? And the answer is nobody. That's the invisible hand at work and that's

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: great. And that's a lesson that Adam Smith figured out more than 200 years ago and

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: it continues to apply. But even Adam Smith has a section in his book about why it's important to

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: regulate banks. So the invisible hand has its limits. Yeah. And that example is actually a

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: powerful one in terms of the supermarket fruit. That was my experience coming from Russia,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: from the Soviet Union, is when I first entered a supermarket and just seeing

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: the assortment of fruit, bananas. I don't think I've seen bananas before, first of all,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: but just the selection of fresh fruit was just mind blowing. It's beyond words. And the fact that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: like you said, I don't know what made that happen. Well, there is some magic to the market,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: but as showing my age, but the old movie quote, sometimes the magic works and sometimes it doesn't

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: and you have to have some idea of when it doesn't. So how do you get regulation right? What can

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: government at its best do? Strangely enough in this country today seems to get a bad rap.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: Everybody's against the government. Yeah. Well, a lot of money has been spent on making people hate

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: the government, but the reality is government does some things pretty well. I mean, government

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: does health insurance pretty well. So much so given our anti-government bias, it really is true

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: that there are people out there saying, don't let the government get its hands on Medicare.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: So people actually love the government health insurance program far more than they love

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: private health insurance. Basic education. It turns out that your local public high school

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: is the right place to have students trained and private for certainly for-profit education is

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: by and large a nightmare of ripoffs and grift and people not getting what they thought they

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: were paying for. It's a judgment case and it's funny. There are things, I mean, everybody talks

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: about the DMV as being, do you want the economy? Actually, my experience is that the DMV have

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: always been positive. Maybe I'm just going to the right DMVs, but in fact, a lot of government works

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: pretty well. So to some extent, you can do these things on a priori grounds. You can talk about the

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: logic of why healthcare is not going to be handled well by the market, but partly it's just experience.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: We tried, or at least some countries have tried nationalizing their steel industries. That didn't

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: go well, but we've tried privatizing education and that didn't go well. So you find out what works.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: What about this new world of tech? What do you think works for tech? Is it more regulation or

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: less regulation? There are some things that need more regulation. We're finding out that

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: the world of social media is one in which competitive forces aren't working very well

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: and trusting the companies to regulate themselves isn't working very well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: But I'm on the whole a tech skeptic, not in the sense that I think the tech doesn't work

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: and it doesn't do stuff, but the idea that we're living through greater technological change than

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: ever before is really an illusion. Ever since the beginning of the industrial revolution,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: we've had a series of ethical shifts in the nature of work and in the kinds of jobs that are available.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: And it's not at all clear that what's happening now is any bigger or faster or harder to cope

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: with than past shocks. It is a popular notion in today's public discourse that automation is

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: going to have a huge impact on the job market now. There is something transformational happening now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: Can you talk about that maybe elaborate a little bit more? Do you not see the

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: software revolutions happening now with machine learning, availability of data, that kind of

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: automation, being able to sort of process, clean, find patterns in data, and you don't see that

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: disrupting any one sector to a point where there's a huge loss of jobs? There may be some things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: I mean, actually, translators, there's a really reduced demand for translators because

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: machine translation ain't perfect, but it ain't bad. There are some kinds of things that are changed,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: but overall productivity growth has actually been slow in recent years. It's been much

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: slower than in some past periods. So the idea that automation is taking away all the jobs,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: the counterpart would be that we would be able to produce stuff with many fewer workers than before,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: and that's not happening. There are a few isolated sectors. There are some kinds of

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: jobs that are going away, but that keeps on happening. New York City used to have

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: thousands and thousands of longshoremen taking stuff off ships and putting them on ships.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: They're almost all gone now. Now you have the giant cranes taking containers on and off ships

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: in Elizabeth, New Jersey. That's not robots. It doesn't sound high tech, but it actually

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: pretty much destroyed an occupation. Well, it wasn't fun for the longshoremen to say the least,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: but we coped, we moved on, and that sort of thing happens all the time. You need farmers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: We used to be a nation which was mostly farmers. There are now very few farmers left. The reason

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: is not that we've stopped eating, it's that farming has become so efficient that we don't need a lot

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: of farmers, and we coped with that too. The idea that there's something qualitatively different

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: about what's happening now so far isn't true. Yeah, your intuition is there is going to be

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: a loss of jobs, but it's just the thing that just continues. There's nothing qualitatively

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: different about this moment. Some jobs will be lost, others will be created,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: as has always been the case so far. Maybe there's a singularity. Maybe there's a moment when

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: the machines get smarter than we are and SkyTech kills us all or something. But

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: that's not visible in anything we're seeing now. You mentioned the metric of productivity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: Could you explain that a little bit? Because it's a really interesting one. I've heard you mention

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: that before, the connection with automation. What is that metric, and if there is something

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: qualitatively different, what should we see in that metric? Well, okay, productivity. First of

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: all, production. We do have a measure of the economy's total production, real GDP, which is

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: itself, it's a little bit of a construct because it's quite literally, it's adding apples and

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: oranges. So we have to add together various things, which we basically do by using market prices,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: but we try to adjust for inflation. But it's a reasonable measure of how much the economy is

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: producing. Is it goods and- Sorry to interrupt. Is it goods and services?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: Goods and services. It's everything. Okay. Productivity is you divide that total output

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: by the number of hours worked. So we're basically asking how much stuff does the average worker

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: produce in an hour of work? And if you're seeing really rapid technological progress,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: then you'd expect to see productivity rising at a rapid clip, which we did for the generation

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: after World War II, productivity rose 2% a year on a sustained basis. Then it dropped down for a
