metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: while. Then there was a decade of fairly rapid growth from the mid-90s to the mid-2000s.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: And then it dropped off again, and it's not impressive right now. You're just not seeing

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: an ethical shift in the economy. So let me then ask you about the psychology of blaming automation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: A few months ago, you wrote in the New York Times, quote, the other day I found myself,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: as I often do at a conference, discussing lagging wages and soaring inequality. There was a lot of

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: interesting discussion, but one thing that struck me was how many of the participants just assumed

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: that robots are a big part of the problem, that machines are taking away the good jobs,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: or even jobs in general. For the most part, this wasn't even presented as a hypothesis,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: just as part of what everyone knows. So why is, maybe can you psychoanalyze our

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: public intellectuals or economists or us actually in the general public, why this is happening?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: Why this assumption is just infiltrated public discourse?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: There's a couple of things. One is that the particular technologies that are advancing now

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: are ones that are a lot more visible to the chattering class. When containerization did

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: away with the jobs of longshoremen, well, not a whole lot of college professors are close friends

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: with longshoremen, right? So we see this one. Then there's a second thing, which is we just went

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: through a severe financial crisis in a period of very high unemployment. It's finally come down.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: There's really no question that that high unemployment was about macroeconomics. It

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: was about a failure of demand, but macroeconomics is really not intuitive. I mean, people just have

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: a hard time wrapping their minds around it. And among other things, people have a hard time

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: believing that something as trivial as, well, people who just aren't spending enough can lead

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: to the kind of mass misery that we saw in the 1930s or the not quite so severe, but still serious

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: misery that we saw after 2008. And there's always a tendency to say it must be something big. It

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: must be technological change. That means we don't need workers anymore. There was a lot of that in

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: the 30s, and that same thing happened after 2008, the assumption that it has to be something,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: some deep cause, not something as trivial as a failure of investor confidence and inadequate

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: monetary and fiscal response. And the last thing on wages,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: a lot of what's happened on wages is at some level political. It's the collapse of the union

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: movement. It's policies that have squeezed workers' bargaining power. And for obvious reasons,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: there are a lot of influential people who don't want to hear that story. They want it to be an

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: inevitable force of nature. Technology has made it impossible to have people earn middle-class wages.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: They don't like the story that says, actually, no, it's kind of the political decisions that we made

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: that have caused this income stagnation. And so they're a receptive audience for technological

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: determinism. So what comes first in your view, the economy or politics in terms of what has impact

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: on the other? Oh, well, look, everything interacts. Actually, that's one of the rules that I was

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: taught in economics. Everything affects everything else in at least two ways. But clearly, the economy

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: drives a lot of political stuff, but also clearly, politics has a huge impact on the economy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: There, we look at the decline of unions in America and say, well, the world has changed and unions

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: don't have a role, but two-thirds of workers in Denmark are unionized. And Denmark has the same

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: technology and faces the same global economy that we do. It's just a difference in political choices

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: that leads to that difference. So I actually teach a course here at CUNY called Economics of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: Welfare State, which is about things like healthcare and retirement and to some extent, wage policy and

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: so on. And the message I keep on trying to drive home is that, look, all advanced countries have

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: got roughly equal competence. We all have the same technology, but we make very different choices.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: Not that America always makes the wrong choices. We do some things pretty well. Our retirement

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: system is one of the better ones. But the point is that there's a huge amount of political choice

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: involved in the shape of the economy. So what is a welfare state? Welfare state is the old

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: term, but it basically refers to all the programs that are there to mitigate, if you like, the

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: risks and injustices of the market economy. So in the US, the welfare state is social security,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: Medicare, Medicaid, minimum wages, food stamps. When you say welfare state, my first feeling is

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: a negative one. Even though I like all, I probably generally, at least theoretically,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: like all the welfare programs. Well, it's been demonized. And to some extent, I'm doing a little

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: bit of thumbing my nose at all of that by just using the term welfare state. Although it's not-

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: I see. Yeah, I got you. But everybody, every advanced country actually has a lot of

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: welfare state, even the US. That's a fundamental part of the fabric of our society. Social security,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: Medicare, Medicaid are just things we take for granted as part of the scene.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: And so if you- there's a lot of people on the right wing who are, you can say,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: oh, it's all socialism. And well, where's, I guess, meaning what you want them to mean.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: And just today, I told my class about the record that Ronald Reagan made in 1961,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: warning that Medicare would destroy American freedom. But it sort of didn't happen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: On the topic of welfare state, what are your thoughts on universal basic income?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: And that's sort of a, not a generic, but a universal safety net of this kind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: There's always a trade-off. When we talk about social safety net programs, there's always a

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: trade-off between universality, which is clean, but means that you're giving a lot of money to

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: people who don't necessarily need it, and some kind of targeting, which makes it easier to

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: get, to deal with the crucial problems with limited resources, but both has incentive problems and

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: kind of political, and I would say even psychological issues. So the great thing about

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: social security and Medicare is no questions asked. You don't have to prove that you need them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: It just comes. I'm on Medicare, allegedly. I mean, it's run through my New York Times health

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: insurance, but I didn't have to file an application with the Medicare office to prove that I needed it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: It just happened when I turned 65. That's good for dignity, and it's also good for

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: the political support because everybody gets Medicare. On the other hand, if you,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: and we can do that with healthcare, to give everybody a guarantee of an income that's

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: enough to live on comfortably, that's a lot of money. What about enough income to carry you over

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: through difficult periods, like if you lose a job or that kind of thing?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: Well, we have unemployment insurance, and I think our unemployment insurance is

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: too short-lived and too stingy. It would be better to have a more comprehensive unemployment

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: insurance benefit. But the trouble with something like universal basic income is that either the bar

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: is too low, so it's really not something you can live on, or it's an enormously expensive program.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: And so at this point, I think that we can do far better by building on the kinds of safety net

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: programs we have. Food stamps, earned income tax credit, we should have a lot more family support

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: policies. Those things can do a lot more to really diminish the amount of misery in this country.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: UBI is something that is being... It goes hand in hand with this belief that the robots are

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: going to take all of our jobs. And if that was really happening, then I might reconsider my

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: views on UBI, but I don't see that happening. So are you happy with discourse that's going

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: on now in terms of politics? So you mentioned a few political candidates. Is the kind of thing

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: going on both on Twitter and debates and the media through the written word, through the spoken word,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: how do you assess the public discourse now in terms of politics?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: We're in a fragmented world. More so than ever before. So at this point, the public discourse

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: that you see if Fox News is your principal news source is very different from the one you get

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: if you read the New York Times. On the whole, my sense is that mainstream political reporting,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: policy reporting is A, not too great, but B, better than it's ever been. Because when I first

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: got into the pundit business, it was just awful. Lots of things just never got covered. And if

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: things did get covered, it was always both sides. It's the line that comes back from me writing

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: during the 2000 campaign was that if one of the candidates said that the earth was flat,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: that the headline would be, views differ on shape of planet. And that's less true. There's still a

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: fair bit of that out there, but it's less true than there used to be. And there are more people

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: reporting, writing on policy issues who actually understand them than ever before.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: So though that's good, but still, how much the typical voter is actually informed is unclear.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: The democratic debates, I'm hoping that we finally get down to not having 27 people on the stage or

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: whatever it is they have, but they're reasonably substantive, certainly better than before. And

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: while there's a lot of still theater criticism instead of actual analysis and the reporting,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: it's not as totally dominant as in the past. Can I ask maybe a dumb question, but

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: from an open-minded perspective, when people on the left and people on the right, I think view the

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: others as sometimes complete idiots. What do we do with that? Is it possible that the people on the

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: right are correct about what they currently believe? Is that kind of open-mindedness helpful,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: or is this division long-term productive for us to have this food fight?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: Well, the trouble you have to confront is that there's a lot of stuff that just is false out

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: there, but commands extensive political allegiance. So the idea, well, both sides need to listen to

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: each other respectfully, I'm happy to do that when there's a view that is worthy of respect,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: but a lot of stuff is not. And so economics is something where I think I know something,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: and I'm not sure that I'm always right. In fact, I know I've been wrong plenty of times, but I

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: think that there is a difference between economic views that are within the realm of we can actually

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: have an interesting discussion and those that are just crank doctrines or things that are

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: purely being disseminated because people are being paid to disseminate them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: So there are plenty of good serious center-right economists that I have to say that I think

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: are center-right economists that I'm happy to talk to. None of those center-right economists

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: has any role in the Trump administration. The Trump administration and by and large,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: Republicans in Congress only want to listen to people who are cranks. And so I think it's

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: being dishonest with my readers to pretend otherwise. There's no way I can reach out to

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: people who think that reading Ayn Rand novels is how you learned about monetary economics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: CB Let me linger on that point. So if you look at Ayn Rand, okay, so you said center-right. What

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: about extreme people who have radical views? You think they're not grounded in any kind of data,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: any kind of reality. I'm just curious about how open we should be to ideas that seem radical.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: RW Oh, radical ideas is fine, but then you have to ask, is there some basis for the radicalism?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: And if it's something that is not grounded in anything, then, and particularly by the way,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: if it's something that's been refuted by evidence again and again, and the people just keep saying

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: it, if it's a zombie idea, and there's a lot of those out there, then there comes a point

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: when it's not worth trying to fake respect for it. CB I see. So through the scientific process,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: you've shown that this idea does not hold water, but I like the idea, zombie ideas,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: but they live on through... It's like the idea that the earth is flat, for example,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: has been, for the most part, disproven, but it lives on actually growing in popularity currently.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: RW Yeah. And there's a lot of that out there. And you can't wish it away, and you're not being fair

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: to either yourself or if you're somebody who writes for the public, you're not being fair

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: to your readers to pretend otherwise. CB So quantum mechanics is a strange theory,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: but it's testable. And so while being strange, it's widely accepted amongst physicists.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: How robust and testable are economics theories if we compare them to quantum mechanics and physics

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: and so on? RW Okay. Look, it's a complex system,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: and it's also one in which by and large you don't get to do experiments. And so economics is never

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: going to be like quantum mechanics. That said, you get natural experiments, you get tests of rival

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: doctrines. In the immediate aftermath of the financial crisis, there was one style, one basic

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: theory of macroeconomics, which ultimately goes back to John Maynard Keynes that made a few

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: predictions. It said, under these circumstances, printing money will not be as efficient as it

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: was. Running big budget deficits will not cause a rise in interest rates. Slashing government spending

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: austerity policies will lead to depressions if tried. Other people had exactly the opposite

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: predictions, and we got a fairly robust test. One theory won. Interest rates stayed low,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: inflation stayed low, countries that implemented harsh austerity policies suffered severe economic

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: downturns. You don't get much. That's pretty clear, and that's not going to be true on everything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: But there's a lot of empirical... I mean, the younger economists these days are very heavily

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: data-based, and that's great. I think that's the way to go. What theories of economics are,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: is there currently a lot of disagreement about, would you say?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: Oh, first of all, there's just a lot less disagreement, really, among serious researchers

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: in economics than people imagine. We can track that. The Chicago Booth School has a panel,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: an ideologically diverse panel, and they regularly pose questions. On most things,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: there's remarkable consensus. There are a lot of things where people imagine that there's

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: dispute, but the illusion of dispute is something that's basically being fed by political forces,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: and there isn't really. I think questions about what are effective ways to regulate

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: technology industries, we really don't know the answers there. Look, I don't follow every part.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: Minimum wages. I think there's pretty overwhelming evidence that a modest increase in the minimum

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: wage from current levels would not have any noticeable adverse effect on jobs. But if you

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: ask how high could it go, $12 seems pretty safe, given what we know. Is 15 okay? There's some

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: legitimate disagreement there, I think probably, but people have a point. Where is the line at

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: which it starts to become a problem? And the answer is, truly, we don't know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: It's fascinating to try to, such a cool, economics is cool in that sense, because you're trying to

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: predict something that hasn't been done before, the impact, the effects of something that hasn't

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: been done before. Yeah, you're going out of sample, and we have good reason to believe that

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: there are, that it's non-linear, that there comes a point at which it doesn't work the way it has

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: in the past. So as an economist, how do you see science and technological innovation? When I took

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: various economics courses in college, technological innovation seemed like a no-brainer way of growing

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: an economy, and we should invest in it aggressively. I may be biased, but it seemed like the various

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: ways to grow an economy seems like the easiest way, especially long-term. Is that correct?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: Yeah. And if so, why aren't we doing it more? Well, okay. The first question is, yeah, I mean,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: all, it's pretty much overwhelming. We think we can more or less measure this, although there are

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: some assumptions involved, but something like 70 to 80% of the growth in per capita income is

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: basically the advance of knowledge. It's not just the crude accumulation of capital. It is the fact

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: that we get smarter. A lot of that, by the way, is more prosaic kinds of technology. So I like to

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: talk about things like containerization or in an earlier period, the invention of the flat pack

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: cardboard box. That had to be invented, and now all of your deliveries from Amazon are made possible

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: by the existence of that technology. The web stuff is important too, but what would we do without

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: cardboard boxes? But all of that stuff is really important in driving economic progress. Well,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: why don't we invest more in, again, more prosaic stuff? Why haven't we built another goddamn real

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: tunnel under the Hudson River for which the need is so totally overwhelmingly obvious?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: How do you think about, first of all, I don't even know what the word prosaic means, but I inferred

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: it, but how do you think about prosaic? Is it the really most basic dumb technology innovation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: or is it just the lowest hanging fruit of what benefit can be gained?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: When I say prosaic, I mean stuff that is not sexy and fancy and high tech. It's building bridges and

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: tunnels, inventing the cardboard box. I don't know, where do we put

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: EasyPass in there? It is actually using some modern technology and all that, but

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: I don't think they're going to make a movie about the guy, whoever it was that invented

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: EasyPass, but it's actually a pretty significant productivity booster.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: To me, it always seemed like something that everybody should be able to agree on

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: and just invest. In the same way, the investment in the military and the DOD is huge.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: Right. So everyone kind of, not everyone, but there's an agreement amongst people that somehow

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: a large defense is important. It always seemed to me like that should be shifted towards,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: if you want to grow prosperity of the nation, you should be investing in knowledge. Yes,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: prosaic stuff, investing in infrastructure and so on. I mean, sorry to linger on it, but do you have

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: any intuition? Do you have a hope that that changes? Do you have intuition why it's not changing?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: I have more than intuition, I have a theory. I'm reasonably certain that I understand why

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: we don't do it. It's because we have a real values dispute about the welfare state, about how much

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: the government should do to help the unfortunate. Politicians believe,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: probably rightly, that there's a kind of halo effect that surrounds any kind of government

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: intervention. That even though providing people with enhanced social security benefits is really

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: very different from building a tunnel under the Hudson River, politicians of both parties seem to

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: believe that the government has seen to be successful at doing one kind of thing. It will

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: make people think more favorably on doing other kinds of things. Conservatives tend to be opposed

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: to any kind of increase in government spending, except military, no matter how obviously a good

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: idea it is, because they fear that it's the thin end of the wedge for bigger government in general.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: And to some extent, liberals tend to favor spending on these things, partly because they see it as a

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: way of proving that government can do things well, and therefore, it can turn to broader social

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: goals. It's clearly, there's a, if you like, what you might have thought would be a technocratic

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: discussion about government investment, both in research and in infrastructure, is contaminated

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: by the fact that government is government and people link it to other government actions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: Perhaps a silly question, but as a species, we're currently working on venturing out into space,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: one day colonizing Mars. So when we start a society on Mars from scratch,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: what political and economic system should it operate under?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: Oh, I'm a big believer in... First of all, I don't think we're actually going to do that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: but let's- Let's imagine. Hypothesize that we colonize Mars or something. Look, representative

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: democracy is... Versus pure democracy. Well, yeah, pure democracy where people vote directly on

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: everything is really problematic because people don't have time to try and master every issue.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: I mean, we can see what government by referendum looks like. There's a lot of that in California,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: and it doesn't work so good because it's hard to explain to people that the various things they

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: vote for may conflict. So representative democracy is... It's got lots of problems,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: and I think kind of the Winston Churchill thing, right? It's the worst system we know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: except for all the others. But so yeah, sticking with the representative... And basically,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: the American system of regulation and markets and the economy we have going on is a pretty good one

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: for Mars. If you start from scratch. If you're going to start from scratch, you wouldn't want

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: a Senate where 16% of the population has half the seats. You probably would want one which is

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: actually more representative than what we have. And the details, it's unclear. I mean,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: when times are good, all of the various representative democracy systems, whether it's

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: parliamentary democracies or a US style system, whether you have a prime minister or the head of

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: state as an elected president, they all kind of work well when times are good and they all have

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: different modes of breakdown. So I'm not sure I know what the answer is, but something like that

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: is given what we've seen through history, it's the least bad system out there. I mean, I don't know...

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: I'm a big fan of the TV series, The Expanse, and it's kind of gratifying that out there,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: that it's the Martian congressional republic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: Okay. In a brief sense, so amongst many things, you're also an expert at international trade.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: What do you make of the complexity? So I can understand trade between two people,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: say two neighboring farmers. It seems pretty straightforward to me, but international,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: when you start talking about nations and nations trading, it seems to be very complicated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: So from a high level, why is it so complicated? What are all the different factors that weigh

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: the objectives that need to be considered in international trade? And maybe feeding that

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: into a question of, do you have concerns about the two giants right now of the US and China

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: and the tension that's going on with the international trade there with the trade war?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: Well, first of all, international trade is not really that different from trade among individuals.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: It's vastly more complex and there are many more players, but in the end,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: the reasons why countries trade are pretty much the same as the reasons why individuals trade.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: Countries trade because they're different and they can derive mutual advantage from

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: concentrating on the things they do relatively well. Also, there are economies of scale.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: Individuals have to decide whether to be a surgeon or an accountant. It's probably not a good idea

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: to try and be both and countries benefit from specializing just because of the inherent

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: advantages of specialization. Now, the fact that it's a big world and we're talking about millions

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: of products being traded and in today's world, often trade involves many stages. So that made

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: in China iPhone is actually assembled from components that are made all over the world,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: but it doesn't really change the fundamentals all that much.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: There's a recurrent... I mean, the dirty little secret of international trade conflict is that

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: actually it's not conflicts among countries are really not that important. Most trade is beneficial

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: to both sides and to both countries, but it has big impacts on the distribution of income within

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: countries. So the growth of US trade with China has made both US and China richer, but it's been

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: pretty bad for people who were employed in the North Carolina furniture industry,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: who did find that their jobs were displaced by a wave of imports from China. And so that's where

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: the complexity comes in. Not at all clear to me. I mean, we have some real problems with China,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: although they don't really involve trade so much as things like respect for intellectual property.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: Not clear that those real problems that we do have with China have anything to do with the

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: current trade war. The current trade war seems to be driven instead by a fundamentally wrong

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: notion that when we sell goods to China, that's good. And when we buy goods from China, that's bad.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: And that's misunderstanding the whole point. Is trade with China in both directions a good thing?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: Yeah, we would be poorer if it wasn't for it. But there are downsides, as there are for any

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: economic change. It's like any new technology makes us richer, but often hurts some people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: Trade with China makes us richer, but hurts some people. And I wouldn't undo what has happened,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: but I wish we had had a better policy for supporting and compensating the losers from that growth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: So we live in a time of radicalization of political ideas, Twitter mobs, and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: And yet here you are in the midst of it, both tweeting and writing in the New York Times

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: articles with strong opinions, writing this chaotic wave of public discourse. Do you ever

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: hesitate or feel a tinge of fear for exploring your ideas publicly and unapologetically?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: Oh, I feel fear all the time. It's not too hard to imagine scenarios in which this is...

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: I might personally find myself kind of in the crosshairs. And I mean, I am the king of hate mail,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: I get that. Amazing correspondence. Does it affect you?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: It did when it started. These days I've developed a very thick skin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: So I know I don't usually get... In fact, if I don't get a wave of hate mail after a column,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: then I probably wasted that day.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: So what do you make of that as a person who's putting ideas out there? If you look at the

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: history of ideas, the way it works is you write about ideas, you put them out there. But now

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: when there's so much hate mail, so much division, what advice do you have for yourself and for

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: others trying to have a discussion about difficult ideas?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: Well, I don't know about advice for others. I mean, for most economists, just do your research.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: We can't all be public intellectuals and we shouldn't try to be. And in fact,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: I'm glad that I didn't get into this business until I was in my late 40s. I mean, it's probably best

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: to spend your decades of greatest intellectual flexibility addressing deep questions, not

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: confronting Twitter mobs. And as for the rest, I think when you're writing about stuff,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: the sort of dances like no one's watching, right? Like nobody's reading, right? Then what you think

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: is right, trying to make it obviously, trying to make it comprehensible and persuasive, but

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: don't let yourself get intimidated by the fact that some people are going to say nasty things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: You can't do your job if you are worried about criticism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: Well, I think I speak for a lot of people in saying that I hope that you keep dancing like

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: nobody's watching on Twitter and New York Times and books. So Paul, it's been an honor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: Thank you so much for talking to me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: Okay, great.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: or simply connect with me on Twitter at LEXFREEDMAN. And now let me leave you some

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: one of the most influential philosophers and economists in our history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paul Krugman: Economics of Innovation, Automation, Safety Nets & UBI | Lex Fridman Podcast #67

body.input: It is not from the benevolence of the butcher, the brewer, or the baker that we expect our dinner,

body.input: but to their self-love, and never talk to them of our necessities, but of their advantages.

body.input: The following is a conversation with Jeff Hawkins,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: a neuroscientist seeking to understand the structure, function,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: and origin of intelligence in the human brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: He previously wrote a seminal book on the subject titled On Intelligence,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: and recently a new book called A Thousand Brains,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: which presents a new theory of intelligence that Richard Dawkins, for example,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: has been raving about, calling the book, quote, brilliant and exhilarating.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: I can't read those two words and not think of him saying it in his British accent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: Quick mention of our sponsors, Codecademy, Biooptimizers, ExpressVPN,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: Asleep, and Blinkist.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: Check them out in the description to support this podcast.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: As a side note, let me say that one small but powerful idea that Jeff Hawkins mentions

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: in his new book is that if human civilization were to destroy itself,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: all of knowledge, all our creations, would go with us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: He proposes that we should think about how to save that knowledge in a way that long outlives us,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: whether that's on Earth, in orbit around Earth, or in deep space,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: and then to send messages that advertise this backup of human knowledge

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: to other intelligent alien civilizations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: The main message of this advertisement is not that we are here,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: but that we were once here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: This little difference somehow was deeply humbling to me,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: that we may, with some non-zero likelihood, destroy ourselves,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: and that an alien civilization, thousands or millions of years from now,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: may come across this knowledge store,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: and they would only with some low probability even notice it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: not to mention be able to interpret it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: And the deeper question here for me is what information in all of human knowledge

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: is even essential?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: Does Wikipedia capture it, or not at all?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: This thought experiment forces me to wonder what are the things we've accomplished

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: and are hoping to still accomplish that will outlive us?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: Is it things like complex buildings, bridges, cars, rockets?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: Is it ideas like science, physics, and mathematics?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: Is it music and art?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: Is it computers, computational systems, or even artificial intelligence systems?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: I personally can't imagine that aliens wouldn't already have all of these things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: In fact, much more and much better.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: To me, the only unique thing we may have is consciousness itself,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: and the actual subjective experience of suffering, of happiness, of hatred, of love.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: If we can record these experiences in the highest resolution directly from the human brain,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: such that aliens will be able to replay them,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: that is what we should store and send as a message.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: Not Wikipedia, but the extremes of conscious experiences,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: the most important of which, of course, is love.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: Do you think there's still neurons in your brain that remember that conversation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: that remember me and got excited?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: I do remember our conversation, or I have some memories of it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: and I formed additional memories of you in the meantime.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: I wouldn't say there's a neuron or neurons in my brain that know you,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: but there are synapses in my brain that have formed,

body.input: that reflect my knowledge of you and the model I have of you in the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeff Hawkins: The Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #208

body.input: As a side note, let me say that nature-inspired algorithms

metadata.title: Podcast: Risto Miikkulainen: Neuroevolution and Evolutionary Computation | Lex Fridman Podcast #177

body.input: to cellular automata to neural networks

body.input: have always captivated my imagination,

metadata.title: Podcast: Risto Miikkulainen: Neuroevolution and Evolutionary Computation | Lex Fridman Podcast #177

body.input: running toward biology, not running away from it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Risto Miikkulainen: Neuroevolution and Evolutionary Computation | Lex Fridman Podcast #177

body.input: is what leads to long-term progress.
